RECORDING I.S. NOTES
Ruled boxes for recording pertinent I.S. Notes
and other service information are provided
along the outer edge of each page in the manual. The filing instructions at the end of each I.S.

### Note specify the page an I.S. Note is to be re-

corded on. This provides a convenient reference to service updates and/or revisions affecting the information on the page.
SPECIAL TOOLS
Special tools needed for the service operations
described in this manual are listed at the beginning of each chapter. The tools are also listed in
the appropriate section of each chapter.

### WIRING DIAGRAMS

Wiring diagrams are printed separately and
should be filed in the pocket at the back of the
plastic binder. The diagrams provide the location of electrical components on the vehicle and
how they are connected and/or wired.

### SAFETY NOTES

Cautions and Warnings are used throughout
this manual. They relate to critical operations
involving personal safety or potential component damage. Cautions are used whenever
component damage could occur if service procedures are not followed. Warnings are used
when procedures must be followed explicitly for
personal safety. Use extreme care and adhere
to stated procedures when involved in such
operations.

Adhesives/Sealers/Cleaners

### Purpose

Loctite 242 (Medium strength)
Prevents loosening of bolts,
nuts, screws. Does not require
re-application every time
fasteners are loosened and
tightened.
Loctite 271 (High strength)
Locks bolts, nuts, screws.

### Must be reapplied if fastener

is loosened.
Loctite 290 or Wick n' Lock
(Medium strength, penetrating)
Prevents loosening of
fasteners, adjustment screws,
etc. Can be applied after
fastener is seated.
Loctite Superbonder
For quick bonding of nonporous materials (glass, metal,
rubber, vinyl and plastics).

### Permatex Gasket

Remover
For removal of gaskets and
cleaning gasket surfaces.
AMC/Jeep Gasket-ln-A-Tube
or Perfect Seal RTV Sealant
For use wherever RTV-Type
sealant is specified.

TOWING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Secure all loose or protruding parts of a damaged vehicle.

### Lift the end of a vehicle being towed a minimum

of 4-inches off the road surface. Be sure the
opposite end of the vehicle also has adequate
ground clearance.
Use safety chains at all times. The chains must
be independant of the tow truck lifting and towing attachments.

### Do not allow any portion of the lifting or towing

attachments to bear against the fuel tank of the
vehicle being towed.
Do not go under the vehicle after it has been
raised by the lifting and towing attachments.
Do not allow anyone to ride in a vehicle being
towed.

### Follow all State and local laws regarding tow

s p e e d s ,
warning
lights, and
nighttime
illumination.
Do not attempt a towing operation that could
jeopardize the operator, bystanders, or other
motorists.
Do not exceed a towing speed of 48 km/h (30
mph).

### Avoid towing distances of more than 24 km (15

miles) whenever possible.
Use towing dollies or a car hauler-type type
wrecker whenever the vehicle is locked and the
ignition key is not available. Use dollies or a
hauler-type wrecker whenever transmission,
transfer case or axle damage is suspected.

### Never attach tow chains or a tow sling to the

bumper, steering linkage, universal joints or
propeller shaft.
FRONT TOWING
CAUTION: Use tow chains with T-hooks for attachment to the frame rails. Do not use J-hooks
under any circumstances.
Attach the T-hooks (A) to the slots in the front
end of each frame rail.

### Position each chain over the top of each front

spring shackle (B).
Double wrap each chain.
Position the tow bar under the front bumper.
Attach the safety chains (C) to the lower half of
the front spring shackles.

FLOOR JACK-SAFETY STANDS-HOIST
Normal shop lifting equipment may be used to
raise and support Wrangler/YJ models during
service operations.

### Floor Jack-Safety Stands

Position floor jacks or safety stands under the
frame rails. Place the jack or safety stand lifting
pad on the frame rail just ahead of the rear
spring shackle, or just behind the front spring
shackle. Be sure the jack or stand is positioned
on a level section of the frame rail.

### Hoist

Wrangler/YJ models can be raised with the following type of hoist:
• Swiveling arm hoist.
• Ramp-type (drive-on) hoist.
• Wheel lift, twin post hoist.
NOTE: If a swiveling arm hoist is being used, be
sure the lifting pads are positioned at the same
frame rail locations recommended for floor
jack-safety stand usage.

### CAUTION: To avoid damaging the vehicle, do

not raise the vehicle with a floor jack positioned
under the axle tubes, body sheet metal, steering linkage components, propeller shafts, engine/transmission oil pans, or fuel tank. Use the
recommended lift points only.

### LUBRICANT CHANGE AND INSPECTION

INTERVALS
Recommended lubricant change and inspection
intervals for the engine, transmission, transfer
case and axles are as follows:
Engine Oil
Change engine oil at 12 000 km (7,500 mile)
intervals.
Check engine oil level at every fuel fill. Correct
level is between the Add and Full marks on the
engine dipstick.

### Refer to the Recommended Fuel-Liquids-Lubri-

cants section in this chapter for recommended
engine oil grade and viscosity.
Manual Transmission Lubricant
Change manual transmission lubricant at
48 000 km (30,000 mile intervals).
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7,500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.

### Use Jeep gear lubricant or an equivalent SAE

75W-90, API Grade GL-5 gear lubricant for top
off or refill purposes.
Automatic Transmission Fluid and Filter
Change the automatic transmission fluid and
filter at 48 000 km (30,000 mile) intervals.
Check fluid level every 12 000 km (7,500 miles).

### Correct fluid level is between the Add and Full

marks on the transmission dipstick.
Check the fluid level with the engine running
and the transmission in Park position. The fluid
must be at normal operating temperature to ensure an accurate reading.

### Use Jeep automatic transmission fluid or an

equivalent Dexron® II fluid only.
Transfer Case Lubricant
Change transfer case lubricant at 48 000 km
(30,000 mile) intervals.
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7,500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.

### Use Jeep automatic transmission fluid or an

equivalent Dexron® II fluid only.
Axle Lubricant
Change front and rear axle lubricant at 48 000
km (30,000 mile) intervals.
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7,500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.

### Use Jeep gear lubricant or an equivalent SAE

75W-90, API Grade GL-5 gear lubricant for top
off or refill purposes.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The one-piece windshield is constructed of two
sheets of laminated glass.
The windshield glass (A) is bonded to the windshield frame (E) with urethane adhesive (B) to
conform to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards and to provide structural support and to
provide glass retention.

### WINDSHIELD REMOVAL/INSTALLATION

PROCEDURES
Although the windshield removal procedure is
common, there are two installation procedures.
Short procedure
This procedure is recommended when the
windshield is removed intact and the body
windshield opening does not require repairs.

### After the glass has been removed, a controlled

amount of adhesive is applied to the pinchweld
flanges and used as a base for the replacement
glass.
Extended Procedure
This procedure is recommended when there is
considerable loss of adhesion between the
original adhesive material and the body windshield opening, or when the body windshield
opening requires repair.

### All adhesive material must be removed from the

pinchweld flanges.

### NOTE: The windshield removal procedure is

common to both installation procedures with
one exception. If the short procedure is to be
used, care must be taken during windshield removal to ensure that an even, uniform bead of
adhesive remains on the body for the replacement glass.

### Cover the area adjacent (interior and exterior)

to the body windshield opening with protective
covering to avoid paint damage and additional
cleanup.
CAUTION: Do not allow the electric knife blade
to remain stationary during the cutting operation. Excessive heat can cause permanent softening of the adhesive material.

### Insert a electric hot knife under the edge of

glass and cut the adhesive material as close
to the inside surface of the glass as possible.
85176
Installation
Short Procedure
When a replacement windshield is installed, a
replacement rear view mirror bracket must be
installed if the replacement windshield is not
equipped with one.

### Refer to the bracket installation procedure in

this chapter or to the instruction sheet included
with the windshield bracket kit.
Inspect the reveal molding retaining clips.
Clean the old sealant from the windshield opening with Kent Aery sol.
Clean the glass with glass cleaner.

### CAUTION: Do not use glass cleaner that con-

tains silicone.
P-6
DETACHABLE COMPONENTS
WINDSHIELD REPLACEMENT
Apply a smooth, continuous bead of adhesive
material around the entire perimeter of the
windshield opening flange.
Use the tape strips as guides and carefully position the glass in the body windshield opening.

### Press the glass to wet-out or set the adhesive

material.
Use care to avoid excessive squeeze-out of the
adhesive material.
Install the windshield reveal moldings and remove the masking tape from the inside surface
of the glass.
Install all the remaining components and clean
the vehicle.

### Refer to the replacement procedure and install

the inside rearview mirror bracket and mirror.
WARNING: The door windows must remain
open during the adhesive curing period.
Extended Procedure — Installation
Remove the windshield (refer to the removal
procedure).

### CAUTION: The interior garnish molding must be

replaced due to the urethane that remains on
the molding from the original installation.
Remove the original urethane from the body
opening around the perimeter of the opening (a
layer of urethane approximately 0.5 mm (0.02
in) to 1 mm (0.04 in) thick can be left on the
pinchweld flange).

### NOTE: If a sheet metal component is being

refinished, it should be prepared for painting as
described in Chapter T of this manual.
Install the lower support spacers (A) and the
standoff spacers (B).

Place the windshield glass in the body window
opening and support it on the spacers.

### When the windshield glass is properly position-

ed in the body opening, place strips of masking
tape on the glass at the lower support spacers
to provide the exact locating references for permanently installing the glass.
Cut the tape at the top edge, remove the glass
and place it either on a bench covered with a
protective covering or in a holding fixture.

Modify the adhesive cartridge nozzle (H) to look

### Use the tape strips as guides an carefully set

the windshield glass in the body opening.
Visually check to insure that full contact is made
between the glass and the urethane bead.
Press the glass to wet-out or set the urethane
but avoid excessive squeeze-out.

### Install the reveal molding and remove the mask-

ing tape from the inside surface of the glass.
Install a new interior garnish molding.
CAUTION: Install the garnish molding as soon
as possible because the urethane will begin to
cure soon after it is applied.

### Clean the vehicle with a cloth dampened with a

solvent such as acrysol.
When the installation is complete, allow the vehicle to set for 2-3 hours to allow the urethane
to initially cure. For the next twenty-four hours,
do not close the vehicle doors unless a window
is open slightly to release the pressure from
inside the vehicle.

Removal
The tailgate rubber seal (A) is made of molded
latex rubber foam and has a smooth skin on the
outside.

### Plastic retaining clips (B) retain the seal to the

tailgate. Barbs on the retaining clips (C) contract when inserted into the holes in the tailgate
and expand when they exit on the inside of the
tailgate.
101224
0

When servicing the seal, use a dampened cloth
to clean any dirt from the seal.

### Remove the screw from the end of the seal.

Carefully remove the seal from the retaining
clips.
NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the retaining clips to remove the seal.
Replace any clips that have been damaged or
distorted.
Installation
Remove the dust and dirt from the seal, tailgate
and body surface.

### Install the seal on the retaining clips and install

the screw that retains the end of the seal.
CAUTION: Do not use graphite, brake fluid or
wax on the seal.

HARD TOP ENCLOSURE REPAIR
General Information
The following material will be required to repair
the hardtop:
• fiberglass mat or cloth
• fiberglass resin and hardener
• structural adhesive (3M brand or equivalent)
• glazing putty
• aluminum foil
plastic spreader

### FIBERGLASS RESIN

%
RESIN
\\
1111/3 HARDENER
1
е««
I
101282
Hole Repair
Use a grinder to remove the paint and to outline
the damaged area.
Use a grade 24 disc for the initial grinding.
Follow up with a grade 50 disc to prevent
coarse scratches from showing up in the final
finish.

### NOTE: If there are any cracks extending from

the hole it will be necessary to stop-drill the
crack(s) using a 3.18-mm (1/8-in) drill bit.
Position a fiberglass mat or cloth on the repair
area, cut out the piece, allow a 2.54 cm (1 in)
extension beyond the damaged area.

### Clean the damaged area.

Place the fiberglass on a piece of aluminum foil.
P-18
DETACHABLE COMPONENTS
HARD TOP ENCLOSURE
Pour the fiberglass resin into a clean container.
Mix the appropriate amount of the hardener
with the resin, according to the manufacturer's
instructions.

### Apply the resin mixture to both sides of the

fiberglass cloth.
Lay the fiberglass and aluminum foil over the
repair area, on the outside. With the plastic
spreader, use firm pressure to remove the air
bubbles. Allow the resin to cure.
Remove the aluminum foil from the cured resin.

### Smooth the area to contour using a 50 grit disc.

Apply plastic filler to complete the repair, and
finish the area with 80 grit paper.
Repeat the previous step on the inside at the
top.
Featheredge the repaired area.
Prime the repaired area with Ditzler Epoxy

### Chromemate Primer (DP-40/401).

Apply primer surface.
Sand the area for paint preparation; reprime if
necessary.
Prepare the area for color coat.
Color coat (refer to Chapter T, Paint and Trim).
Fracture Repair
Use a grinder to remove the paint, from both
sides, and to outline the damaged area.

### Stop-drill the crack(s) using a 3.18-mm (1/8-in)

drill bit.
Bevel the edges of the crack(s) on both sides,
using a rotary file.
NOTE: The edges should be beveled on the
inside and outside of the enclosure to ensure
sufficient surface area for good bonding.

### Complete the process as above.

Textured Paint
To duplicate the texture on the enclosure, one
of the following paint kits will be necessary:
• paint repair kit (white) part no. 8997320
• paint repair kit (black) part no. 8997319
• paint repair kit (honey) part no. 8982 200 234

General Information
Exterior wind noise caused by loose or unseated moldings, trim, vibrating grille components, etc., can be hard to diagnose.

### The most common exterior wind noise is gener-

ally called a tea kettle whistle and it is usually
caused by air flowing under instead of around
or over a molding.
Road Test
There is no method available to simulate the air
flow that causes exterior wind noise, therefore
a road test is usually necessary.

### Take along a roll of tape to help isolate the

problem areas as they are located during the
road test.
It is usually helpful to have an assistant either
drive the vehicle or search for the source(s) of
the noise.
Road test the vehicle with the front windows
closed and then open to determine for sure that
the wind noise is originating from the outside of
the vehicle.

### Also, drive the vehicle in all directions because

the prevailing wind could influence the level of
the wind noise.
Try to determine from which area(s) of the vehicle the wind noise is originating:
• grille area
• hood bezel
• fender flares
• body side molding
• windshield reveal molding

### Apply masking tape to the suspected area(s)

and road test the vehicle.
If the wind noise still exists, apply additional
strips of tape to the suspected area(s) until the
wind noise is located.
If a large area has been covered with masking
tape, continue the road test and progressively
remove the strips of masking tape until the
source of the noise is isolated.

### Align and tighten the molding or fill the gap(s)

with sealant.

WATER LEAK DIAGNOSIS
SEE

### I.S.

N
O
' T '
E
S
The successful resolution of a water leak is dependent on three conditions:
•
accurate diagnosis based on careful visual
inspection and water testing
correct sealing methods and equipment
use of correct sealing material

### Visual Inspection

An accurate diagnosis is the important first step
in correcting water leaks.
The visual exterior inspection should cover the
vehicle exterior as well as the interior. It should
include removal of the seats, carpeting , floor
mats, and trim from suspected leak areas to
check for water tracking. Tracking will usually
indicate leak direction and help pinpoint the
source.

### The vehicle exterior should be carefully ex-

amined for:
• misaligned doors , windows, hardtop,
tailgate
• missing, loose or damaged weatherstripping
• missing or loose grommets in doors, floorpan or engine compartment dash panel
• gaps in the sealed seams or lack of sealer
• hollow spotwelds in gutters and welded
seams

### Water Test

The next diagnostic step is the water test which
should be performed by two technicians for
best results. In this situation, one man sprays
the vehicle exterior with water while the other
inspects the interior for leak sources.

### For the best results, use a garden hose with

water pressure of 27 to 42 psi (2-3 bars).
101188
The technician inside the vehicle should have a
flashlight and a mirror to search for the source
of the leak. The mirror can be used for reflecting light into dark corners and observing otherwise unaccessible places.

### R-10

SEALING
WATER LEAK DIAGNOSIS AND REPAIR
84224
84225
The method of spraying the vehicle is critical to
accurate diagnosis. Random spraying may miss
the leak source. The spray pattern must be
through and methodical.

### The best method is the spray zone method

which divides the vehicle into five separate
zones as shown below. Start at the lowest zone
and work upward through each of the zones.
DIAGNOSTIC TIPS
Water leaks are traced in a reverse direction
(e.g., from the wet area back to the source).

### Use the zone spray method. Start at the bottom

of the vehicle and work upward. This method
allows the elimination of each potential leak
area in stages.
Do not assume that a water leak has only one
source. A single water leak may have as many
as three sources.

### Seal each leak source as soon as it is located

and respray the same zone. This checks the
repair and will reveal any additional leaks in the
same zone.
Do not apply the water stream directly against
window seams or fresh air vents. This may create temporary and false leaks that can hinder
accurate diagnosis.

### WELDED COMPONENTS

BODY AND FRAME COMPONENTS
BODY CONSTRUCTION
General
Jeep vehicles are of all-steel construction, with
insulated body mounting points that provide a
secure attachment to the chassis frame.
All major body panels are of heavy-gauge steel,
reinforced, flanged and welded. The bodies are
completely detachable from the chassis unit
and are insulated from the frame by body
spacers placed between the body and frame
and held in position with body bolts.

### Spacers are located between the body and

chassis mounting points to insulate against vibrations and road noises.
Periodic inspection is necessary to determine
the condition of the body spacers and holddown bolts. Worn, loose or fatigued spacers
permit the body to settle, causing body lean or
possible interference between the floorpan and
various chassis components.

BODY REPAIR INFORMATION
BODY DAMAGE INSPECTION AND
MEASUREMENTS
An inspection and several measurements must
be completed before any body repairs are
initiated.
Visual Inspection
Walk slowly around the vehicle and visually inspect for damage.

### Inspect at every body location and note all dam-

age even if some of it appears to be minor.
Inspect for the following:
• alignment of the external sheet metal
• bends or buckles in the floor pan
• crushed or bent sillmember(s)
• alignment of the body structure
• alignment of the frame structure

### WELDED COMPONENTS

BODY REPAIR INFORMATION
FRAME CONSTRUCTION
The frame is the foundation and structural
center of the vehicle. In addition to carrying the
load, it mounts and supports the power unit
while maintaining the correct relationship and
alignment of the power train. This relationship
assures normal functioning of the units and
freedom from excessive wear, stress and
strain. The frame is constructed of heavy-channel steel side rails and crossmembers.

### The crossmembers maintain the proper posi-

tions of the side rails in direct relationship to
each other, providing maximum resistance to
torsional twist and strains.
FRAME ALIGNMENT DIAGNOSIS
There are three methods for checking frame
alignment:
# Self-Centering Gauges — for estimating and

repair

### S-10

WELDED COMPONENTS
BODY REPAIR INFORMATION
TRAMMEL GAUGE — DIAGNOSIS
The trammel gauge is primarily used for diagnosis, but can be used for longitudinal and diagonal measurements during a straightening operation. Using the trammel gauge, cross
measurment will indicate the amount of bow or
side sway. Measuring the length indicate any
smash or sag.

### CHECKING BY COMPARING PARALLEL

LENGTHS AND DIAGONAL LENGTHS
This is a comparative check between body or
frame sections that are parallel or diagonal. The
diagonals must be checked and compared as
well as the parallels to ensure alignment
accuracy.

### HOW TO USE THE TRAMMEL GAUGE

Place the vehicle on a two post hoist.
Insert the straight pointer with the stepped tip
into one of the floor frame jigging holes.
NOTE: For the particle check in progress, select
the most suitable shape of pointer for the other
end of the gauge.

### Keep the trammel gauge as parallel to the vehi-

cle frame as possible and use the shortest
pointers possible for each check.

BODY REPAIR INFORMATION
SELF-CENTERING ALIGNMENT GAUGES
Alignment gauges show misalignment by projecting alignment points of the frame into a lineof-sight that can be read by the technican. A
through understanding of the information
shown by the gauges will enable the technican
to diagnos damage and misalignment quickly
and accurately.

### Gauges have two sliding horizontal bars which

remain parallel as they move inward and outward. This inward or outward action permits
adjustment to any width for installation on various areas of the vehicle. Once the gauges are
hung in place, the horizontal bars will be parallel
to that portion of the frame that they are attached. This permits the technican to "read"
that area relative to an adjacent area.

### Gauges are equipped with center pins that are

designed to remain in the center of the gauge
regardless of the width of the horizontal bar.
This allows for a true centerline throughout the
length of the vehicle.
Each gauge accommodates two vertical scales.

### These scales can be adjusted vertically to as-

sure that the horizontal bars accurately reflect
the true position of the parts to which they are
attached. This allows all structional misalignments to be read - centerline, level and datum.
CENTER LINE AND DATUM LINE

### Before laying out a mechanical drawing, it is

necessary for the drafter to establish a reference line from which to start. This is accomplished by establishing a centerline or a datum
line. In fact the centerline or datum line will exist
only on paper.

### Consequently, when installing gauges, it is sim-

ply a matter of using the reference points and
measurements to establish proper gauge
heights or location.
FRAME ALIGNMENT
Before any attempt is made to read the frame
alignment gauges, it is important that the
technician fully understand the definition of
correct alignment.

### Structural alignment gauges should be installed

in such a way that the line of sight reading can
easily be read by the technican.
If the gauges are installed properly on a straight
frame, all gauges will be parallel, on the same
plane and the center pins will align.

### Also rember that correct frame alignment must

include correct length and width measurements
through the entire frame.

A bent or twisted frame may be straightened
using a frame straightening machine, provided
the extent of the misalignment is not excessive.
Use of self-centering and trammel gauges or jig
bench is necessary to maintain accuracy.

### Repair Procedures

The repair procedures contained in this chapter
describe how to repair and replace welded body
components.
They are intended only to provide general
guidelines and may be altered if it will assist the
technician to expedite the repairs.

### There are certain components in each vehicle,

however, that must not be cut or completely
replaced without using special precautions to
preserve the safety characteristics (integrity) of
the vehicle.
It is NOT advisable to:
• heat a sillmember to straighten it
m cut (section) a side member or pillar and their
inner panels along the same line (i.e., offset
cutting will improve the strength of the
repair)

### S-! •27

WELDED COMPONENTS
BODY REPAIR INFORMATION
• submit a vehicle that is positioned on a repair
jig bench to hydraulic traction (pull or push)
without correctly anchoring the vehicle
CAUTION: The only recommended methods of
welding these members are MIG and spot
welding.

### WELDING PROCEDURES

WARNING: Ensure that safety goggles are
worn during ALL welding operations.
Electric Spot Welding
Spot welding is a function of pressure, current
(amps) and time.
Pressure Adjustment
The pressure adjustment (H) is controlled by
distance (E).
87433

### The distance (E) is determined by the thickness

(minimum) of the metal being welded.
Use a feeler gauge to adjust the distance (E).
After adjusting the distance, test the pressure
adjustment (H) with sample sections of sheet
metal that has the same thickness as the body
members that are to be welded.

### Current and Time Adjustments

NOTE: To test the adjustments, use sample
sections of sheet metal that is the same thickness as the body components to be welded.
Initially place the power/current (amps) adjustment control (1) at position 1 and gradually increase the current until excessive arcing occurs, then decrease the current one position.

### Increase the time adjustment control (2) until

the correct spotweld diameter is obtained.
Refer to the chart.

Welding
Standard, coated and lightweight high strength

the sillmembers.

### CAUTION: Do NOT arc weld high strength steel

MIG plug or seam (continuous) welding is recommended for replacement of high strength

Repairing
High strength steel (HSS) is adversely affected
by heat.

### The application of heat must be strictly con-

trolled during a straightening operation.
Use the following time guides when heating
high strength steel (HSS):
# 361° to 427°C (700° to 800°F) — maximum
of two hours

### CAUTION: Once the maximum temperature and

time limits have been reached, the application
of any additional heat will cause disruption of
the molecular structure and reduce the strength
of the steel.
To assist in monitoring the temperature of a
repair area, use a temperature indicating
crayon.
84559

### REPLACEMENT PROCEDURES

Spotweld Removal
Removing spotwelds from the welded members
of a vehicle body is a intricate operation.
Chisel or Snips
Using a chisel or snips to remove spotwelds
causes distortion and tears the mating surfaces
of the panels.

### The damaged mating surfaces must be welded,

straightened and smoothed before the replacement member is placed in position.

Color matching can be accomplished by the use
of several different techniques.
The techniques are as follows:
• gun technique, including reduction (thinner)
and air pressure
• tinting
• blending

### Gun Technique

A color can be changed to be either lighter or
darker by using one of the following methods.
Lighten (drier):
• thinner/reducer (more reduction)
• higher air pressure
• greater gun distance
• Darker (wetter):
• thinner/reducer (less reduction)
• lower air pressure
• less gun distance

### Tinting Technique

The tinting technique usually requires more experience than the gun technique.
Tinting is based on the primary color concept
that is described in the following illustrations.

A color can be broken down into three areas;
coloration, brightness or tone and purity:
• coloration — determined by pigments (refer
to the color chart)
• brightness or tone — generally can be adjusted by changing the aluminum content in
metallic colors

### NOTE: When adjustments are made, refer to

the paint formula information for the aluminum
type and size.
• purity — black or white variation
Blending Technique
Blending is a common technique for color
matching.
This technique is generally used if the proper
color cannot be obtained by using the other
techniques described above.

### Blending is used to eliminate the variation in

color when there are two very similar colors
located on adjacent body panels.

Procedure
Complete repair to the damaged area and

Sand the the adjacent panels with 600 grit wet

Blend the paint into the adjacent body panels

previous coat.

PRECAUTIONS

### Air Compressor

Undesirable impurities (e.g., small quantities of
water and oil) can be avoided if the air tank is
purged at the end of each day.
86363
Distributor Air Filters
The distributor air filters must be purged two
times per day to eliminate impurities that cause
paint blistering and lack of luster.
86364

### Ingredients and Quantities

The ingredient and quantity instructions provided by the paint vendor must be closely observed to prevent paint runs, orange peel and
pitting.

Paint Filtering
Filter the paint after thinning it to remove impurities (i.e., dust).
The spray gun must have a filter.
86365
Equipment Cleaning
The spray gun and associated equipment must
always be clean to avoid spraying contaminated
paint, imperfect coloring and other undesirable
results.
86362

### Air Pressure

The air pressure should be adjusted to compensate for:
• hose length
• hose diameter
$ air leaks

Environment
Clean spray booth filters will assure the proper
downward airflow (0.3 m/s or 1 ft/s) and the
elimination of dust.

### For good paint application and coat tension, the

spray booth temperature must be maintained at
a close vicinity of 20°C (68°F).
86359
Vehicle Grounding
The vehicle must be grounded (i.e., at the same
voltage potential as the spray booth) to assure
a safe working condition and to minimize the
attraction of dust particles.

dry sandpaper and prepare the surface for top
coating.

REFINISHING MOLDINGS AND WHEELS
WARNING: Ensure that there is adequate ventilation and avoid breathing the vapor or spray
mist. The use of a fresh-air supplied respirator
is recommended. Wear the respirator for the
entire time of spraying and until all vapor and
mist have dissipated.

### Exterior Reveal Moldings (Anodized Or Non-

Anodized Aluminum)
Remove the existing paint (to bare metal) from
the moldings with chemical stripper.
Apply Alumiprep 33 (Ditzler DX-533) to the
moldings according to the manufacture's
instructions.
Apply Alodine 1201 (Ditzler DX-503) to the
moldings according to the manufacture's
instructions.

### Apply Ditzler DP 40/401 Epoxy Chromate Pri-

mer to the moldings.
Apply a semi-gloss black top coat on the
moldings.
Slightly scuff moldings with a scratch pad or
400 grit wet or dry sand paper to enhance
adhesion.
Apply wax and grease remover (e.g.,Ditzler DX330 or Sikkens M-600) to clean the moldings.

### Apply an acid etching wash primer (e.g., Sik-

kens Wash Primer).
NOTE: Acid etching wash primers provide superior adhesion and also eliminates the metal
prep step.
Apply a semi-gloss black top coat on the
molding.
Aluminum Wheels
Remove the coating from the wheel with a
chemical stripper.

### Apply Alumiprep 33 (Ditzler DX-533) to the

wheel.
Apply Alodine 1001 (Ditzler DX-501) to the
wheel.
NOTE: Apply Alodine 1001 to a wheel that will
be color coated as well as one that wilt be
clearcoated only.
Apply Ditzler DP-40/401 Epoxy Chromate Primer to the surface areas that will be color
coated.

### Apply the color coat, if applicable, to the wheel.

Apply Ditzler DAU75 Urethane Clearcoat to the
wheel.
NOTE: Coat the entire wheel, including the outer edge.

Plastic Identification
International identification code letters are
molded on the back side of major plastic components to identify the type of plastic.
The following information explains the code
letters:
• ABS — Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (flexible or hard) is used for grilles, headlamp
doors and instrument panels
• ABS/PVC — Vinyl is used for crash pads
• EPDM — Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer is used for bumper impact strips
• PA — Polyamide (Nylon) is used for exterior
finish trim panels
• PC — Polycarbonate (Lexan) is used for grilles, instrument panel components and
lenses
• PPO — Polyhenylene Oxide (Noryl) is used
for chrome grilles, headlamp doors, bezels
and ornaments
• PE — Polyethylene is used for fender inner
panels, interior trim panels, valances and
spoilers
• PP — Polypropylene is used for interior kick
panels, hard plastic trim, fender aprons, radiator shrouds and certain heater/evaporator
housings
# PUR — Polyurethane (Thermoset) is used for
bumper covers
# TPUR — Polyurethane (Thermoplastic) is
used for soft filler panels, bumper covers,
gravel deflectors and soft bezels
• PVC — Polyvinyl Chloride (Vinylite) is used
for upholstery and interior trim
* SAN — Styrene Acrylonitrile is used for instrument panel gauge lenses
• TPR — Thermoplastic Rubber is used for
valance panels and filler panels
• UP — Polyester Unsaturated is used for fiberglass panels, grille openings and body
fillers

### Plastic Classification

Plastics are divided into two major groups according to the chemical nature of their molecular chains:
# thermoplastics (reversible processing)

### REFINISHING PLASTIC EXTERIOR COMPONENTS (SMC)

WARNING: Ensure that there is adequate ventilation and avoid breathing the vapor or spray
mist. The use of a fresh-air supplied respirator
is recommended. Wear the respirator for the
entire time of spraying and until all vapor and
mist have dissipated.

### Replacement Hard Top Panel (SMC)

Wash the replacement panel with denatured
alcohol.
Scuff sand the panel surface area with a double-action sander and 240 grit sandpaper or use
320 wet or dry sandpaper.
Clean the panel surface area with a wax and
grease removal solution (Ditzler DX-330, Sikkens M-600 or an equivalent product).

### Tack and prime the panel surface area with Dit-

zler DP 40/401 Epoxy Chromate Primer according to the manufacture's instructions.
Apply a primer surfacer and prepare the panel
surface area for paint (i.e., sand, clean and
tack).
Apply the top coat to the panel surface area.

### NOTE: If the top has been repaired and the

texture has been removed, an additive such as
Ditzler DX-1507 can be added to the paint and
sprayed on the repaired area to produce the
textured appearance.

REFINISHING PLASTIC COMPONENTS

### Fender Flares

Clean the surface area with a wax and grease
removal solution (Ditzler DX-330, Sikkens M600 or an equivalent product).
Scuff sand the surface area with 400 wet or 320
dry sandpaper.
Apply a propylene primer (AMC P/N 899 3756
or Ditzler DX-800) to the surface area.

### NOTE: Prime the entire surface area of replace-

ment flares.
Apply the top coat of acrylic enamel mixed with
a flex agent according to the manufacture's
instructions.
NOTE: The flex agent is a modifier that gives
the enamel elastomeric properties.
REFINISHING PLASTIC INTERIOR TRIM

### Refinishable plastic interior trim components

are divided into three general types:
• acrylonitrile butadiene styrene plastic (ABS)
m vinyl (ABS/PVC)
It is important that the type of plastic be correctly identified so that the corresponding component can be refinished satisfactorily.

### If the plastic component does not have molded

identification code letters, the following tests
enable the type of plastic to be identified so that
the proper refinishing procedures and materials
can be used.
Test For Polypropylene (PP) And Acrylonitrile

### Butadiene Styrene (ABS) Plastic

To determine if a component is PP or ABS
plastic, use the following burn test:
• remove a sliver of the plastic from the backside or unseen surface of the component to
be tested with a sharp knife
• hold the sliver of plastic with needlenose pliers and ignite the plastic
m observe the burning plastic closely

### When burning, PP plastic has a clear blue flame

that has a yellow tip and no readily visible
smoke (A).
# polypropylene plastic (PP)

When extinguished, polypropylene plastic will
emit white smoke that has a paraffin wax odor.

### When burning, ABS plastic has an orange flame

and highly visible black, sooty smoke (B) that
hangs temporarily in the air.

Test For Vinyl (ABS/PVC)
To determine if a component that is to be refinished is vinyl or not, use the following copper
wire test:
# heat a copper wire (C) with a propane torch
until the wire glows (a red color)
# touch the heated copper wire to the backside
or unseen surface of the component to be
tested in a manner so as to retain some of
the liquid plastic on the wire

PAINT AND TRIM
ft
REFINISHING PLASTIC COMPONENTS
ft
Refinishing ABS Plastic Components
ABS plastics does not require a primer.

### AMC/JEEP/RENAULT Interior Spray Paint or

spray paint from a local supplier will adhere
satisfactorily to ABS plastic.
Scuff sand the surface of the component that is
to be painted.
Clean the surface of the component with a wax
and grease removal solution (e.g., Ditzler DX330, DuPont Prep-Sol or an equivalent
product).

### Color coat the surface of the component with a

semior low-gloss lacquer.
NOTE: Apply only enough paint to provide
proper concealment of the natural color to
avoid wash-out of the grain effect, if applicable.
Refinishing PP Plastic Components
CAUTION: It is essential that the component be
primed first with a coat of AMC/JEEP/RE-

### NAULT Aerosol Polypropylene Primer (or an

equivalent product) according to the instructions printed on the container. Failure to use the
required primer as instructed will result in the
color coat lifting or peeling.
Painting polypropylene plastic components involves the use of a special primer.

### Because polypropylene (PP) plastic is rigid, it

can be color coated after priming with the appropriate interior spray paint color (plastic and
vinyl) or lacquer.
Clean the component with either DuPont PrepSol, Ditzler Acryli-Clean or an equivalent
product.

### Apply either a thin coat of polypropylene primer

according to the instructions printed on the
container or Ditzler DPX-800 polypropylene primer
according to
the
manufacture's
instructions.
NOTE: Ensure that the primer application covers all the edges to assure proper color coat
adhesion.

### Allow the primer to dry completely.

Apply an appropriate color coat of interior spray
paint and allow to air dry before installing the
component.
Refinishing Vinyl Components
Clean the component surface area with Ditzler
UK-403 Vinyl Cleaner (or an equivalent
product).

### Apply Ditzler UK-405 Vinyl Conditioner (or an

equivalent product) to the component surface
area.
Apply Ditzler UCV-Vinyl Color (or an equivalent
product) to the component surface area according to the manufacture's instructions.
NOTE: Instrument panels must be sprayed with

### Ditzler UCV-69 Low-Gloss Clear Coat to reduce

gloss.

### PAINT AND TRIM

ft
ft
CORROSION PROTECTION
ft
GENERAL INFORMATION
Jeep vehicles undergo several anti-corrosion
processes during manufacture.
The anti-corrosion processes are:
• phosphate rinse
• E-dip (cathathonic primer)
• intermediate primer
• base coat
• clear coat

### In addition, many exterior panels are either sin-

gle or double-sided galvanized and aluminum
wax is applied to most of the vehicle interior.
Sealants are also applied to several critical areas of the vehicle during manufacture, therefore, after vehicle body repair, the sealants
must be replaced.

### After repair, when applicable, a sealant must

also be applied to the joints and seams for corrosion protection.
Corrosion protective material can be injected
inside hollow sections of the vehicle via strategically located 8-mm (0.31-in) diameter holes
that are punched during manufacture.

### The holes are plugged with plastic plugs.

NOTE: If necessary, additional holes can be
drilled for the purpose of injecting corrosion
protective material.
Equipment
An air-operated spray gun and several types of
nozzles are required for application of the corrosion protective material.

### A vertical nozzle should be used for boxed-in

sections (e.g., door interiors, crossmembers,
sillmembers and rocker panels).
100737
An angled nozzle should be used for hoods,
liftgates and the engine compartment.
T-28
ft

ft

ft
' (
v..
100738
100740

### A flexible nylon nozzle should be used for inner

fender panels and quarter panels.
100739
NOTE: Aerosol spray cans of Rust Fighter-I (3M
08892, US and Canada) can be used if spray
equipment is not available.
PROTECTIVE MATERIAL APPLICATION
Vehicle Interior

### Anti-corrosion wax should be applied to the in-

terior side of repaired or replaced panels.
NOTE: Ensure that a generous amount of wax
is applied to all welded areas.
Vehicle Underbody
After an underbody component has been repaired or replaced, corrosion protective material must be applied.

EXTERIOR DECALS
ft
GENERAL INFORMATION
The exterior decals and stripes are durable,
weather-resistant vinyl and have a pressuresensitive adhesive backing.

### The pressure-sensitive adhesive backing is

protected by a paper cover that is removed during installation.
The outward side (or face) of the stripes and
decals is covered with an easy-release paper
for protection during shipment and storage.

### This paper should be removed after installation.

REPAIR
Small nicks or scratches can be touched-up
with paint in the same manner as painted
surfaces.
The proper color match can be obtained by
mixing small amounts of appropriate paint colors and then applied to the damaged area of the
decal or stripe.

### To remove air bubbles, pierce them with a

sharp needle or pin.
Force the trapped air out through the hole and
press the decal or stripe firmly against the body
panel.
It may be necessary to preheat the body panel
slightly with heat gun to soften the adhesive.

### Heat may also be used to remove small wrin-

kles and other irregularities.
REPLACEMENT
Preparation
The temperature of the service area should be
between 18°C and 32°C (65°F and 90°F).
Decals or stripes should not be replaced if the
temperature is below 18°C (65°F).

### The following equipment and materials are nec-

essary for a professional installation:
• woodgrain and stripe removal solution — 3M
or an equivalent product
• adhesive removal solution — 3M or an
equivalent product
• liquid detergent — Joy, Vel or an equivalent
product
• wax and silicone removal solution — 3M

### General Purpose Adhesive Cleaner, Xylol, or

an equivalent product
• isopropyl (rubbing) alcohol
• squeegee — 10 to 13 cm (4 to 5 in) wide,
plastic or hard rubber
• Heat gun or an infrared heat lamp with an
extension cord
• clean wiping cloths or paper towels
• sharp knife, single-edged razor blade, or an


# scissors

Removal
Clean any repair surfaces, adjacent panels and
openings as required.

### Remove parts overlapping the decal on affected

panel.
Mask off the area surrounding decal.
Scuff sand the complete decal with 360 grit
wet-or-dry sandpaper. Avoid cutting through
the vinyl and reclean the surfaces.
WARNING: Use 3M Woodgrain and Stripe Remover, or equivalent, in a well-ventilated area
only. Observe manufacture's warnings printed
on the label.

### CAUTION: Woodgrain and Stripe Remover from

3M is designed for use on acrylic enamel surfaces only.
Spray 3M Woodgrain and Stripe Remover, or
equivalent, on flange area first. Spray entire decal to be removed.
86915
Allow the remover to remain on the decal for
approximately 15 minutes.

### After the allotted time, peel the decal away from

the flange areas. Then, start in one corner and
peel the decal away from the panel. If there is
any difficulty in peeling the decal/overlay away
from the panel, use a squeegee to assist in
removing.
Scrape all of the 3M Woodgrain and Stripe Remover from the surface before proceeding.

### T-32

After the decal is removed, spray the panel using 3M Adhesive Remover, or equivalent, to remove any remaining adhesive.
NOTE: Allow the remover to work on the adhesive surface for three to five minutes.

### After five minutes, use a squeegee to remove

adhesive residue.
86917
NOTE: If some adhesive is difficult to remove,
spray additional remover on troublesome
spots. Wait approximately two minutes and
squeegee remaining spots. Repeat as
necessary.
Remove the masking tape and paper.

### Wash the entire panel with 3M General Purpose

Adhesive Cleaner, or equivalent. If any spots of
adhesive remain on the panel, hard rubbing
during washdown will remove them.
Installation
Clean the painted surface with 3M General Purpose Adhesive Cleaner, or equivalent. Wipe the
surface with a clean cloth and allow to dry.

### NOTE: Freshly painted surfaces must be thor-

oughly dry prior to installing decals. Residual
solvents in fresh paint may cause the decal to
blister.
Position the decal on the panel surface and
mark its position with a grease pencil. Be sure
that a 12.7 mm (1/2-in) excess is allowed to be
wrapped around the door and fender areas, if
necessary.

Where possible, extend the decal 12.7 mm (1/2

### Remove the easy-release paper from the face

of the decal (if applicable).
Inspect the decal installation using reflected

Install any previously removed parts and clean
the vehicle as required.

### Installation of Intricate Decals

For large, intricately shaped decals, the following procedure will simplify installation.
The use of wetting solution aids in the installation of intricate decals. Prepare a supply of wetting solution by thoroughly mixing two or three
teaspoons of detergent (Joy, Vel, or equivalent)
in 3.78 liters (1 gallon) of water.

### NOTE: DO NOT USE SOAP. Too much deter-

gent will reduce the effectiveness of the bond.
Place the decal on a clean, flat surface with the
paper backing side up. Bend the corner of decal
toward the decorative face side, and with flick
of a finger, separate the paper backing from the
decal. Hold the decal firmly to the surface of
table and remove the paper backing. In hot,
humid conditions, a slight jerking motion will aid
in removing the paper backing.

### CAUTION: Always remove the paper backing

from the decal, never the decal from the backing as stretching may result.
NOTE: Hold the decal in the corners when removing the paper backing as fingerprints will
adversely affect the adhesion.
Using a clean sponge, apply ample wetting solution to the decal adhesive and the panel surface. The wetting solution permits ease of
movement of the decal while positioning it on
the panel surface.

### Immediately apply the wetted decal to the panel

surface. Apply the wetting solution to the decorative face of the decal to allow the squeegee to
slip during application.
Squeegee a short section of the decal at the
center. Lift the right or left side of the decal,
position it straight and close to the panel, and
squeegee toward the lifted edge. Avoid stretching the decal at the lifted end. Squeegee outward from center with firm, overlapping
strokes.
$ Lift the upper area of the decal (up to bonded
area) and, working upward from the bonded
section at the center, squeegee the decal into place.

### TOWING SAFETY PRECAUTIONS

Secure all loose or protruding parts of a damaged vehicle
Lift the end of a vehicle being towed a minimum
of 4-inches off the road surface. Be sure the
opposite end of the vehicle also has adequate
ground clearance.

### Use safety chains at all times. The chains must

be independant of the tow truck lifting and towing attachments.
Do not allow any portion of the lifting or towing
attachments to bear against the fuel tank of the
vehicle being towed.
Do not go under the vehicle after it has been
raised by the lifting and towing attachments.

### Do not allow anyone to ride in a vehicle being

towed.
Follow all State and local laws regarding tow
speeds, warning lights, and
nighttime
illumination.
Do not attempt a towing operation that could
jeopardize the operator, bystanders, or other
motorists.

### Do not exceed a towing speed of 48 km/h (30

mph).
Avoid towing distances of more than 24 km (15
miles) whenever possible.
Use towing dollies or a car hauler-type type
wrecker whenever the vehicle is locked and the
ignition key is not available. Use dollies or a
hauler-type wrecker whenever transmission,
transfer case or axle damage is suspected.

### Never attach tow chains or a tow sling to the

bumper, steering linkage, universal joints or
propeller shaft.
FRONT TOWING
CAUTION: Use tow chains with T-hooks for attachment to the frame rails. Do not use J-hooks
under any circumstances.
Attach the T-hooks (A) to the slots in the from
end of each frame rail.

### Position each chain over the top of each front

spring shackle (B).
Double wrap each chain.
Position the tow bar under the front bumper.
Attach the safety chains (C) to the lower half of
the front spring shackles.

REAR TOWING
Use wheel lift equipment only when rear towing
is necessary. This is the only recommended
method of rear towing Wrangler/YJ models.
101268

### Shift the transmission and transfer case into

Neutral.
Raise and tow the vehicle at a maximum speed
of 48 km/h (30 mph). Keep towing distance
under 24 km (15 miles) whenever possible.
A10
FLOOR JACK-SAFETY STANDS-HOSST
Hoist
Normal shop lifting equipment may be used to
raise and support Wrangler/YJ models during
service operations.

### Wrangler/YJ models can be raised with the fol-

lowing type of hoist:
• Swiveling arm hoist.
• Ramp-type (drive-on) hoist.
• Wheel lift, twin post hoist.
NOTE: If a swiveling arm hoist is being used, be
sure the lifting pads are positioned at the same
frame rail locations recommended for floor
jack-safety stand usage.

LUBRICANT CHANGE AND INSPECTION
INTERVALS
Recommended lubricant change and inspection
J | E
intervals for the engine, transmission, transfer

### " N"

case and axles are as follows:
O
T
E
S
Engine Oil
Change engine oil at 12 000 km (7,500 mile)
intervals.
Check engine oil level at every fuel fill. Correct
level is between the Add and Full marks on the
engine dipstick.

### Refer to the Recommended Fuel-Liquids-Lubri-

cants section in this chapter for recommended
engine oil grade and viscosity.
Manual Transmission Lubricant
Change manual transmission lubricant at
48 000 km (30,000 mile intervals).
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7f500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.

### Use Jeep gear lubricant or an equivalent SAE

75W-90, API Grade GL-5 gear lubricant for top
off or refill purposes.
Automatic Transmission Fluid and Filter
Check fluid level every 12 000 km (7,500 miles).
Correct fluid level is between the Add and Full
marks on the transmission dipstick.

### Check the fluid level with the engine running

and the transmission in Park position. The fluid
must be at normal operating temperature to ensure an accurate reading.
Use Jeep automatic transmission fluid or an
equivalent Dexron® II fluid only.
Transfer Case Lubricant

### Change transfer case lubricant at 48 000 km

(30,000 mile) intervals.
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7,500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.
Use Jeep automatic transmission fluid or an
equivalent Dexron® II fluid only.

### Axle Lubricant

Change front and rear axle lubricant at 48 000
km (30,000 mile) intervals.
Check lubricant level every 12 000 km (7,500
miles). Correct lubricant level is to the bottom
edge of the fill plug hole.
Use Jeep gear lubricant or an equivalent SAE
75W-90, API Grade GL-5 gear lubricant for top
off or refill purposes.

### Change the automatic transmission fluid and

filter at 48 000 km (30,000 mile) intervals.

GENERAL INFORMATION
GENERAL INFORMATION
The 2.46 liter (150 CID) four-cylinder engine and
S
E
(
the 4.2 liter (258 CID) six-cylinder engine are
L
S
in-line, lightweight, overhead valve engines.
N
o
T

### Both engines are designed for unleaded fuel.

E
s
The cylinder heads have dual quench-type
combustion chambers that create turbulence
and fast burning of the air/fuel mixture, which
results in good fuel economy.
"
The cylinders in the four-cylinder engine are
numbered 1 through 4 from front to rear. The
firing order is 1 -3-4-2.

### The crankshaft rotation is clockwise, when

viewed from the front of the engine. The
crankshaft rotates within five main bearings and
the camshaft rotates within four line-bored
bearings.
The cylinders in the six-cylinder engine are
numbered 1 through 6 from front to rear. The
firing order is 1 -5-3-6-2-4.

### The crankshaft rotation is clockwise, when

viewed from the front of the engine. The
crankshaft rotates within seven main bearings
and the camshaft rotates within four line-bored
bearings.

GENERAL SERWICE AID DIAGNOSIS
DIAGNOSIS PROCEDURES
General Information
Engine diagnosis is helpful in determining the
causes of malfunctions not detected and
remedied by routine tune-ups.

### These malfunctions may be classified as either

mechanical (e.g., a strange noise), or performance (e.g., engine idles rough and stalls).
Refer to the Service Diagnosis - Mechanical
chart and the Service Diagnosis - Performance
chart for possible causes and corrections of
malfunctions. On four-cylinder models, refer to

### INJ. R.. (G) service manual for fuel injection

diagnosis.
Additional tests and diagnostic procedures may
be necessary for specific engine malfunctions
that can not be isolated with the Service
Diagnosis charts.
Information concerning additional tests and
diagnosis is provided within the Diagnosis With

### A Scope Analyzer, Cylinder Compression

Pressure Test, Cylinder Combustion Pressure
Leakage Test, Cylinder Head Gasket Failure
Diagnosis and Intake Manifold Leakage
Diagnosis.

SCOPE ANALYZER DIAGNOSIS - IGNITION
SYSTEM TESTER
A scope analyzer is an ignition system tester
that provides a means for quick and accurate
diagnosis of ignition system performance
problems.

### All phases of the ignition cycle are displayed

graphically on an oscilloscope (cathode ray
tube) as they occur during engine operation.
The manufacturers of scope analyzer
equipment provide descriptions of the test
procedures that are possible with their
equipment. This manual is not intended to
describe all the possible uses of scope analyzer
equipment, but to illustrate a typical display of
the Solid State Ignition (SSI) system.

NOTE: Ensure the battery is completely
charged and the starter motor is in good
operating condition. Otherwise the indicated
compression pressures may not be valid for
diagnosis purposes.

### Clean the spark plug recesses with compressed

air.
Remove the spark plugs.
Secure the throttle in the wide-open position.

CYLINDER COMBUSTION PRESSURE
LEAKAGE TEST
The combustion pressure leakage test provides
an accurate means for determining engine
condition.

### Combustion pressure leakage testing will

ascertain exhaust and intake valve leaks
(improper seating), leaks between adjacent
cylinders or into the water jacket, or any causes
for combustion/compression pressure loss.
WARNING: Do not remove the radiator cap with
the system hot and under pressure because
serious burns from coolant can occur.

### Check the coolant level and fill as required. Do

not install the radiator cap.
Start and operate the engine until it attains
normal operating temperature, then turn the
engine OFF.
Remove the spark plugs.
Remove the oil filler cap.
Remove the air cleaner.

### Position the carburetor fast idle speed adjust-

ment screw on the top step of the fast idle cam.
Calibrate the tester according to the manufacturer's instructions.
NOTE: The shop air source for testing should
maintain 483 kPa (70 psi) minimum, 1 379 kPa
(200 psi) maximum, and 552 kPa (80 psi)
recommended.

### Perform the test procedures on each cylinder

according to the tester manufacturer's
instructions.
NOTE: While testing, listen for pressurized air
escaping through the carburetor, tailpipe and oil
filler cap opening. Check for bubbles in the
radiator coolant.

### All gauge pressure indications should be equal,

with no more than 25 percent leakage. For
example, at 552 kPa (80 psi) input pressure, a
minimum of 414 kPa (60 psi) should be
maintained in the cylinder.
Refer to the Cylinder Combustion Pressure
Leakage Test Diagnosis.

### CYLINDER HEAD GASKET FAILURE DIAGNOSIS

A leaking cylinder head gasket usually results in
a loss of power, loss of coolant and engine
misfire.
A cylinder head gasket leak can be located
between adjacent cylinders or between a
cylinder and the adjacent water jacket.

### A cylinder head gasket leaking between two

adjacent cylinders is indicated by a loss of power
and/or engine misfire.
A cylinder head gasket leaking between a
cylinder and an adjacent water jacket is
indicated by coolant foaming or overheating and
loss of coolant.

Cylinier-ti-Water Jacket Leakage Test
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or the fan. Do not wear loose
clothing.

### Remove the radiator cap.

Start the engine and allow it to warm up until the
thermostat opens.
If a large combustion/compression pressure
leak exists, bubbles will be visible in the coolant.
If bubbles are not visible, install a radiator
pressure tester and pressurize the coolant
system.

### If a cylinder is leaking combustion pressure into

the water jacket, the tester pointer will pulsate
with every combustion stroke of the cylinder.
Apply engine oil to the exposed gasket area
(EDGE) between the manifold and the cylinder
head.
INTAKE MANIFOLD LEAKAGE DIAGNOSIS

### An intake manifold air leak is characterized by

lower than normal manifold vacuum. Also, one
or more cylinders may not be functioning.
Intake Manifold Eiterior Leak Diagnosis
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or the fan. Do not wear loose
clothing.

### Start the engine.

Open the acetylene valve of an oxyacetylene
torch. Do not ignite.
Pass the torch tip over the exposed gasket area
(EDGE) between the manifold and the cylinder
head.
If the engine speed increases, the manifold has
an air leak.

### If oil is forced into the manifold and if smoke is

visible from the exhaust tailpipe, the manifold
has an air leak.

ENGINE TUNE-UP PROCEDURES
GENERAL INFORMATION
An engine tune-up is recommended every
48 OOO km (30,000 mi). A tune-up ensures
the engine is operating as efficiently and
economically as it was designed to operate.

### Also, it ensures that undesirable exhaust and

fuel system emission to the atmosphere are
within the limits defined by regulations.
For convenience, when performing a tune-up,
the necessary services are grouped together by
either major assembly or system.

### DRIVE BELTS

Inspect the belts for defects such as fraying and
cracks.
Test the belt tension. Belt tension testing,
adjustment, arrangements and tension specifications are listed in the Cooling Systems
section.
WACUUM HOSES AND FITTINGS

### Inspect the vacuum hose fittings for looseness

and corrosion. Inspect the hoses for brittleness
and cracks.
Thoroughly inspect the hose ends that are
slipped onto nipples.
Engine performance may be adversely affected
by air leaks into such unlikely places as the
heater and air conditioner control vacuum hoses
or the power brake booster vacuum hose.

### IGNITION SYSTEM

Spark Plugs
Remove and examine the spark plugs for
burned electrodes and fouled, cracked or
broken porcelain insulators.
Retain the plugs arranged in the order in which
they were removed from the engine. A specific
plug displaying an abnormal condition indicates
that a problem exists in the cylinder from which it
was removed.

### Replace the plugs at the interval recommended

in the Engine Maintenance Schedule. Plugs with
less engine mileage may be cleaned and reused
in some circumstances. Refer to Spark Plug
Condition.
After cleaning, file the center electrode tip flat
with a point file. Adjust the gap (SEPARATION)
between the electrodes to the specified
dimension.

Always use a torque wrench when .installing the
spark plugs. Distortion from overtightening will
change the plug electrode gap. For all engines,
tighten the plugs with 9.5 - 20 N«m (7-15 ft-lbs)
torque.

### Spark Plug Condition

Compare the spark plug condition with the
illustrated examples and the following
descriptions.
Spark Plug Condition - Electrode Gap Bridging
Electrode gap bridging can result from loose
deposits in the combustion chamber.

### LOW MILEAGE PLUGS WITH THIS

CONDITION MAY BE CLEANED.
60770A
Fluffy deposits may accumulate on the plug
electrodes during stop-and-go driving.
When the engine is suddenly operated with a
high torque load, this material can liquefy and
bridge the gap (i.e., short circuit the electrodes).

### Spark Plug Condition - Scavenger Deposits

Fuel scavenger deposits may be white or yellow.

They may appear to be harmful, but this is a

### Such additives are designed to change the

Notice that the accumulation of deposits on the
ground (side) electrode and shell area may be

### Spark plugs with this type of deposit can be

Spark Plug Condition - Chipped Electrode Insulator
A chipped electrode insulator usually results
from bending the center electrode while
adjusting the spark plug electrode gap.

### PLUGS WITH THIS CONDITION

MUST B E REPLACED.
60770C
Under certain conditions, severe detonation can
also separate the insulator from the center
electrode.
Spark Plug Condition - Pre-ignition Damage
60770D
The Insulators appear relatively clean of
deposits.

### Determine if the spark plug has the correct heat

range rating, if the ignition timing is
overadvanced or if other conditions are causing
engine overheating.
NOTE: The heat range rating refers to the
operating temperature of a particular type spark
plug. Spark plugs are designed to operate within
specific temperature ranges depending upon
the thickness and length of the center electrode
porcelain insulator.

### Pre-ignition damage is caused by excessive

engine temperature. First the center electrode
liquefies, and somewhat later, the ground (side)
electrode.
PLUGS WITH THIS
CONDITION MUST B E REPLACED.

Spark Plug Condition-Cold Fouling/Carbon Fouling

### The deposits that cause cold fouling are

basically carbon.
LOW MILEAGE
P L U G S IN THIS CONDITION MAY B E
CLEANED.
60770E
A dry, black appearance of one or two plugs in a
set may be caused by sticking valves or faulty
spark plug wires.
Cold (carbon) fouling of the entire set may be
caused by a clogged air cleaner or a faulty
carburetor choke.

### Spark Plug Condition - Spark Plug Oterheating

Overheating is indicated by a white or gray
electrode insulator that also appears blistered.
PLUGS IN THIS CONDITION
MUST B E REPLACED.
60770F
The increase in electrode gap will be
considerably in excess of 0.025mm per 1 609
km (0.001 in. per 1000 mi) of engine operation.

### This suggests that a spark plug with a cooler

heat range rating should be used.
Overadvanced ignition timing, detonation and
cooling system malfunctions can also cause
spark plug overheating.
NOTE: Fuel refiners in several parts of the
United States have introduced a manganese
compound additive (MMT) for unleaded fuel.

### During combustion, fuel with MMT causes the

entire tip of the spark plug to be coated with a
rust-colored deposit. This rust color may be
misdiagnosed as being caused by coolant in the
combustion chamber. Spark plug performance
is not affected by MMT deposits.

ENGINE TUNE-UP PROCEDURES
Spark Plug and Ignition Coil Wires
To remove the wires from the spark plugs, twist
the rubber protector boot approximately 1/2 turn
to break the seal.
Grasp the boot and pull it away from the plug
with a constant force.

### Do not pull on the wire itself because this will

damage the conductor and terminal connection.
To remove the wires from the distributor cap or
ignition coil tower, loosen the boot first, then
grasp the upper part of the boot and the wire and
gently pull straight up.

### Spark Plug Wire Test

Do not puncture the spark plug wires with a
probe while performing any test. This may cause
a separation in the conductor.
The preferred method is to remove the
suspected wire and use an ohmmeter to
determine if the resistance is correct for the
length of the particular wire.

### Refer to the Spark Plug and Coil Wire

Resistance Values chart.

### When installing the spark plug wires and the

ignition coil high voltage wire, ensure that
mechanically tight connections are made at the
spark plugs, distributor cap towers and ignition
coil tower.
The wire protector boots at the spark plugs,
distributor cap towers and coil tower must also fit
tightly.

### A partially seated wire terminal creates an air

separation (resistance) in the high voltage
circuit and the resulting arcing will cause
terminal corrosion and wire conductor damage.
When replacing spark plug wires, route the
wires correctly and secure them within the
proper retainers.

### Failure to route the wires properly can result in

radio ignition noise and cross ignition of the
plugs, or short circuit the wires to ground.

ENGINE TUNE-UP PROCEDURES
Ignition Coil
Always test a suspected malfunctioning ignition
coil while installed in the vehicle. Because a coil
may break down only after it has reached normal
operating temperature, it is important that the
coil be at normal operating temperature, when
tested.

### If using an ignition coil tester (not an ohmmeter),

perform the tests according to the instructions
provided by the manufacturer of the equipment.
Refer to the Ignition Systems section within
Chapter C for additional information.
Distributor
The distributor is the Solid State Ignition (SSI)
type.

### Other than cap and rotor inspection, there is no

scheduled maintenance for the distributor.
Refer to the Ignition Systems section within
Chapter C for distributor service procedures.
Distributor Rotor Inspection
Visually inspect the rotor for cracks (1),
evidence of corrosion (2) and the effects of
arcing on the metal tip, and evidence of
mechanical interference with the cap (3).
4
840114

### A small quantity of silicone dielectric compound

is applied to the rotor tips during manufacture to
reduce radio ignition noise and interference.
After a few thousand miles of engine operation,
this compound becomes charred. This is
normal. Do not scrape the residue from the rotor
tip.

### Inspect the spring (4) for insufficient tension.

Replace a rotor displaying any adverse
condition.
Coat the tip of the replacement rotor with AMC
Silicone Dielectric Compound, or equivalent.

Distributor Cap Inspection

### Remove the distributor cap and clean it with a

clean, dry cloth. Visually inspect for cracks (1),
carbon paths (2), broken towers (3), charred or
eroded terminals (4) and a damaged rotor
button (5). Replace any cap that has any of
these discrepancies.

### When replacing a cap, transfer one ignition wire

at a time to the replacement cap. If necessary,
refer to the Distributor Wiring Diagram.

Ignition System Timing
Six-cylinder engines have a graduated timing
degree scale (1) located on the timing case
cover that is used for reference when timing the
ignition system.

### A milled index notch (2) in the vibration damper

is used to align the No. 1 cylinder ignition
position of the crankshaft with the correct timing
degree mark on the graduated scale.
Magnetic Timing Probe
Six-cylinder engines have a magnetic timing
probe socket (3) integral with the timing degree
scale for use with a special magnetic timing
probe.

### This special probe detects the milled notch on

the vibration damper. The probe is inserted
through the probe socket until it contacts the
vibration damper.
Ignition timing can then be obtained from a
meter or computer printout, depending on the
type of equipment being used.

### The probe socket is located at 9.5° ATDC, and

the equipment is calibrated to compensate for
this location.
Do not use the timing probe socket as a
reference to check the ignition timing when
using a conventional timing light.
Ignition Timing Procedure - 4.2 Liter (218 CID)
(Sii-Cylinder Engine)

### The ignition timing can be adjusted according to

the following primary timing procedure.
Set the parking brake. Shift automatic
transmissions to P A R K and manual
transmissions to the NEUTRAL position.
Start the engine and allow it to attain normal
operating temperature. Ensure that the A/C is
turned OFF, if equipped.

advance hose.
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or the fan. Do not wear loose
clothing.

### Start the engine.

Increase the engine speed to 1600 rpm and
check the ignition timing. If necessary, adjust the
timing to the specification listed on the Emission
Control Information label. Also, refer to the
ignition advance curve illustrations.

### Tighten the distributor hold-down clamp and

verify that the ignition timing is correct.
Turn the engine OFF and remove the timing light
and tachometer.
Connect the No. 1 spark plug wire, if disconnected. Connect the hose to the distributor
vacuum advance mechanism. Connect the wire
connector to the vacuum switch assembly.

### The ignition timing can also be adjusted

according to the following alternate procedure.
The Alternate Timing Procedure does not
require that the engine speed be increased to
1600 rpm.
Set the parking brake.
Shift automatic transmissions to PARK and
manual transmissions to the N E U T R A L
position.

### Start the engine and allow it to attain normal

operating temperature. Ensure that the A/C is
turned to the OFF position, if equipped.
With the ignition switch OFF, connect an ignition
timing light and a calibrated, expanded scale
tachometer.
NOTE: If the timing light has an adjustable
advance control feature, turn the control to the

### OFF position.

Disconnect the 4-in. Hg vacuum switch hose
(located at the top of the cylinder head cover)
and plug the hose opening.
NOTE: The 4-in. Hg vacuum switch has black
and red wires connected to it.
Disconnect the distributor vacuum advance
hose and connect the hose to the 4-inch Hg
vacuum switch.

### Disconnect the knock sensor wire connector

and connect the wire connector to the cylinder
block (GROUND) with a jumper wire.
NOTE: Grounding the knock sensor wire connector prevents electromagnetic interference
(EMI) from causing erroneous reactions by the

### FFB system micro computer unit (MCU).

Start the engine.

ENGINE TUNE-UP PROCEDURES
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or the fan. Do not wear loose
clothing.

### With the engine at idle speed, check the timing.

If necessary, adjust the timing one degree
higher than the specification listed on the
Emission Control Information label. Also, refer
to the ignition advance curve illustrations.
NOTE: With the alternate timing procedure, the
basic timing must be one degree higher than the
specification listed on the Emission Control

### Information label. For example, if the timing

specification is listed as 6° ± 2° at 1600 rpm, the
alternate procedure requires 7° ± 2 ° at idle
speed.

Six-Cylinder OILY
Centrifugal Advance Test
Set the parking brake. Shift automatic transmissions to PARK and manual transmissions to

### NEUTRAL

Start the engine and allow it to attain normal
operating temperature. Ensure that the A/C is
turned OFF, if equipped.
With the ignition switch OFF, disconnect the
three-wire connector from the 4-in. and 10-in.

### Hg vacuum switch assembly.

Disconnect and plug the vacuum hose
connected to the distributor vacuum advance
mechanism.
Connect a timing light between the No. 1 spark
plug and wire.
Connect the timing light power wire connectors
according to the manufacturer's instructions.

### Connect a calibrated, expanded scale tach-

ometer to the coil negative (TACH) terminal.
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or fan. Do not wear loose clothing.

### Start the engine and slowly increase the speed

while observing the timing mark and index with
the timing light.
The ignition timing should advance smoothly as
the engine speed increases. Refer to the ignition
advance curve illustrations.
If the ignition timing advances unevenly, check
and repair the centrifugal advance mechanism.

### Connect the distributor vacuum advance hose

and the vacuum switch assembly three-wire
connector.
Remove the timing light and connect the No. 1
cylinder spark plug wire.
Remove the tachometer.
Vacuum Advance Test - Six-Cylinder ONLY
Set the parking brake. Shift automatic
transmissions to P A R K and
manual
transmissions to the NEUTRAL position.

### Start the engine and allow it to attain normal

operating temperature. Ensure that the A/C is
turned OFF, if equipped.

m
With the ignition switch OFF, disconnect the
three-wire connector from the 4-in. and 10-in.
vacuum switch assembly.

### Disconnect and plug the vacuum hose

connected to the distributor vacuum advance
mechanism.
Connect Hand Operated Vacuum Pump
J-23738-A, or equivalent, to the distributor
vacuum advance mechanism.
Connect a timing light between the No. 1 spark
plug and wire.

### Connect the timing light power wire connectors

according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Connect a calibrated, expanded scale tachometer to the coil negative (TACH) terminal.
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or fan. Do not wear loose clothing.

### Start the engine.

Increase the engine speed and apply 60.9 kPa
(18-in. Hg) vacuum.
Observe the ignition timing degree scale and
index with the timing light.
The ignition timing should advance smoothly.
Refer to the ignition advance curve illustrations.

### NOTE: A defective FFB system MCU or ignition

system ECU can alter the ignition timing.
Remove the timing light and tachometer.
Connect the spark plug wire.
Distributor Advance Mechanism Testing -
OFF-Engine - Six-Cylinder ONLY
The distributor ignition advance may also be
tested with the distributor removed from the
engine. Follow the distributor test equipment
manufacturer's instructions.

### The information provided within the ignition

advance curve illustrations is for on-engine
testing.
If the distributor ignition advance is boing tested
with a distributor tester, convert the information
within the ignition advance curves from engine
rpm to distributor rpm and from engine degrees
to distributor degrees:

### Distributor

Divide the engine rpm by 2 to obtain the
distributor rpm.
Distributor Degrees Advance
Divide the engine degrees advance by 2 to
obtain the distributor degrees advance.
For example, if the ignition advance curve
indicates 8 -12 degrees advance at 2000 rpm,
the corresponding on-tester specifications
would be 4 - 6 degrees advance at 1000 rpm.

### NOTE: The specified kPa (in. Hg) of vacuum is

the same, regardless if the test is on-engine or
off-engine.

ENGINE TUNE-UP PROCEDURES

### FUEL SYSTEM

General Information
The fuel system depends on hoses and tubing to
route liquid fuel, fuel vapor and vacuum.
Fuel vapor leaks and air leaks into the vacuum
hoses and fittings upset the operation of the
engine and may reduce the effectiveness of the
emission control devices.

### Liquid fuel leaks not only waste fuel but also

create a fire hazard.
Carefully inspect the hoses and fuel pipes for
cracks, dents, corrosion and abnormal bends.
Inspect the fittings for corrosion and looseness.
Inspect the fuel tank for leaks caused by loose
mounting straps, broken seams, dents or
corrosion.

### Inspect the filler neck grommets and hoses for

the proper condition.
Air Cleaner
Replace the dry-type air cleaner filter element
during each tune-up. Under extreme engine
operating conditions, more frequent replacement is recommended.
Fiil Filter

### All Jeep vehicles have two fuel filters:

• The in-tank filter is designed to be maintenance-free.
• The in-line filter located between the fuel
pump and the carburetor/throttle
body
requires periodic replacement.
The fuel filter is located on the left frame rail on

### TBI models.

When installing a replacement filter, ensure the
fuel return nipple is positioned above the filter
(Six-Cylinder ONLY).

Idle Speed Adjustment - Six-Cylinder Engine

### WARNING: Use extreme caution when the

engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulleys, belts or fan. Do not wear loose clothing.
Connect a calibrated, expanded scale tachometer to the ignition coil negative (TACH)
terminal.

### Start and allow the engine to attain normal

operating temperature.
The carburetor choke and intake manifold
heater must be off. This occurs when the engine
coolant heats to approximately 71 °C (160°F).
NOTE: When adjusting the idle speed, place
manual transmissions in the NEUTRAL position
and automatic transmissions in DRIVE. Turn all
accessories off.

### WARNING: Set the parking brake firmly. Do not

accelerate the engine.
NOTE: Adjust the idle speeds to the specifications listed on the engine compartment
emission label.
Sole-Wac Wacuum Actuator Adjustment
Disconnect and plug the vacuum hose to the
sole-vac vacuum actuator.

### Disconnect the sole-vac electrical connector.

Connect an external vacuum source to the
vacuum actuator and apply 10-15 inches (Hg.)
of vacuum.
Open throttle for AT LEAST 3.0 SECONDS
(1200 rpm); then, close the throttle.
Set the speed using the vacuum actuator
adjustment screw on the throttle lever to obtain
specified rpm.

### Disconnect the external vacuum source.

Reconnect the sole-vac vacuum hose and
electrical connector.
Sole-Wac Holding Solenoid Adjustment
NOTE: The sole-vac vacuum actuator adjustment should ALWAYS PRECEDE the sole-vac
solenoid adjustment.

### Disconnect and plug the vacuum hose to the

sole-vac vacuum actuator.
Disconnect the sole-vac electrical connector.
