Install the park gear on the output shaft.
Install the governor body (D) on the output shaft
(A) and against the park gear (E).
Align the shaft bore in the governor body with
the shaft bore in the output shaft.

### NEUTRAL SAFETY SWITCH

The switch (1) is actuated by the valve body
manual lever (2). The switch has three terminals. The center terminal is the starting circuit. It
provides a ground for the starter solenoid circuit through the gearshift lever in Park and Neutral. The outer terminals of the switch are for
the backup lamp circuit. Switch removal, testing
and installation procedures are as follows:
1
84105

### Starting Circuit Test

Remove the wiring connector from the switch
(1).
Check continuity between the center switch terminal and the transmission case in all gearshift
lever positions. Continuity should exist only in
Park and Neutral.

### If continuity exists in any position other than

Park or Neutral, check and adjust the gearshift
linkage and repeat the continuity check. Replace the switch if continuity still exists in any
position other than Park or Neutral.
Backup Lamp Circuit Test

### Remove the wiring connector from the switch

(1).
Check continuity between the switch outer terminals. Continuity between the two terminals
should exist only in Reverse. Replace the
switch if continuity is indicated in any gear other
than Reverse.

### Check continuity between each terminal and the

transmission case in Reverse. Replace the
switch if continuity is indicated.
Neutral Safety Switch Replacement
Raise the vehicle.
Disconnect the switch harness.
Position a drain pan under the switch and remove the switch from the c center of the case
opening if necessary.
35

### AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
Install the replacement switch and seal in the
case. Tighten the switch to 35 N*m (24 ft-lbs)
torque.
Verify that switch continuity exists only in Park
and Neutral.
Top off the transmission fluid level.

### OIL COOLER AND COOLER LINE FLUSHING

Main Oil Cooler
The main transmission oil cooler is located in
the radiator lower tank. The cooler and cooler
lines must be flushed whenever a transmission
malfunction generates sludge and metal or friction material particles.

### Auxiliary Oil Cooler

The auxiliary oil cooler augments the transmission cooler in the radiator lower tank. The auxiliary cooler helps prevent fluid overheating during heavy-duty operation. The auxiliary cooler
and lines must also be flushed whever a malfunction generates sludge and metal or friction
material particles.

### Oil Cooler and Line Flushing Procedure

Remove the auxiliary oil cooler and lines.
Disconnect and remove the main cooler lines.
Dislodge any foreign material in the inlet side of
the main cooler with a small screwdriver.
Reverse flush the main and auxiliary coolers
and lines with a combination of mineral spirits
and short bursts of compressed air. Continue
forcing solvent through the coolers until all oil
and foreign material are removed.

### Remove any remaining mineral spirits from the

coolers and lines by flushing them with clean
transmission fluid.
Check fluid flow through the main cooler as
follow:
• Connect the cooler inlet line to the main (radiator) cooler.
• Connect the cooler outlet line to the main
cooler but not to the transmission.
• Place the transmission end of the cooler outlet line in a one quart container.
• Overfill the transmission by one quart.
• Shift the transmission into Neutral.
• Run the engine at curb idle speed for exactly
20 seconds and observe oil flow into the
container. If less than one quart flows into
the container in 20 seconds, replace the radiator or recondition the cooler.

### Connect the main cooler outlet line to the

transmission.
Install and connect the auxiliary cooler and
lines.
Check and adjust transmission fluid level.
F-36
AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
TRANSMISSION REMOVAL
Disconnect the battery negative cable.

### Remove the fan shroud attaching screws.

Disconnect the transmission fill tube upper
bracket.
Raise the vehicle.
Remove the converter housing inspection cover, transmission fill tube and the starter motor if
necessary.
Mark the front and rear propeller shafts for assembly reference and remove the shafts.

### Disconnect the transmission gearshift and

throttle linkage.
Disconnect the transfer case vent and vacuum
hoses and the neutral safety switch wires.
Mark the converter and drive plate for assembly
reference and remove the converter-to-drive
plate attaching bolts.

### Support the transmission with a jack stand and

remove the rear crossmember.
Drain the transfer case lubricant and disconnect
the speedometer cable.
Disconnect the transmission main cooler lines
at the transmission.
Disconnect the transfer case shift linkage.

### Support the transmission-transfer case assem-

bly with a transmission jack.
Remove the support stand previously installed
under the transmission and reposition it under
the engine rear main.
Remove the bolts attaching the transmission to
the engine and remove the transmission-transfer case assembly from the vehicle.

### Remove the nuts attaching the transfer case to

the transmission adapter housing and remove
the transfer case from the transmission.
TRANSMISSION INSTALLATION
Mount the transmission on a transmission jack.
Position the transfer case on the transmission
adapter housing and install the transfer case
attaching nuts. Tighten the nuts to 35 U*m (26
ft-lbs) torque.

### If the torque converter was removed, align the

converter hub drive slots with the pump rotor
drive lugs using alignment tool J 24033. Then
install the converter.
NOTE: Be sure the rotor drive lugs are fully
seated in the converter hub drive slots before
proceeding.

### Raise the transmission-transfer case assembly

and align the converter pilot hub with the pilot
bore in the engine crankshaft. Move the transmission forward and seat the hub.
Install two of the transmission attaching bolts.
Tighten the bolts just enough to draw the converter housing forward and into contact with the
engine.

### P~37

AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
SEE
i.S.
N
O
T
E
S
Align the converter and drive plate according to
the reference marks made during removal. Install and tighten the drive plate-to-converter
bolts to 35 N«m (26 ft-lbs) torque.

### Install the remaining transmission attaching

bolts. Tighten all of the attaching bolts to 38
NTTI (28 ft-lbs) torque.
Install the converter housing inspection cover
and connect the main cooler lines to the
transmission.
Connect the transfer vent and vacuum lines and
connect the neutral safety switch wires and the
speedometer cable.

### Install the transmission fill tube and install the

starter motor if removed.
Remove the support stand from under the engine and reposition it under the transmission
clutch housing. Then remove the transmission
jack from under the transmission-transfer case
assembly.

### Install the rear crossmember. Tighten the sup-

port cushion-to-crossmember bolts to 45 fskn
(33 ft-lbs) torque. Tighten the crossmember-toframe rail bolts to 41 NеН (30 ft-lbs) torque.
Connect the transmission throttle and gearshift
linkage.
Connect the transfer case shift linkage and refill
the transfer case with JEEP automatic transmission fluid, or an equivalent Dexron® II fluid.

### Install the front and rear propeller shafts. Align

the shafts according to the reference marks
made during removal. Tighten the U-joint clamp
bolts to 19 N « m (170 in-lbs) torque.
Check and adjust the transmission gearshift
and throttle linkage if necessary.

### Fill the transmission with specified fluid.

STEERING AND FRONT AXLE

### GENERAL INFORMATION

STEEHING AND PiONT AILE COMPONENTS
Steering Columns
One standard steering column and two tilt
steering columns are used. The standard
column is used for manual transmission
applications. One tilt column is used for manual
transmission applications. A second tilt column
is used for column shift automatic transmission
applications.

### Steering Gears

Manual and power steering gears are available.
Both gears are recirculating ball design units.
Power Steering Pump
A constant displacement, vane-type pump is
used for power steering applications. The pump
is belt driven off the engine crankshaft.

### Steering Damper

A steering damper is used on all models. The
damper is attached to the center steering link
and the spring mounting bracket.
Front Axle
A Model 30 front axle is used in all models. The
axle
has a vacuum
shift
mechanism to
disengage or engage the right front axle shaft for
two or four wheel drive operation.

Steering Linkage
Parallel linkage rods are used. A pitman arm
connects the linkage to the steering gear.

Front wheel alignment should be checked on an
alignment rack to ensure accurate results.
The front wheel toe setting and caster angle are
the only adjustable alignment angles on the front
axle. Camber is preset during manufacture and
is not adjustable.

### CHECKING FiONT WHEEL ALIGNMENT

Check and adjust tire inflation pressures. Note
any unusual wear pattern on the tires.
Check the front and rear suspension components for loose or damaged attaching bolts/
nuts. Tighten or replace as necessary.

### Check the steering knuckle ball studs, steering

linkage and front wheel bearings. Repair or
replace loose, worn parts if necessary.
Check steering gear adjustment. Correct the
overcenter and drag torque adjustments if
necessary.
Position the vehicle on the alignment rack.

### Check camber angle (A-B). Camber is preset

at 0°. Ok range is from minus 1/2 degree to plus
1/2 degree.

STEEiliG LINKAGE COMPONENTS
The linkage consists of the
following
components:
• Center link (1).
• Center link rod ends (2).
• Tie rod (4).
• Tie rod adjusting sleeve (5).
• Tie rod end (6).
• Steering damper (7).

### The steering damper, tie rod, pitman arm, center

link and rod ends (2) and (6) are serviceable
components. The tie rod (4) must be replaced if
the fixed rod end is worn or damaged.
Replacement procedures are as follows.
101478
Center Link Replacement

### Remove the cotter pins and nuts attaching the

link to the pitman arm and center link.
Loosen the rod ends with a puller tool and
remove the center link.
NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the center
link if only one of the rod ends is to be replaced.

### Loosen the rod end clamp bolts and remove the

rod ends from the link.
Assemble the replacement center link
components and install the link.
Tighten the rod end nuts and install replacement
cotter pins.
Adjust front wheel toe setting as outlined in this
section.

### Tie Rei Replacement

Disconnect the steering damper from the tie rod.
Remove the cotter pins and nuts attaching the
tie rod to the steering knuckles and center link.
Loosen the tie rod ends with a puller tool and
remove the tie rod.

### Remove the adjusting sleeve and rod end from

the tie rod.
Assemble the tie rod end components and
install the rod.
Install the nuts attaching the tie rod to the
steering knuckles and center link.

STEERING LINKAGE

### Tighten the attaching nuts and install

replacement cotter pins.
Connect the steering damper to the tie rod.
Adjust front wheel toe setting as outlined in this
section.
Steering Damper Replacement
Place the front wheels in a straight-ahead
position.

### Remove the damper attaching bolt, nuts and

cotter pins.
Remove the damper.
Extend the damper piston enough to align the
damper mounting eye and rod end with the axle
bracket and tie rod.
Mount the damper on the bracket and tie rod.
Install the damper attaching bolt, nuts and
replacement cotter pins.

STEERING COLUMN SERVICE
GENERAL SERfiCE INFORMATION
It is not necessary to remove the steering
column in order to service the various switches
and components inside the column housing.

### Column removal is only necessary when the

column jacket, shift tube, steering shaft, or lower
bearing assembly must be replaced.
Refer to the steering column disassembly
procedures for removal and installation of the
switches and components mounted inside the
column housing.

### The ignition and dimmer switches are both

mounted on the exterior of the column jacket.
Switch replacement and adjustment procedures
are outlined in the following procedures.
IGNITION SWITCH REPLACEMENT
Ignition Switch Removal
Disconnect the battery negative cable.

### Tape the dimmer switch actuator rod (3) to the

column to prevent the rod from disengaging.
Remove the dimmer switch (2).
Disconnect the ignition switch wire harness.
Remove the ignition switch (1). Lift the switch
upward until it clears the actuator rod and
remove the switch.

### Ignition Switch Installation

Insert the actuator rod into the access hole at the
bottom of the replacement ignition switch.
Install the switch on the column.
Adjust the ignition switch as follows:
• Turn the ignition lock cylinder to the Off-

### U/nlock position.

• Loosen the switch screws.
<§ Move the switch downward to eliminate
lash and tighten the switch screws to 4 N-m
(35 in-lbs) torque.
Connect the wire harness to the ignition
switch (1).
Engage the actuator rod (3) in the dimmer switch
(2) and install the switch on the column jacket.

### Remove the tape holding the actuator rod (3) to

the column.
Adjust the dimmer switch (2) as follows:
• Compress the switch slightly and insert a 3/32
inch diameter drill into switch hole (A). The drill
will prevent any horizontal movement of the
switch.
• Move the switch toward the steering wheel to
remove actuator rod lash.

• Tighten the switch attaching screws to 4 N-m
(35 in-lbs) torque.
• Connect the battery negative cable.
• Remove the drill and check switch operation.

### Readjust the switch if necessary.

NOTE: If a tilt column is being serviced, check
switch operation in all tilt positions.
84714
DIMMER SWITCH REPLACEMENT
Dimmer Switch Removal
Disconnect the battery negative cable.
Tape the dimmer switch actuator rod (3) to the
column to prevent the rod from disengaging.

### Remove the dimmer switch attaching screws

and remove the switch (2).
Dimmer Switch Installation
Engage the actuator rod in the switch (2) and
mount the switch on the column.
Remove the tape holding the actuator rod to the
column.
Adjust the dimmer switch (2) as follows:
• Compress the switch slightly and insert a 3/32
inch diameter drill into switch hole (A). The drill
will prevent any horizontal movement of the
switch.
o Move the switch toward the steering wheel to
remove actuator rod lash.
• Tighten the switch attaching screws to 4 N-m
(35 in-lbs) torque.
• Connect the battery negative cable.
o Remove the drill and check switch operation.

### Readjust the switch if necessary.

NOTEIf a tilt column is being serviced, check
switch operation in all tilt positions.

STEERING COLUMN INSTALLATION AND
ALIGNMENT
CAUTION: Be sure to preserve the energy
absorbing features of the steeering column. Use
only the specified screws, bolts and nuts and
tighten them to specified torque during
reassembly. Incorrect size or length fasteners
can prevent the column from compressing
under impact. The bolts and nuts that attach the
column mounting bracket to the column and
instrument panel must be tightened to the
correct torque to maintain the breakaway
capability of the bracket.

### Position the column in the vehicle.

Align the intermediate shaft U-joint (2) and
steering shaft (1) and slide the U-joint onto the
shaft.
Install and tighten the U-joint pinch bolt (3) to 45
N-m (33 ft-lbs) torque.
Install the mounting bracket (B) on the steering
column. Tighten the bracket-to-column bolts to
28 N-m (21 ft-lbs) torque.

### Install the upper and lower toe plates (4) on the

column. Do not tighten the toe plate bolts at this
time.
Position the toe plates on the floorpan and install
the toe plate-to-floorpan bolts. Do not tighten the
bolts at this time.
Position the column mounting bracket (B) on the
instrument panel and install the bracket
attaching bolts (A) finger tight.

### Pull up on the column and tighten the mounting

bracket bolts (A) to 28 N-m (21 ft-lbs) torque.
Tighten all of the toe plate attaching bolts to 14
N-m (10 ft-lbs) torque.
Install the trim cover on the speedometertachometer assembly.
Connect all of the column wire harnesses.

### Remove the protective tape from painted areas

of the column.
Install the steering wheel.
On models with automatic transmission, check
and adjust the gearshift linkage if necessary.
Connect the battery negative cable.

MANUAL STEERING GEAR ADJUSTMENT-IN
VEHICLE
Manual steering gear worm bearing preload and
overcenter drag torque can be adjusted with the
gear in the vehicle.
CAUTION: Adjust steering gear preload and
overcenter drag torque in the following
sequence only. Failure to do so could result in
damage to the gear or improper steering
response. Always adjust worm bearing preload
first and overcenter drag torque last.

### Raise and support the vehicle. Check and

correct steering gear mounting bolt torque, if
necessary.

### CAUTION: Do not turn the steering wheel hard

against the stop when the linkage is disconnected. This could damage the steering gear
ball return guides.
Measure worm bearing preload as follows:
• Install a socket and inch-pound torque wrench
on the steering wheel nut.
• Measure worm bearing preload by rotating the
wheel through a 90° arc (1/4 turn). Preload
should be 0.6 to 1 N-m (5-8 in-lbs) torque.
• Record worm bearing preload and proceed to
tne next step,

### Center the steering gear. Rotate the steering

wheel from stop-to-stop and count the total
number of turns. Then turn the steering wheel
back 1/2 the total number of turns to center the
gear.
Measure steering gear overcenter drag torque
as follows:
9 Turn the steering gear off center.
• Install the socket and inch-pound torque
wrench on the steering wheel nut.
© Measure the torque required to turn the gear
through the center of travel (overcenter drag
torque).
• Drag torque should equal worm bearing
preload torque plus 0.5-1.0 N-m (4-10 in-lbs)
but must not exceed a total of 2 N-m (18 in-lbs)
torque.
• For example if worm bearing preload is 0.7

### N-m (6 in-lbs) torque, overcenter drag torque

should not exceed 1.3 N-m (12 in-lbs) torque.
This makes a total of 2 N-m (18 in-lbs) which is
the maximum allowable,
If adjustment is necessary, adjust preload first
and drag torque last as follows:
• Loosen the worm bearing adjuster locknut.
• Turn the worm bearing preload adjuster
clockwise
to
i n c r e a s e preload
or
counterclockwise to decrease preload. When
desired preload is obtained, tighten the
adjuster locknut and recheck preload.

### Readjust if necessary and proceed to next

step.
• Loosen the pitman shaft adjusting screw
locknut and loosen or tighten the adjusting
screw to obtain desired drag torque. Tighten
the adjusting screw locknut and recheck drag
torque. Correct adjustment if necessary.

Disconnect the intermediate steering shaft from
the gear.
Raise and support the vehicle.
Disconnect the center link from the pitman arm.

### Remove the front stabilizer bar.

Remove the pitman arm nut.
Mark the pitman arm and shaft for installation

Remove the steering gear mounting bolts and
remove the gear.

### Position the steering gear on the frame and

install the gear mounting bolts.
Align and install the pitman arm on the pitman
shaft.
Install and tighten the pitman nut.
Stake the pitman nut to the shaft in two places.
CAUTION: The pitman nut must be securely
staked to the pitman shaft for proper retention.

### Connect the center link to the pitman arm.

Install the front stabilizer bar.
Remove the supports and lower the vehicle.
Connect the intermediate steering shaft to the
steering gear.

### Cleaning and Inspection

Clean the steering gear components with
solvent and dry them with shop towels or
compressed air.
Inspect the housing for cracks, porosity,
damaged threads or gasket surface scoring or
distortion.
Inspect the pitman shaft bore contact surface
and the sector teeth for wear, pitting, or other
damage.

### Insert the pitman shaft in the housing bore and

check for shaft or housing bore wear. The shaft
should be a smooth, bind free fit and not display
any visible side play when installed in the bore.
If the shaft appears loose but is not visibly worn,
trial fit a replacement shaft in the housing bore. If
the replacement shaft is also loose, replace the
housing. However, if the replacement shaft fits
properly, discard the original pitman shaft.

### Inspect the wormshaft bearings and races for

wear, flat spots, pitting, cracks, or other
damage. If either the bearing or race is
damaged, both parts must be replaced.
If the upper race is loose in the housing, trial fit a
replacement race. If the replacement race is
also loose, replace the housing. If the
replacement race fits properly, do not replace
the housing.

AND ADJUSTMENT
Position the ball nut (12) on its side with the deep
part of the sector teeth (A) facing down.
Thread the wormshaft (11) into the ball nut (12)
until an equal number of shaft threads (B) are
visible at each end of the nut.

### 84753A

CAUTION: The ball nut teeth are machined to a
greater width and depth on one side (A). When
assembling the wormshaft and ball nut, position
the ball nut so these teeth (A) will face the
housing side cover after installation.

### Install one bearing (13) in each ball guide hole in

the ball nut. Move the wormshaft up and down
and side-to-side until the bearings roll down
the ball nut threads and under the wormshaft to
support it.
Install the ball guides (15) in the ball nut (12).

(18 in-lbs). For example if worm bearing preload
is 0.7 N-m (6 in-lbs), overcenter drag torque
must not exceed 1.3 N-m (12 in-lbs). This makes

allowable.

### POWER STEERING SYSTEM LEAK INSPECTION

Raise and support the vehicle.
Clean the exterior surfaces of the gear, pump,
hoses, and fittings thoroughly.
Check and correct fluid level in the pump
reservoir.
Check for aerated fluid which can cause
overflow from the reservoir and be mistaken for
a leak.

### Check and tighten the hose connections at the

gear and the pump if necessary.
Start the engine. Have a helper turn the steering
wheel left and right while checking for leak
sources. Contact the stops momentarily in each
direction. Stop the engine when the leak source
is identified.

### Steering gear leaks can develop in the following

areas.
• hoses and fittings
• adjuster plug O-ring
• stub shaft seals
• steering gear housing core plug
• torsion bar seal (replace valve body assembly
if seal leaks)
• side cover locknut and cover gasket
• pitman shaft seals
• end plug gasket
• cracked or porous gear housing

### PITMAN SHAFT SEAL REPLACEMENT

Raise and support the vehicle. Place the front
wheels in a straight ahead position.
Remove the front stabilizer bar.
Disconnect the center link from the pitman arm.
Mark the pitman arm and shaft for assembly
reference and disconnect the arm with puller

### J 6632-01.

pitman shaft.

snap ring pliers and remove the outer seal
backup washer (2).

backup washers (2-4) from the pitman shaft.

and in the gear housing. Replace the shaft or

Apply a single layer of thin tape to the pitman

Leave only enough room for the retaining ring.

### Fill the pump reservoir to the correct level with

power steering fluid.
Start the engine and allow it to idle for at least
three minutes, Do not turn the steering wheel
during this time.
Turn the steering wheel left and right and check
for leaks.
Recheck fluid level in the reservoir. Add fluid if
required.

HOUSING END PLUG SEAL REPLACEMENT
Rotate the end cover retainer ring until one end
of the ring is positioned over the hole in the side
of the housing. Unseat the ring from the housing
groove with a punch inserted through the hole in
the housing.

### Position a drain pan under the steering gear end

plug.
CAUTION: Do not turn the steering wheel any
farther than necessary during the next step. The
ball bearings could drop out of the rack piston
circuit and fall inside the rack piston chamber.
Turn the steering wheel slowly to the left until the
rack piston forces the end plug out of the
housing. Then immediately turn the wheel back
to center position and stop the engine.

### Remove and discard the end plug O-ring seal.

Lubricate the replacement end plug seal with
power steering fluid and install the seal on the
end plug.
Install the end plug and end plug retaining ring.

HISSING NOISE IN
STEERING GEAR
(1) There is some n o i s e in all power
steering systems. One of the
most common is a hissing
sound most evident at standstill
parking. There is no relationship between this noise and performance of the steering. Hiss
may be expected when steering
wheel is at end of travel or when
slowly turning at standstill.
(1) Slight hiss is normal and in no way
affects steering. Do not replace
valve unless hiss is extremely objectionable. A replacement valve
will also exhibit slight noise and is
not always a cure. Investigate
clearance around flexible coupling
rivets. Be sure steering shaft and
gear are aligned so flexible coupling rotates in a flat plane and is not
distorted as shaft rotates. Any
metal-to-metal contacts through
flexible coupling will transmit valve
hiss into passenger compartment
through the steering column.

### POWER STEERING GEAR

POWER STEERING GEAR REMOVAL
Place the wheels in a straight-ahead position.
Position a drain pan under the steering gear.
Disconnect the hoses at the gear. Raise and
secure the hoses above pump fluid level to
prevent excessive oil spillage. Cap the ends of
the hoses to prevent any entry of dirt.

### Disconnect the intermediate shaft from the

steering gear stub shaft.
Raise and support the vehicle.
Mark the pitman arm and shaft for assembly
reference.
Disconnect the center link from the pitman arm
and remove the front stabilizer bar.
Disconnect the pitman arm with tool J 6632-01.

### Remove the steering gear mounting bolts and

remove the gear.
POWER STEERING GEAR INSTALLATION
Center the steering gear.
Install the gear in the vehicle.
Align and connect the intermediate shaft to the
stub shaft.
Align and connect the pitman arm. Tighten the
pitman nut and stake the nut to the pitman shaft
in two places.

### Install the front stablizer bar and connect the

center link to the pitman arm.
Lower the vehicle.
Connect the hoses to the gear and tighten the
fittings.
Fill the pump reservoir and bleed air from the
system.

### POWER STEERING GEAR DISASSEMBLY

CAUTION: Cleanliness is extremely important
when overhauling the power steering gear.
Keep the bench, tools, and component parts
clean at all times. Thoroughly clean the exterior
of the gear with solvent before disassembly and
drain as much of the fluid as possible. Use
protective vise jaws at all times when mounting
subassemblies in a vise. At assembly, lubricate
all parts with power steering fluid or petroleum
jelly as indicated.

### Major Component Renewal

Drain all fluid from the gear.
Mount the gear in a vise with the pitman shaft
pointing downward. Clamp the vise jaws on the
unmachined housing boss (A) only.

punch.

### 84772A

stub shaft (17) counterclockwise with 12-point

piston (3) pushes the end plug out.
NOTE: Do not rotate the stub shaft any further
than necessary or the ball bearings will drop out
causing the pitman shaft and rack piston to
disengage. If disengagement occurs, remove

### 84788A

Cleaning and Inspection
Cleaning
Clean the valve body components with solvent
and dry them with compressed air only. Do not
use shop towels or similar lint producing
materials. Place the gear components on paper
after cleaning and during assembly operations.

### Inspection

Inspect the valve body components. A slight
polishing is normal on valve body surfaces as
are tiny flat spots on the valve spool locating pin
(B). If there are scores, nicks or burrs on any of
the finely machined surfaces that cannot be
removed with crocus cloth, replace the valve
body assembly. Inspect the outside diameter of
the spool valve and the inside diameter of the
valve body for nicks or wear. Replace the valve
body assembly if minor irregularities cannot be
removed with crocus cloth.

Power Steering Gear Adjustment
CAUTION: The following adjustment procedures must be performed exactly as
described and in the sequence outlined. Failure
to do so can result in damage to the gear internal
components or improper steering response.

### Always adjust worm bearing preload first and

pitman shaft overcenter drag torque last.
Worm Bearing Preload Adjustment
If the adjuster plug was not previously seated in
the housing, seat the plug with tool J 7624.
Approximately 27 N-m (20 ft-lbs) torque is
required.

### Place an index mark (J) on the gear housing

opposite one of the holes (K) in the adjuster
plug (45).
84802A
Measure back (counterclockwise) 4.7 to 6.3 mm
(3/16 to 1/4 inch) from index mark (J) and make
a second index mark (L) on the housing.

index mark (L).

Install and tighten the adjuster plug locknut (20)
to 115 N-m (85 ft-lbs) torque. Do not allow the
adjuster plug to rotate when tightening the
locknut.

### Turn the stub shaft clockwise to the stop. Then

turn the stub shaft back 1/4 turn.
Install a 12-point deep socket (M) on the stub
shaft splines.
Measure torque required to turn the stub shaft
with an inch-pound torque wrench having a
maximum capacity of 6 N-m (50 in-lbs). Take the
reading with the beam of the torque wrench at or
near the vertical position (N) while turning the
stub shaft at an even rate.

### 84804A

Torque required to turn the stub shaft should be
from 0.45 to 1.13 N-m (4 to 10 in-lbs).
If torque is above or below specified, adjust
worm bearing preload by loosening or tightening
the adjuster plug as needed.

### NOTE: If preload is incorrect, the adjuster plug

may have turned when the locknut was installed
or tightened. Or the gear may be assembled
incorrectly, or the wormshaft thrust bearings and
races may be worn or damaged. Check and
correct as necessary before proceeding.

### If turning torque is within specifications, remove

the socket and torque wrench.
Record the worm bearing preload torque
reading and proceed to Pitman Shaft
Overcenter Drag Torque.
Pitman Shaft Overcenter Drag Torque
Turn the pitman shaft adjuster screw
counterclockwise until fully extended; Then turn
it back 1/2 turn clockwise.

### Center the gear. Rotate the stub shaft from stop-

to-stop and count the total number of turns.
Then turn the shaft back (from either stop) 1/2
the total number of turns.
G-94
STEERING AND FRONT AXLE
POWER STEERING GEAR
NOTE: When the gear is centered, the flat on
the stub shaft (17) should face upward and be
parallel with the side cover (9). The master
spline (P) on the pitman shaft (6) should be
aligned with the adjuster screw (7).

### Reinstall the 12-point socket and torque wrench

on the stub shaft. Place the torque wrench in a
vertical position to take the reading.
Rotate the torque wrench 45° left and right of
center and record the highest drag torque
measured on or near center (R).

### 84807A

Overcenter drag torque should be as follows:
* On new steering gears, drag torque should
equal worm bearing preload plus an additional
0.45 to 0.90 N-m (4 to 8 in-lbs). However, the
combined torque (preload plus drag torque)
must not exceed 2 N-m (18 in-lbs) torque.
• On used steering gears (400 or more miles),
drag torque should equal worm bearing
preload plus an additional 0.5-0.6 N-m (4-5
in-lbs). However, the combined torque
(preload plus drag torque) must not exceed 2

### N-m (14 in-lbs).

If drag torque must be adjusted, turn the pitman
shaft adjusting screw (7) clockwise or
counterclockwise until desired drag torque is

### Operation procedure.

Fluid Level and Initial Operation
Fill the pump reservoir.
Operate the engine until the system fluid
reaches normal operating temperature of
approximately 170°F (77°C).
Turn the wheels to a full left turn position and
stop the engine.

### Add power steering fluid to the COLD mark on

the dipstick.
Start and operate the engine at curb idle speed.
Recheck fluid level. Add fluid, if necessary, to
the COLD mark on the dipstick.
Bleed the system by turning the wheels from
side-to-side without hitting the stops. Fluid with
air in it will have a milky appearance. Continue
turning the wheels side-to-side until all air is bled
from the system.

### Return the wheels to center. Operate the engine

for an additional 2-3 minutes and stop the
engine.
Road test the vehicle to verify that the steering
system functions normally.
Check fluid level. Add fluid as required to raise
level to the HOT mark on the dipstick after the
system has stabilized at normal operating
temperature.

POWER STEERING PUMP
LEAK liSPECTiOi AND DIAGNOSIS
Raise and support the vehicle and wipe the
leakage area dry.
Check for an overfilled reservoir. If overfull, drain
fluid from the reservoir with a suction gun.

### Check for aerated fluid (full of bubbles and milky

in color). Aerated fluid can cause an overflow
from the reservoir and be mistaken for a leak.
Check and tighten all hose connections and
union fittings at the pump and gear.
Start the engine. Have a helper turn the steering
wheel to the left and right several times while
locating the exact source of the leak. Contact
stops in each direction. Stop the engine when a
leak source is determined.

### HYDRAULIC PRESSURE TEST

Check and adjust pump belt tension if
necessary.
Position a drip pan under the pump and
disconnect the power steering pump pressure
hose at the pump or steering gear.
Connect the pump and steering gear to test
gauge J 21567. Use adapter J 5176-5 to
complete hose connection if necessary.

### CAUTION: Be sure the gauge pressure hose is

connected to the pressure circuit between the
pump and gear as shown.
21567
84809A
Open the test gauge valve completely. Turn the
valve counterclockwise to open.
Add fluid to the pump reservoir if necessary.

### Operate the engine until the system fluid

reaches normal operating temperature.
Note initial pressure with the gauge valve open.
Pressure should be 552-862 kPa (80-125 psi). If
initial pressure is 1 379 kPa (200 psi) or higher,
check the hoses for restrictions.

### CAUTION: During the following test step, do not

hold the gauge valve closed for more than five
seconds at a time as pump damage could occur.
Close the test gauge valve, note pressure, then
open the valve. Repeat this procedure two more
times. Record the highest pressure reading
each time the gauge valve is closed. Do not
close the valve for more than 3-4 seconds at a
time.

If pressures are within? 584 to 8 274 kPa (11001200 psi) and the three readings do not vary by
more than 345 kPa (50 psi), the pump is
functioning within specifications.

### For example, if pressures are 7 929, 7 998,

8 067 kPa, (1150, 1160, 1170 psi), pressure
variance range is within 345 kPa (50 psi) and
pump operation is OK.
If pressures recorded are high but do not repeat
within 345 kPa (50 psi), the flow control valve (A)
is sticking.

### Remove and clean the valve (A). Remove any

burrs with crocus cloth. If the system contains
dirt, flush the system.
NOTE: The power steering system is a closed
system. Contamination of fluid in either the
pump or gear will be circulated into the other
unit. If the system is exceptionally dirty, the
pump and gear must be disassembled and
cleaned and all hoses removed and flushed.

### 8481OA

If pump pressure is OK with the gauge valve
open but low with the gauge valve closed, check
the steering gear for internal leakage as follows:
Turn the steering wheel to the left and right stops
and record highest pressure Compare the
gauge readings with maximum pump output. If
pump output cannot be repeated at either side of
the gear, the steering gear is leaking internally
and must be repaired.

Connect the pressure hose to the pump (or
gear).
Make the necessary repairs and correct the fluid
level.
Remove the drip pan.

scoring or any other type of damage. However, a
high polish on the rotor pressure plate and thrust
plate is normal.

### Inspect all the rotor vanes for free movement in

the rotor slots.

Differential Cleaning and Inspection
Clean all of the parts in solvent. Allow the
bearings to air dry. Dry the other differential
parts with compressed air.

### Inspect the bearings and cups for pitting, galling,

flat spots, or cracks. Replace any bearing or cup
exhibiting these conditions.

Inspect the differential case. Replace the case if
cracked, or the pinion shaft bore is elongated or
enlarged or the machined thrust washer surface
areas and counterbores are damaged. Also
replace the case if the ring gear mounting
surface is distorted or damaged.

### Inspect the pinion mate shaft for excessive

wear, scoring, or galling. The shaft must be
smooth and concentric. Replace the shaft if
worn or damaged.
Inspect the pinion gear, ring gear, side gears
and pinions. All gear teeth should exhibit a
uniform contact pattern. Replace any of the
gears if cracked, scored, excessively worn, or
chipped.

### NOTE: If either the ring gear or pinion gear is

damaged, replace both gears as a set only.
Inspect the thrust washers for wear, or damage.
Replace the thrust washers in sets if damaged.
Inspect the pinion mate shaft lockpin. Replace
the pin if damaged in any way.

### Inspect the bearing shims. Replace the shims if

damaged in any way.
Service and Adjustment Information
The ring gear and pinion gear are serviced as a
matched set only. They are identified as a
matched set by numbers etched on the two
gears.
The first two numbers (A) on each gear identify
them as a matched set. The second number (B)
on the pinion gear is the pinion depth variance. It
indicates the amount (in thousandths of an inch)
that the set varied from the standard setting of
2.250 inches (57.1 mm). The variance may be a
plus or minus figure.

gear depth. The chart helps determine startei

measurement.
NOTE: The chart will only help determine startei
shim thickness. It will not provide the exact shirr
thickness needed for final depth adjustment.

• Subtract desired depth from initial depth. This

### NOTE: Refer to the following example for

an illustration of how the shim thickness
computation is performed.
Example - Pinion Depth Variance is Plus (4-)
0.004.
Step 1 - Determine desired pinion depth.
Add depth variance (marked on pinion gear) to
the standard setting. Result is desired pinion
depth.
• standard setting - 57.1 mm (2.250 in)
• pinion depth variance - +0.10 mm ( + 0.004
in)
• desired pinion depth equals - 57.2 mm
(2.254 in)

### Step 2 - Determine initial pinion depth.

Add measured pinion depth to starter shim
thickness. Result is initial pinion depth.
• measured pinion depth - 56.6 mm (2.224 in)
• starter shim thickness - +2.71 mm ( + 0.017
in)
• initial pinion depth equals-59.2 mm (2.331 in)

### Step 3 - Determine correct shim thickness.

Subtract desired depth from initial depth. Result
is correct shim thickness.
• total measured pinion depth - 59.2 mm
(2.331 in)
• desired pinion depth - 57.2 mm (2.254 in)
• correct shim thickness equals - 1.96 mm
(0.077 in)

PROPELLER SHAFT
DESCRIPTION
The front propeller shaft has single cardan
universal joints (A-B) at each end. A slip yoke
(C) connects the shaft to the front axle yoke.
101515

### Propeller Shaft Lubrication

The shaft universal joints and the slip yoke are
equipped with zerk-type lubrication fittings. The
slip yoke and joints should be lubricated at
periodic intervals with chassis grease.
Driveline Vibration

### Driveline vibration may be caused by a loose,

worn, or damaged propeller shaft, axle yoke, or
universal joint. Driveline vibration may also be
the result of a loose or damaged engine/
transmission mount, engine driven accessory,
or damaged wheels/tires.

### Vibration caused by a propeller shaft may be the

result of:
• undercoating on the shaft tube
• missing shaft balance weight
• excessive shaft runout
• worn or damaged propeller shaft yokes or
universal joints
• broken seam welds at either end of the shaft
• dents or bends in the shaft

### Vibration caused by a yoke may be the result of:

• excessive yoke runout
• loose U-joint clamp bolts or loose pinion nut
• damaged yoke
An incorrect universal joint angle can produce
an out-of-phase condition and cause vibration at
low or high speed.

### PROPELLER SHAFT RUNOUT

Measure propeller shaft runout at the center and
both ends of the shaft with a dial indicator.
The dial indicator should be installed
perpendicular to the shaft surface and be rigidly
mounted for accurate readings.

### Remove all dirt and undercoating from the areas

where the dial indicator stylus will contact the
shaft.
SEE
I.S.
N
O
T
E
S
G-133
STEERING AND FRONT AXLE
PROPELLER SHAFT
Take the front reading 0.13 mm (1/2 inch) from
the slip yoke splines.
Take the rear reading 0.13 mm (1/2 inch) from
the rear yoke weld joint.

### Take the center reading as close to the shaft

mid-point as possible.
Runout should not exceed 0.38 mm (0.015 in) at
any point.

Shift the transmission into Neutral.

NOTE: The inclinometer frame must face the
same direction for both readings.

### The difference in readings is the front angle.

Repeat the procedure at the transfer case end of
the shaft to obtain the rear angle.
Compare the front and rear angles. The
difference between them represents the
universal joint angle.

VACUUM CONTROL SYSTEi
The front axle shift motor disconnects the rightfront axle shaft for two-wheel drive operation.
The shift motor is vacuum operated.

### The shift motor is mounted in the motor housing

located on the right-front axle tube.
The vacuum control system consists of:
• The axle mounted shift motor (A).
• The control switch (B) on the transfer case.
• The four-wheel drive indicator switch (C).
• An air vent filter (D).
• Two check valves (E).
B

### 84856A

f ACUUM SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS
Diagnosis procedures for the vacuum system
are outlined in diagnosis charts in Chapter D -
Gearboxes. Refer to the Transfer Case section
in this chapter. However, shift motor function
testing is outlined in the following procedure.

### SHIFT MOTOR FUNCTION TEST

Disconnect the vacuum harness from the shift
motor (A).
Connect a hand operated vacuum pump to the
shift motor front port (B).
Apply 51 kPa (15 in. Hg.) to the motor through
port (B) and rotate the right-front wheel to
disengage the axle shaft.

### The shift motor should maintain applied vacuum

for a minimum of 30 seconds. Replace the motor
if it does not hold vacuum for the specified time.
101516
G-136
STEERING AND FRONT AXLE
FRONT AXLE SHIFT MOTOR
Disconnect the vacuum pump from port (B) and
connect the pump to port (C).

### Block off the shift motor-to-transfer case port (D)

with a rubber vacuum cap.
Apply 51 kPa (15 in. Hg.) to the motor through
port (C). Replace the motor if it will not hold
vacuum for a minimum of 30 seconds.
Maintain vacuum to port (C).
Remove the rubber cap blocking off port (D) and
check for vacuum at port (D). If vacuum is
present, the motor is OK. If vacuum is not
present, proceed to next step.

### Maintain vacuum to port (C). Rotate the right

front wheel as necessary to be sure the axle has
shifted into four-wheel drive.
NOTE: The axle must be completely engaged in
four-wheel drive mode in order to open port (C)
to vacuum.
Check for vacuum at port (D) again. If vacuum is
now present at port (D), the shift motor is OK. If
vacuum is still not present at port (D), replace
the shift motor.

### SHIFT MOTOR AND HOUSING REMOVAL

Raise and support the vehicle. Position a drain
pan under the shift motor housing (A).
Disconnect the vacuum harness from the motor.
Remove the housing attaching bolts and
remove the housing (A) and motor (B).
101508

### Mark the shift fork and housing for assembly

reference.
Rotate the shift motor and remove the shift fork
and motor snap rings.
Remove the shift motor (2) from the housing
and remove the O-ring (1) from the motor (2).
Discard the O-ring.

WHEELS AND TIRES
THE REPAIR
Punctured tires should be removed from the
wheel and permanently repaired from the inside
with a combination repair plug and vulcanized
patch. When repairing punctures, always follow
the manufacturers repair kit instructions.

### Only punctures in the tread area (1) are

repairable.
84860
Never attempt to repair punctures in the tire
shoulders or sidewalls. In addition, do not repair any tire that has sustained the following
damage.
• bulges or blisters
• ply separation
• broken or cracked beads
• fabric cracks or cuts
tires worn to the fabric, or if wear indicators are
visible
• punctures larger than 6.35 mm (1/4 in) in
diameter

### TIRE ROTATION

To equalize tire wear, it is recommended that the
tires be rotated every 8 046 km (5,000 mi). The
first rotation is by far the most important in
setting the stage for long, even tread wear.
Earlier and more frequent rotations may be
desirable under certain conditions.

### After rotation, adjust inflation pressures to

recommended levels.
Radial tires are rotated on the same side frontto-rear and rear-to-front (2).
84861A

COMPACT SPARE TIRE
WARNING. The compact spare tire is designed
for emergency temporary use only. Do not
exceed 80 km/h (50 mph) or travel more than 80
continuous km (50 mi) with the compact spare
installed. This is especially important if the
vehicle is equipped with a Trac-Lok rear axle.

### The compact spare tire is air-inflated with

standard inflation equipment. Recommended
inflation pressure is 414 kPa (60 psi).
The compact spare tire has a tread life of
approximately 4 828 km (3,000 mi) under
normal use. Do not attempt to install standard
size tires on the special wheel used with the
compact spare.

### WARNING: To guard against bodily injury, use

caution when inflating or adding air to the
compact spare. Use a 689 kPa (100 psi)
capacity pressure gauge to check pressure and
inflate the tire to a maximum of 414 kPa (60 psi)
only. When inflating the tire, add air only in very
small amounts.

### WHEEL AND TIRE RUNOUT

Measure runout with a dial indicator. All
measurements should be made on the vehicle
with the tires inflated to recommended inflation
pressures.
Measure tire radial runout at the center and
outside ribs of the tread face (1). Measure lateral
runout just above the buffing rib on the sidewall
(2).
84862

### Mark the high points of lateral and radial runout

for reference.
On conventional tires, radial runout should not
exceed 2.66 mm (0.105 in). Lateral runout
should not exceed 2.54 mm (0.100 in).
G-140
STEERING AND FRONT A X L E
WHEEL AND TIRES
On radial tires, radial runout should not exceed
2.03 mm (0.080 in). Lateral runout should not
exceed 2.54 mm (0.100 in).

### If the total radial or lateral runout of the tire

exceeds specified limits, check wheel runout to
determine if the wheel or tire is at fault.
Wheel radial runout is measured at the wheel
rim just inside of the wheel cover retaining nibs
(1).
Wheel lateral runout is measured at the wheel
rim bead flange just inside of the curved lip of the
flange (2).

### 100657A

Wheel radial runout should not exceed 0.89 mm
(0.035 in). Wheel lateral runout should not
exceed 1.14mm (0.045 in). Mark the high points
of radial and lateral runout.
If tire runout (either lateral or radial) exceeds
specified limits but wheel runout is within limits, it
may be possible to reduce runout to an
acceptable level. This is accomplished by
changing tire position on the wheel so that the
previously marked high points are 180° apart.

### FRONT WHEEL SHIiiY

Front wheel shimmy may be caused by one of
the following conditions:
• loose front wheel bearings
• worn, out of round or unbalanced front tires
• loose or damaged steering damper
• worn or loose tie rod ends
• worn, loose or damaged steering knuckle ball
studs
w incorrect front wheel alignment
• incorrect or uneven tire pressures

### Check all of the above items when diagnosing a

shimmy condition. Repair or replace components as necessary.

Differential Removal
Raise the vehicle.

lubricant.

propeller shaft.

### NOTE: If the pinion gear, bearings or seal are to

be serviced, measure and record pinion preload

section or Pinion Seal Replacement procedure.
Remove the wheels and brake drums.

### H-11

REAR AXLE
GENERAL SERVICE PROCEDURES
Loosen the bearing cap bolts until only two or
three bolt threads are engaged.
Install spreader tool J 24385-01 on the axle
housing.
Mount djal indicator J 8001 on the housing.

### Position the indicator stylus so it contacts one

side of the differential opening in the housing.
Spread the housing only enough to remove the
differential. This should only require about 0.12
mm (0.005 inch). Measure the amount the housing is spread with the dial indicator.

### CAUTION: Do not spread the housing any more

than 0.38 mm (0.015 inch). Overspreading may
distort or damage the housing.
Remove the dial indicator and differential bearing caps. Tag the caps for assembly reference.
Remove the differential assembly. If the differential is still a fairly snug fit, use a pry bar
to ease the differential out of the bearing
saddles.

### Remove the spreader tool and clamps im-

mediately after removing the differential. This
is important in avoiding the possibility of the
housing taking a set.
Remove the pinion gear, bearings and seal if
they are to be serviced.
Differential Installation

### Install the pinion gear, bearings and seal if re-

moved. Adjust pinion gear depth if required.
Refer to the procedure outlined in the overhaul
sections.
Spread the axle housing no more than 0.38 mm
(0.015 inch) with tool J 24385-01
Start the differential bearing cups in the axle
housing bearing saddles.

### Tap the outer edges of the differential bearing

cups with a rawhide mallet to seat them in the
axle housing.
Remove the axle housing spreader tool.
Install the differential bearing caps. Tighten the
cap bolts to 77 l\hm (57 ft-lbs) torque.
Check and adjust ring gear backlash if
necessary.

### NOTE: If the pinion gear, bearings or seal were

serviced, adjust pinion preload as outlined in
the Differential Overhaul section or in the Pinion
Seal Replacement procedure.
Align and connect the propeller shaft. Tighten
the U-joint clamp bolts to 19 NеН (170 in-lbs)
torque.

### Install the axle housing cover. Tighten the cover

bolts to 19 N«m (170 in-lbs) torque.
Fill the axle with 1.2 liters (2.5 pints) of JEEP
axle lubricant or an equivalent SAE 75W-90,
API Grade GL 5 gear lubricant.
Install the brake drums and wheels. Tighten the
wheel nuts to 102 NеН (75 ft-lbs) torque.

REAR AXLE ASSEMBLY REMOVAL/INSTALLATION
REAR AXLE ASSEMBLY REMOVAL
Raise the vehicle.
Position safety stands under the frame rails.
Place the stands even with, or slightly ahead of
the rear spring front eyes.

### Remove the rear wheels.

Mark the rear propeller shaft and axle yokes for
assembly reference.
Disconnect the propeller shaft from the axle
yoke.
Disconnect the track bar at the axle bracket and
the axle vent tube at the axle.

### Disconnect the parking brake cables from the

equalizer.
Disconnect the shock absorbers from the axle
brackets.
Disconnect the brake hose from the fitting on
the floorpan. Cap the hose end to prevent dirt
entry.
Remove the spring U-bolts and tie plates.

### Loosen, but do not remove, the bolts that at-

tach the spring eyes to the frame brackets and
rear shackles.
Support the axle with a hydraulic jack.
Raise the axle just enough to relieve axle
weight from the springs.

and slide the axle into position under the
vehicle.

the U-joint clamp bolts to 19 N*m (170 in-lbs)

necessary.
Install the wheels.

Remove supports and lower the vehicle.

### Cleaning and Inspection

Clean all of the differential components in solvent. Use compressed air to dry all parts except
the bearings. Dry the bearings with shop towels
only.
Examine each component for wear or damage.
Inspect the bearings and bearing cups. Replace
bearings and races as a set if either part is
galled, worn, cracked, flat spotted or scored.

### Inspect the differential side and pinion gears.

Replace any gear that is worn, cracked,
chipped or broken.
Inspect the ring and pinion gears. Replace the
gears as a set if either is worn or damaged.
Inspect the differential case. Replace the case if
cracked or damaged.

### Service and Adjustment Information

Pinion gear depth must be measured and adjusted before installing the differential in the axle housing. Depth is controlled by a shim (14)
installed between the pinion rear bearing cup
(13) and the axle housing (A).
A

### 84128A

The ring gear (10) and pinion gear (11) are serviced as a matched set only. They are identified
as a matched set by numbers etched on the
ring and pinion gears.
The first two numbers (A) on each gear identify
them as a matched set. The second number (B)
on the pinion gear is the pinion depth variance.

### It indicates the amount (in thousandths of an

inch) that the set varied from the standard setting of 2.095 inches (53.21 mm). The variance
may be a plus or minus figure.
mi
REAR AXLE
STANDARD DIFFERENTIAL OVERHAUL
84129
Service replacement ring and pinion gear sets
are machined to the standard setting only. Pinion depth variance on replacement sets will
range from plus to minus 0.004 inch'*. (0.10
mm). Any service replacement set with a variance exceeding these figures, or a set with mismatched identification numbers must not be
used. These gear sets should be returned to the
parts distribution center.

### NOTE: Some factory installed gear sets may

have an extra 0.010 or 0.020 inch (0.25 or 0.50
mm) milled off the pinion. These sets have a
unique variance number. For example, if the
number on the pinion is 23, the number 2 indicates 0.020 inch (0.50 mm) was milled off the
pinion and the variance is 0.003 inches (0.076
mm). Similarily, if the variance number is 16, the
number 1 indicates 0.010 inch (0.25 mm) was
milled off the pinion and variance is 0.006 inch
(0.15 mm).

thickness
needed
for
initial
depth
measurement.
NOTE: The chart will only help determine starter
shim thickness. It will not provide the exact
shim thickness required for final depth
adjustment.

### Pinion Bearing Preload Adjustment

A collapsible spacer (15) controls preload which
is adjusted at the pinion nut (20). The spacer is
designed to crush and hold at the set preload.
Correct preload is 2-3 N«m (15-25 in-lbs).
Preload is measured as the amount of torque
required to turn the pinion gear with an inchpound torque wrench.
84134

### Install a replacement pinion nut (20) on the pi-

nion gear. Tighten the nut only enough to remove end play. Do not overtighten the nut.
Place a socket and inch-pound torque wrench J
5853-B on the pinion nut and begin rotating the
pinion gear.
Slowly tighten the pinion nut until torque required to rotate the pinion gear is between 2-3

### N*m (15-25 in-lbs). Check torque frequently and

tighten the nut in very small amounts only.
CAUTION: The preload spacer is designed to
permanently crush and hold at whatever
preload is set. If specified preload is exceeded,
do not attempt correction by loosening and retightening the pinion nut. The spacer must be
replaced and preload reset.

### Position the indicator stylus against the drive

side of one of the ring gear teeth. Be sure the
stylus is at a right angle to the tooth.
Move the ring gear forward and zero the dial
indicator.
Move the ring gear rearward then forward and
note the dial indicator reading.

### Correct backlash is between 0.13 and 0.23 mm

(0.005 and 0.009 in). However, the optimum
backlash setting is 0.20 mm (0.008 in).
Record the dial indicator reading and remove
indicator set J 8001.
Remove the differential assembly from the axle
housing.

### Remove the differential bearings and end play

shims. Do not intermix the shims. Tag them for
reference if necessary.
If backlash is within specified tolerance, proceed to Differential Bearing Preload
Adjustment.
If backlash is not within specified tolerance, adjust backlash as follows:
# To increase backlash, use a thinner shim
pack on the ring gear side of the case. To do
this, subtract the amount needed from the
ring gear shim pack. Then add the same
amount to the opposite shim pack.
# To decrease backlash, use a thicker shim
pack on the ring gear side of the case. To do
this, add the amount needed to the ring gear
shim pack. Then subtract the same amount
from the opposite shim pack.

### NOTE: The total (or combined) thickness of

both shim packs does not change. The amount
required for desired backlash is simply transferred from one side to the other as needed.
For example, if measured backlash is 0.28 mm
(0.011 in) and the optimum setting of 0.20 mm
(0.008 in) is desired, backlash must be decreased by 0.076 mm (0.003 in). To do this, add
0.076 mm (0.003 in) to the ring gear shim pack
and subtract the same amount from the opposite shim pack.

### Assemble the neccessary shim packs and pro-

ceed to Differential Bearing Preload Adjustment. Do not install the bearings at this time.

Service and Adjustment Information
The clutch packs are serviced as sets only. If
one clutch pack is damaged, both clutch packs
must be replaced.
Pinion gear depth must be measured and adjusted before installing the differential in the axle housing. Depth is controlled by a shim (17)
installed under the pinion rear bearing cup (16).

### 84128B

The ring gear (13) and pinion gear (14) are serviced as a matched set only. They are identified
as a matched set by numbers etched on the
ring and pinion gears.
The first two numbers (A) on each gear identify
them as a matched set. The second number (B)
on the pinion gear is the pinion depth variance.

### It indicates the amount (in thousandths of an

inch) that the set varied from the standard setting of 2.095 inches (53.21 mm). The variance
may be a plus or minus figure.

Service replacement ring and pinion gear sets
are machined to the standard setting only. Pinion depth variance on replacement sets will
range from plus to minus 0.004 inches (0.10
mm). Any service replacement set with a variance exceeding these figures, or a set with mismatched identification numbers must not be
used. Such gear sets should be returned to the
parts distribution center.

starter shim thickness.

The intersecting figure represents the plus or

intersecting figure is +0.004 inch (0.10 mm).

the old pinion is -3 and the new pinion is -2,
the intersecting figure is -0.001 inch (0.025

### Determine desired pinion depth as follows:

• Record depth variance marked on the pinion
gear.
• If the variance is a plus figure, add the variance to the standard setting of 2.095 inches
(53.21 mm). If the variance is a minus figure,
subtract it from the standard setting.
• Record the desired depth figure for final
shim selection.

Mount gauge block clamp J 5223-14 and holding screw J 5223-24 on the axle housing. Secure the clamp to the housing with an axle cover bolt. Position the holding screw over the
gauge block.

### Then loosen the holding screw and remove the

Measure the distance between the anvil (A) and

selection. It represents the initial pinion depth.

### Select the required pinion depth shim as

follows:
• Subtract pinion variance from standard setting. This equals desired depth.
• Add starter shim thickness to existing depth.
This equals total depth.
• Subtract desired depth from total depth. This
equals required shim thickness.

Pinion Bearing Preload Adjustment
A collapsible spacer (18) controls preload which
is adjusted at the pinion nut (23). The spacer is
designed to crush and hold at the set preload.

### Correct preload is 2-3 N«m (15-25 in-lbs).

Preload is measured as the amount of torque
required to turn the pinion gear with an inchpound torque wrench.
84134B
Install a replacement pinion nut (23) on the pinion gear. Tighten the nut only enough to remove end play. Do not overtighten the nut.

### Place a socket and inch-pound torque wrench J

5853-B on the pinion nut and begin rotating the
pinion gear.
Slowly tighten the pinion nut until torque required to rotate the pinion is between 2-3 N«m
(15-25 in-lbs). Check torque frequently and
tighten the nut in very small amounts only.

### CAUTION: The preload spacer is designed to

permanently crush and hold at whatever
preload is set. If specified preload is exceeded,
do not attempt correction by loosening and retightening the pinion nut. The spacer must be
replaced and preload reset again.

### Remove the inch pound torque wrench and

socket.
Proceed to the Differential Case Runout Check.
NOTE: Do not assemble the differential until
case runout and bearing end play have been
checked and adjusted.

### Ring Gear Backlash Adjustment

NOTE: Ring gear backlash establishes the running clearance between the ring and pinion
gears. Adjustment involves moving the ring
gear toward or away from the pinion. Adjustment is controlled by the differential bearing
end play shims.

Correct backlash is between 0.13 and 0.23 mm

### Differential

Bearing
Preload
Adjustment.
If backlash is not within specified tolerance, adjust backlash as follows:
• To increase backlash, use a thinner shim
pack on the ring gear side of the case. To do
this, subtract the amount needed from the
ring gear shim pack. Then add the same
amount to the opposite shim pack.
• To decrease backlash, use a thicker shim
pack on the ring gear side of the case. To do
this, add the amount needed to the ring gear
shim pack. Then subtract the same amount
from the opposite shim pack.

### Assemble the neccessary shim packs and pro-

ceed to Differential Bearing Preload Adjustment. Do not install the bearings at this time.

GENERAL INFORMATION
The rear propeller shaft is a tubular steel unit
with welded yokes. Single cardan U-joints (A)
are used at the front and rear. A slip yoke (B) is
used to connect the shaft to the transfer case.
101332

### PROPELLER SHAFT REMOVAL

Raise the vehicle.
Mark the propeller shaft and axle yokes for
alignment reference.
Remove the U-joint clamp strap bolts and disconnect the shaft from the axle yoke. Discard
the U-joint clamps. They are not reusable.

### Slide the slip yoke out of the transfer case and

remove the propeller shaft.
PROPELLER SHAFT INSTALLATION
Install the propeller shaft slip yoke on the transfer case output shaft.
Align and install the propeHer shaft rear U-joint
in the axle yoke.
Secure the rear U-joint to the yoke with replacement clamps.

### Tighten the clamp bolts to 19 Mm (170 in4bs)

torque.
Lower the vehicle.

press.

cap to be removed. Position the small socket
(B) against the opposite bearing cap. Then
tighten the vise to press the cap partially out of
the yoke.

DRIVELINE VIBRATION
Driveline vibration can be caused by damage to
the propeller shaft, universal joints or the axle
and transfer case yokes.
Propeller Shaft
Inspect the shaft for dents, missing balance
weights, cracked weld seams or yokes, undercoating on the shaft tube and excessive
runout.

### Universal Joints

Inspect the joints for loose clamp bolts, worn
bearings, damaged bearing cap retainers, or
damaged clamps.
Axle and Transfer Case Yokes
Inspect the yokes for damaged bearing cap
bores. Check the pinion yoke for excessive runout or or a loose pinion nut. Check the slip
yoke splines and seal surface for damage.

### NOTE: Driveline vibration may also be the result

of loose or damaged engine mounts or engine
operated accessories. In addition, loose or
damaged crossmembers, support cushions or
driveline mounting bolts/nuts can also contribute to vibration.

A leaf spring suspension system with dual action shock absorbers is used on Wrangler/YJ
models.

### Front Suspension

Two leaf springs and dual action shock absorbers are used in the front suspension. A track
bar and stabilizer bar complete the front suspension components.
Rear Suspension
Two leaf springs and dual action shock absorbers are used in the rear suspension. A track bar
forms the remainder of the rear suspension
components.

### Track Bars

The front and rear track bars are attached to
brackets on the axle and frame rail. The track
bars maintain lateral positioning of the front and
rear axles.
Front Stabilizer Bar
A stabilizer bar is used only at the front suspension on Wrangler/YJ models. Rubber bushings
are used at the bar attaching points on the
frame rails and front axle.

### Shock Absorbers

Dual action, telescopic shock absorbers are
used to control front and rear leaf spring action.
One shock absorber is used for each spring.
Rubber bushings and grommets are used at all
shock absorber mounting points.

Remove the bolt that attaches the spring rear
eye to the frame bracket.

### Remove the spring.

Front Spring Installation
Position the spring in the frame bracket and
front shackle.
Install, but do not tighten the bolts that attach
the spring to the frame bracket and front
shackle.
Align the front spring center bolt with the locating hole in the front axle.

### Lower the front axle until it it fully supported by

the spring.
NOTE: Be sure the spring center bolt is seated
in the axle locating hole. Realign the center bolt
and locating hole if necessary.
Install the tie plate (D), U-bolts (C) and U-bolt
nuts (B).

### Tighten the U-bolt nuts to 122 N*m (90 ft-lbs)

torque.
Tighten the stabilizer bar link nut (A) to 61 N®m
(45 ft-lbs) torque.
Install the wheels. Tighten the wheel nuts to 102
N«m (75 ft-lbs) torque.
Remove all supports and lower the vehicle.
Tighten the front shackle bolt (E) to 129 N*m (95
ft-lbs) torque.

### Tighten the spring rear eye-to-frame bracket

bolt to 142 N*m (105 ft-lbs) torque.
REAR SPRINGS
Rear Spring Removal
Raise the vehicle.
J-7
SUSPENSION
SUSPENSION COMPONENT SERVICE
Remove one or both rear wheels as necessary.
Raise the rear axle enough to relieve the rear
springs of axle weight.

### Disconnect the rear shock at the axle bracket.

Remove the U-bolt nuts (1) and remove the Ubolts (2) and the spring tie plate (3).
Remove the bolts attaching the rear spring (4)
to the shackle and frame bracket.
Remove the spring.
1
101299
Rear Spring Installation

### Position the spring in the shackle and frame

bracket.
Install but do not tighten the bolts that attach
the spring to the shackle and frame bracket.
Align the rear spring center bolt with the locating hole in the rear axle.
Lower the rear axle until it it fully supported by
the spring.

### NOTE: Be sure the spring center bolt is seated

in the axle locating hole. Realign the center bolt
and locating hole if necessary.
Install the tie plate (3), U-bolts (2) and U-bolt
nuts (1).
Tighten the U-bolt nuts to 122 N*m (90 ft-lbs)
torque.
Connect the shock absorber to the axle bracket. Tighten the shock retaining nut to 60 N-m (44
ft-lbs) torque.

### Install the wheels. Tighten the wheel nuts to 102

N«m (75 ft-lbs) torque.
Remove all supports and lower the vehicle.
Tighten the rear spring shackle bolt to 129 N«m
(95 ft-lbs) torque.
Tighten the rear spring eye-to-frame bracket
bolt to 142 N*m (105 ft-lbs) torque.

### SPRING BUSHING REPLACEMENT

The front and rear spring eye bushings are serviceable components.
Special tools are not required to remove or install the bushings. Once the spring is removed,
the bushings can be replaced using an arbor
press and a suitable size socket and length of
pipe as bushing drivers.

Brake system diagnosis procedures are outlined in the diagnosis guides and charts.

### Diagnosis Guides

The procedures in Diagnosis Guides A and B
are the beginning diagnostic steps. Use them to
determine if a malfunction is related to the
mechanical/hydraulic portion of the system, or
to the vacuum brake booster portion of the
system.

### Guide A checks the mechanical/hydraulic por

tion of the system. Guide B checks the vacuun
booster portion of the system. Both guides are
used in conjunction with a road test.
Diagnosis Charts

### BRAKE SYSTEM

DIAGNOSIS
A. LOW BRAKE PEDAL — (Excessive pedal travel required f o r braking action.)
POSSIBLE CAUSES
(1) Worn pads or brakelining.
(2) Worn rotors or drums.
(3) Rear brake adjustment incorrect.
(4) Caliper pistons not retracting.

### CORRECTION

(1) Inspect and replace pads and lining if
beyond minimum thickness
specification.
(2) Replace if worn beyond specifications.
(3) Make 10 to 15 alternate forward and
reverse brake stops to adjust brakes. If
brake pedal does not come up, repair or
replace rear brake parts as necessary.
(4) Replace worn rotor or pads. Overhaul
caliper if piston is sticking or seal
leakage has occurred.
B. LOW BRAKE PEDAL — (Pedal may go to fioor with steady pressure applied.)

### POSSIBLE CAUSES

(1) Low fluid level or fluid leak in hydraulic
system.
(2) Air in hydraulic system.
(3) Sub-standard brake fluid (fluid boils off at
normal brake operating temperatures).
(4) Master cylinder piston seals worn, or
master cylinder bore is scored, worn or
corroded.

### CORRECTION

(1) Fill master cylinder. Have helper apply
brakes and check calipers, wheel
cylinders, differential valve tubes, hoses
and fittings for leaks. Repair or replace
as necessary.
(2) Bleed the brakes.
(3) Flush hydraulic system. Refill with correct
fluid.
(4) Repair or replace master cylinder.
C. LOW BRAKE PEDAL — (Pedal low on first application — O.K. on subsequent applications.)

### POSSIBLE CAUSES

(1) Low fluid level.
(2) Disc brake pads sticking on abutment
surfaces of anchor plate. Caused by a
build-up of dirt, rust, or corrosion on
abutment surfaces.
CORRECTION
(1) Add fluid. Check for leaks.
(2) Clean abutment surfaces.

POSSIBLE CAUSES

(2) Master cylinder caliper, or wheel cylinder

### CORRECTION

(1) Fill master cylinder reservoirs. Have
helper apply brakes, check calipers,
wheel cylinders, differential valve, tubes,
hoses, and fittings for fluid leaks. Repair
or replace parts as necessary.
(2) Repair or replace as necessary.

### BRAKE SYSTEM

DIAGNOSIS
E. DECREASING BRAKE PEDAL TRAVEL — (Pedal travel required for braking action decreases
and may result in hard pedal.)
POSSIBLE CAUSES
(1) Caliper or wheel cylinder pistons sticking
or seized.
(2) Master cylinder inlet ports blocked
(preventing fluid return to reservoirs) or
pistons sticking or seized in master
cylinder bore.
(3) Power brake unit malfunction.

### CORRECTION

(1) Repair or replace the calipers, or wheel
cylinders.
(2) Repair or replace the master cylinder.
(3) Test unit as follows:
(a) Shift transmission into neutral and
start engine.
(b) Increase engine speed to 1500 rpm,
close throttle and fully depress brake
pedal.
(c) Slowly release brake pedal and stop
engine.
(d) Have helper remove vacuum check
valve and hose from booster. Check
for rearward movement of brake
pedal.
(e) If the pedal moves rearward, booster
has malfunctioned — replace booster.

### 1 0 1 3 4 2 E

F. SPONGY BRAKE PEDAL — (Pedal has soft, springy, spongy feel when pressed.)
POSSIBLE CAUSES
CORRECTION
(1) Air in hydraulic system.
(1) Bleed brakes
(2) Rear brakeshoes bent or distorted.
(2) Replace brakeshoes.
(3) Rear drum brakes not properly adjusted.
(3) Adjust rear brakes.
(4) Rear drums worn beyond specification.
(4) Replace drums.
G. HARD BRAKE PEDAL - (Excessive pedal pressure required to stop vehicle. May be
accompanied by brake fade.)

### POSSIBLE CAUSES

(1) Loose or leaking booster vacuum hose.
(2) Incorrect or poor quality brakelining.
(3) Bent, broken, distorted brakeshoes.
(4) Calipers binding or dragging on
mounting pins. Rear brakeshoes
dragging on support plate.

### CORRECTION

(1) Tighten connections or replace leaking
hose.
(2) Replace lining.
(3) Replace brakeshoes.
(4) Replace mounting pins and bushings.
Clean rust or burrs from rear brake
support plate ledges and lubricate ledges
with molydisulfide grease.

### NOTE: If ledges are deeply grooved or

scored, do not attempt to sand or grind
them smooth — replace support plate.

J. VEHICLE PULLS WHEN BRAKES ARE APPLIED
POSSIBLE CAUSES
(1) Incorrect front tire pressure.
(2) Worn or damaged wheel bearings.
(3) Brakelining on one side contaminated.
(4) Brakeshoes on one side bent, distorted,
or lining loose on shoe.

(5) Tighten or replace support plate.
(6) Tighten anchor plate bolts.
(7) Repair or replace caliper.
(8) Drive vehicle with brakes lightly applied
to dry linings.
(9) Tighten suspension bolts. Replace worn
suspenson components.

assemblies.

### BRAKE SYSTEM SERVICE

SYSTEM COMPONENTS
SEE
I.S.
N
O
T
E
S
Wrangler/YJ models are equipped with power
assisted front disc and rear drum brakes. A dual reservoir master cylinder and pressure differential valve are used in the hydraulic system.

### The parking brakes are actuated by a foot-op-

erated lever assembly. A cable and equalizer
mechanism connects the lever to the rear
brakes.
Power brake assist is provided by a single diaphragm, vacuum operated brake booster. Pin
mounted, slider-type disc brake calipers are
used at the front and self adjusting drum brake
assemblies are used at the rear.

### BRAKE FLUID

Use JEEP brake fluid or an equivalent that
meets SAE standard J 1703F and is graded
DOT 3 or DOT 4. This is the only type of brake
fluid recommended for use in Wrangler/YJ
models.
BRAKE FLUID LEVEL
The correct master cylinder fluid level is to within 6 mm (1/4 in) of the reservoir rim. Use the
recommended brake fluid only and do not
overfill the reservoir.

### CAUTION: Avoid contaminating the brake fluid.

Always clean off the master cylinder and cover
before checking fluid level or filling the
reservoir.
MASTER CYLINDER REMOVAL
Disconnect the brake lines at the master cylinder. Cap the lines to prevent dirt entry.

### Remove the nuts that attach the master cylinder

to the brake booster mounting studs and remove the cylinder.
MASTER CYLINDER OVERHAUL
Remove the cylinder cover and drain the fluid
from the reservoirs.
Inspect the rubber diaphragm in the cover. Replace the diaphragm if cut, torn or damaged in
any way.

### Press the primary piston (2) inward and remove

the snap ring (2).
Remove and discard the primary piston (2).
Remove the secondary piston (5) and spring (8).
Apply air pressure through the cylinder rear
outlet port to push the piston and spring out.
2

### BRAKE SYSTEM

< U 4 §
BRAKE SYSTEM SERVICE
84035A
Remove and discard seals (3) and (4) from the
secondary piston.
Remove the rear seal (6), spring (8) and retainer
(7) from the secondary piston. Discard the seal.
Inspect the outlet port tube seats (10). Replace
the seats if loose or damaged as follows:
# Enlarge the hole in the seats with a 5 mm
(13/64 in) drill bit.
# Place a flat washer on each outlet port and
thread a 1 /4 - 20 by three quarter inch long
screw into each tube seat.

### Then remove the screw and seat.

Clean the master cylinder with brake cleaning
fluid. Dry the cylinder with compressed air. Be
sure to remove any chips generated during tube
seat replacement. Replace the cylinder if the
bore is scored, corroded or pitted.

### Coat the master cylinder bore, pistons and

seals with clean brake fluid.
Install replacement seals (3), (4) and (6) on the
secondary piston.
CAUTION: Be sure the lip of seal (3) faces forward and the lip of seal (6) faces rearward.
Install the retainer (7) and spring (8) on the secondary piston and install the piston assembly in
the cylinder.

### Install the replacement primary piston assembly

(2) and install the snap ring (1).
Bleed the master cylinder as follows:
• Mount the cylinder in a vise and fill the
reservoirs.
j Fabricate and install two bleed tubes (1) and
install them in the outlet ports.
• Slowly compress the pistons with a dowel
rod (2). Then allow the pistons to return
under normal spring pressure. Continue this
operation until air bubbles no longer appear
in the brake fluid.
• Press the replacement tube seats into the
outlet ports with a spare tube fitting.

MASTER CYLINDER INSTALLATION

### Position the master cylinder on the booster

mounting studs.
Install and tighten the cylinder attaching nuts.
Connect the brakelines to the master cylinder.
Wipe the cylinder cover clean then remove it.
Fill the cylinder reservoirs to within 6 mm (1 /4
in) of the rims and reinstall the cylinder cover.

### Check brake operation.

BRAKE BOOSTER REMOVAL
NOTE: The brake booster is serviced as an assembly only. Do not attempt to disassemble the
unit for service if a malfunction occurs.
Disconnect the push rod (1) from the brake
pedal.

### Disconnect the booster vacuum hose from the

check valve (2).
Remove the nuts attaching the master cylinder
to the booster and move the cylinder away from
the booster.
NOTE: It is not necessary to disconnect the
brakelines from the master cylinder.

### Remove the nuts (3) from the booster mounting

studs and remove the booster (5) from the
mounting bracket (4).

BRAKE BOOSTER INSTALLATION
Position the booster (5) on the mounting bracket (4) and install the mounting stud nuts (3).

### Connect the vacuum hose to the check valve

(2).
Attach the booster push rod (1) to the brake
pedal.
Install the master cylinder on the booster.
Check brake operation before moving the
vehicle.
FRONT BRAKE PAD REPLACEMENT
Brake Pad Removal
Remove two-thirds of the fluid from the master

REAR BRAKESHOE ADJUSTMENT
The rear brakeshoes must be adjusted whenever the shoes have been removed during service
operations and before adjusting the parking
brakes.
The procedure requires an initial in-shop adjustment followed by final adjustment with the
vehicle in motion.

### Initial adjustment can be performed with the

brake drums on, or off the vehicle.
Final adjustment is performed with the vehicle
in motion. It involves a series of alternating reverse and forward brake stops.
Adjustment procedures are as follows:
