Valve Service
The valve (A) is serviced as an assembly only.
It is not a repairable component and must be
replaced if a malfunction occurs.

### The valve is located on the left fender panel just

below the master cylinder.
84051
Valve Operation
The valve contains a pressure differential piston
and a plunger-type electrical switch. The valve
is connected to the front and rear brake systems. The switch is connected to the brake
warning light.

### A pressure differential of 483 to 2 068 kPa (70

to 300 psi) between the front and rear systems
will trigger piston operation.
If a fluid pressure drop occurs in the front or
rear brake system, pressure from the functioning system moves the piston to the low pressure side. The piston then closes off the low
pressure side diverting all fluid pressure to the
functioning system. The piston will remain at
the low pressure side until the malfunction is
corrected.

### The electrical switch is actuated by the differen-

tial piston. Movement of the piston in either direction will press the switch plunger upward
closing the circuit to the brake warning light.
The differential piston will reset automatically
after correcting a malfunction. Valve hold-off
tools are not required in order to bleed the
brakes.

### BRAKE BLEEDING

The brake hydraulic system must be bled when
diagnosis indicates air has entered the system.
Brake bleeding is also required whenever a
brakeline has been disconnected or a system
hydraulic component has been removed for
service.

### System contamination requires that the entire

system be flushed with clean brake fluid. Continue flushing until only clear, clean brake fluid
is bled from the calipers and wheel cylinders.
Use JEEP brake fluid or an equivalent fluid with
the SAE J 1703F or DOT 3 or 4 rating.

### The pressure differential piston is actuated by a

pressure drop in the front or rear brake system.
K-30
BRAKE SYSTEM
BRAKE SYSTEM SERVICE
—
—
Brake Bleeding Sequence
Bleed the brake system in the following sequence. Use the sequence for both pressure
and manual bleeding procedures.
• Right rear wheel cylinder.
% Left rear wheel cylinder
• Right front caliper.
• Left front caliper.

### Pressure Bleeding Procedure

Fill the bleeder tank with the specified brake
fluid and close the tank fluid supply valve.
Pressurize the bleeder tank to 103-138 kPa (1520 psi).
Open the tank fluid supply valve and bleed all
air from the tank and supply line.

### Close the fluid supply valve and repressurize

the tank.
Install the bleeder adapter cover on the master
cylinder.
Connect the tank supply line to the fitting on the
bleeder adapter cover.
Bleed only one wheel at a time and in the recommended sequence as follows:
• Open the fluid supply valve on the bleeder
tank.
# Connect a bleed hose to the wheel cylinder
or caliper bleed fitting.
# insert the end of the bleed hose in a glass
container partially filled with brake fluid. Be
sure the hose end is completely submerged
in the fluid.
# Close the bleed fitting when fluid flowing into

the glass container is clear and free of air
bubbles.

### Repeat the bleeding procedure at the remaining

wheels.
Discard the brake fluid remaining in the glass
container.
Disconnect the bleeder tank supply line and remove the adapter cover from the master
cylinder.
Top off the master cylinder reservoirs to within
6 mm (1 /4 inch) of the reservoir rims.

### Install the master cylinder cover.

Check brake operation before moving the
vehicle.
Manual Bleeding Procedure
Fill the master cylinder reservoirs with fresh
brake fluid.
Connect a bleed hose to the wheel cylinder or
caliper bleed fitting.

### Insert the end of the bleed hose in a glass

container partially filled with brake fluid. Be sure

HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
HEATING SYSTEM
GENERAL
A blend-air heating system is used in
Wrangler/YJ vehicles. The blend-air system provides a constant flow of engine coolant through
the heater core.

### The temperature of heated air entering the

passenger compartment is controlled by
regulating the quantity of air flow through the
heater core. This is accomplished by blending
a controlled amount of unheated air from outside the vehicle with heated air from the heater
core.

### HEATER AND DEFROSTER OPERATION

The heater core is connected to the engine
cooling system. It operates on the circulation
of heated engine coolant through the core and
a supply of fresh air drawn in through the intake grille on the cowl. Engine coolant flows
through the heater core at all times.

### The heater controls are on the heater control

panel (1).
101167
The air control lever (2) operates a door in the
fresh air intake duct. The door controls the
amount of fresh air flow into the heater housing and core. When the lever is in the Off position, the intake door is closed preventing air
flow into the housing.

### The temperature control lever (3) determines air

flow through the heater core. The lever operates
the heater housing blend-air door which controls air flow through the core.
The blower motor is operated by the control
switch (4). The switch provides three biower
speeds for increased air flow in heat or defrost
mode.

### Heating

Maximum air flow and heater output occurs
when the air control lever (2) is in Heat position and the temperature control lever (3) in
Warm position. The blend-air door is closed and
all intake air is directed through the core in this
operating mode.

### Temperature regulation of the heated air is

determined by position of the temperature control lever (3). Moving the control lever from Warm
to an in-between position, opens the blend-air
door in the heater housing. As the door opens,
unheated outside air is drawn into the system
and blended with heated air from the core.

### Defrosting

The heater housing contains a defroster door
to divert heated air to the defroster duct and
windshield outlets. Defrost air flow is controlled by the air control lever (2).
For defroster operation, the air control lever (2)
must be moved to the defrost detent. The detent is identified by the defrost symbol on the
control panel. In this position, the defroster
door in the heater housing diverts all heated air
(from the core) to the defroster duct windshield
outlets.
•4

### HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING

HEATING SYSTEM
NOTE: if the air control lever (2) is moved to any
position between the heat and defrost detents,
the defroster door does not close completely.
In this mode, the door remains partially open
causing heated air to be divided equally between the heat and defrost outlets.

### FRESH AIR VENTILATION

The fresh air ventilating system is operated by
the air control lever (2). When the lever is
moved to Vent position, outside air from the
cowl intake flows into the heater housing. Incoming air is directed into the vehicle interior
through vent doors in the housing.

### A door in the intake duct controls air flow into

the duct. The door is operated by a vacuum
motor. The motor is controlled by a vacuum
switch in the heater control panel. The vent air
doors are opened and closed by a cable and
linkage operated by the air control lever. Fresh
air intake occurs only when the lever is in the

### Vent position.

AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
GENERAL
The air conditioning system on Wrangler/YJ
models is a dual flow unit. Cooling air can be
drawn from outside the vehicle or previously
cooled air can be recirculated within the interior.

### The evaporator, blower fan and motor, thermo-

stat, expansion valve, capillary tube, air outlets
and system controls are located in the evaporator housing. The evaporator housing is mounted under the instrument panel. The compressor, condensor, receiver-dryer and refrigerant
lines are located in the engine compartment.

### A rotary-type compressor with magnetic clutch

operated drive pulley is used for Wrangler/YJ
models with air conditioning.
SYSTEM OPERATION
Refrigerant R-12 is the only refrigerant used in
the air conditioning system.
The compressor pressurizes and increases
temperature of the refrigerant converting it from
a liquid to a high pressure vapor. The vapor is
then pumped into the condenser which cools
the vapor by transferring heat to the air passing
over the condenser fins.

### The receiver-dryer is a reservoir that supplies

pressurized liquid refrigerant to the expansion
valve at all times. The receiver-dryer also operates as a dehumidifier by removing moisture
from the refrigerant.
The pressurized liquid refrigerant flows into the
expansion valve from the receiver-dryer. The
expansion valve meters refrigerant into the
evaporator where a low pressure is maintained
by the inlet (suction) side of the compressor.

### As refrigerant enters the evaporator, it immedi-

ately absorbs heat from the ambient temperature air flowing over the evaporator core. The
rapid absorption of heat cools the incoming air
which is then distributed into the vehicle
interior.
The rapid absorption of heat by the liquid refrigerant, causes the refrigerant to begin boiling
almost immediately after entering the evaporator. This process converts the high pressure
liquid into a low pressure gas which flows back
to the compressor to begin the cooling cycle
again.

### As the refrigerant vapor cools, it condenses

back into a liquid that is still pressurized. The
pressurized liquid then flows into the receiverdryer.
1 „-JA
HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
SERVICE DIAGNOSIS
General Diagnosis Information

### The air conditioning system generally operates

at peak efficiency at normal highway speeds.
However, a slight reduction in cooling efficiency
may be experienced in congested city driving
conditions; especially when ambient temperatures are high.

### Driving at relatively high speeds for extended

periods may cause the evaporator coils to frost
over. If frosting is severe, a temporary loss of
cooling may occur. To correct a frost-over condition, turn the control temperature knob off
and operate the blower fan for a few minutes.

### When diagnosing a gradual decrease in cooling

efficiency, remember to check condition of the
condensor and radiator fins. Air flow blockage
of either component, caused by dirt, foreign
material or insects, will affect the air conditioning and engine cooling systems equally. Also
note if the vehicle is equipped with a protective
screen. Some screens can restrict air flow to
the radiator and condensor.

### During high ambient temperature operation, a

slight increase in engine coolant temperature is
a normal occurence when the air conditioner
system is operating.

diagnosis procedures.

### Diagnosis Charts A and B outline general per-

formance diagnosis information. Chart C provides information needed to interpret results of
a pressure test using gauge and manifold assembly J 23575 or portable station J 23500-01.
Chart D outlines diagnosis information exclusive to the air conditioning compressor.

AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
REFRIGERANT SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
The refrigerant used for automotive air conditioner systems is dichlorodifluoromethane,
commercially known as Refrigerant-12 or R-12.

### R-12 is transparent and colorless in both the

liquid and vapor state. Because it has a boiling
point of 29 J ° C (217°F) below zero at atmospheric pressure, it vaporizes repidly at all ambient temperatures and pressures.
The vapor is heavier than air. It is not flammable
nor explosive and is not poisonous unless exposed to an open flame. It is also not corrosive
unless combined with water.

### Observe the following safety precautions when

working with R-12.
• R-12 evaporates almost immediately at normal atmospheric pressures and temperatures. As a result, it can freeze objects on
contact.
o For this reason, extreme care must be taken
to prevent R-12 from contacting the skin and
.specially the eyes

### WARNING: Always wear safety goggles when

servicing the refrigeration part of the air conditioner system. Keep a bottle of sterile mineral
oil and a weak solution of boric acid handy
when servicing the refrigeration system. If liquid
R-12 gets into the eyes, wash them out with a
few drops of mineral oil (R-12 is rapidly absorbed by oil). Then wash the eyes again with a
weak solution of boric acid. Call a doctor immediately, even if irritation has ceased after first
aid treatment.

### WARNING: Never heat a container of R-12

above 51.7°C (125°F).
• Before charging or adding R-12 to the system, moderate heat will be required to increase the pressure of R-12 in a container
above system pressure. Use warm water in a
bucket or pan for this purpose. The water
temperature must not exceed 5 1 . 7 ° C

### (125°F).

• Do not heat the R-12 container with an open
flame or any means that would raise refrigerant temperature above the specified
maximum.
• Do not weld or steam clean system hoses or
components.
CAUTION: Do not add R-12 in liquid form to the
system. Liquid refrigerant can damage the
compressor.
• Add R-12 to the system in vapor form only.

### Keep refrigerant containers upright when

charging the system to ensure this. When
recharging the system after service, keep the
supply tank or cans in an upright position. If
the refrigerant container is on its side or upside down, liquid refrigerant will enter the
system and damage the compressor

### WARNING: Large quantities of R-12 vapor in

small poorly ventilated areas can displace the
air and cause suffocation. Always work in a
well-ventilated area and be sure to maintain
good ventilation throughout the work area.
• Discharge refrigerant into the service bay exhaust system or outside the building only.

### WARNING: Although R-12 vapor is normally not

poisonous, it changes into a highly poisonous
gas if allowed to contact an open flame.
L-: -20
HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
• Do not discharge R-12 in any area containing
an open flame (e.g. portable heaters, welding
equipment).
• Use an electronic-type leak detector to check
for system leaks whenever possible. The
halide torch leak detector utilizes an open
flame for the detection process. R-12 refrigerant becomes a highly poisionous gas when
exposed to an open flame. If a halide torch
detector must be used, avoid inhaling the resulting fumes.

### CAUTION: Generally, R-12 is not corrosive un-

less combined with water. However, it can discolor chrome and bright metal trim. Keep R-12
refrigerant away from these items.
• R-12 becomes highly corrosive when combined with water and can damage painted
and unpainted metal surfaces. Do not allow

### R-12 to contact any metal surfaces during

service operations.
SERVICE VALVES
The discharge (high pressure) and inlet (suction) service valves are used for diagnosis,
charging, discharging and evacuating the system. They are also used to isolate the system
during component removal/installation.

### The service valves are three-position valves.

Normal operating position for the valve stem is
position (A) which is the back-seated (full-out)
position. The stem is turned counterclockwise
to place it in this position.
L-21
HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING

### AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM

Valve stem position (B) is the front seated (fullin) position. It is used to isolate the compressor
from the system. The stem is turned clockwise
to place it in this position.
In position (C), the valve stem is mid-positioned
and the gauge port is open. This position is
used for pressure testing and for charging, discharging and evacuating the system.

Connecting The Pressure Gauge and Manifold
Remove and retain the service valve protective
caps.
Close both of the hand valves on the gauge and
manifold.

### Connect the compound gauge hose (1) to the

suction (low pressure ) service valve.
Connect the high side gauge hose (2) to the
discharge (high pressure) service valve.
Turn both of the service valve stems to midposition (C).
Open both of the manifold hand valves (3) for 35 seconds to purge air from the manifold and
hoses.

Verify that both hand valves are fully closed.
The gauge and manifold is now ready for pressure testing. Refer to the System Pressure Test

### SYSTEM PRESSURE TEST

Connect the pressure gauge and manifold to
the service valves.
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put your hands near the
pulley, belts or fan. Do not wear loose clothing.

### Start the engine.

Set the A/C system at the full cooling setting
but not to the MAX setting.
Operate the engine at 1500 rpm for about 10
minutes to stabilize the A/C system.
Insert a thermometer into the discharge air outlet and note air temperature. Temperature
should be approximately 7.1 °C (45°F).

### NOTE: Discharge air temperature will vary de-

pending upon relative humidity. Generally, low
humidity results in a slightly lower temperature
while high humidity results in slightly higher
temperatures. The range variance is usually
plus or minus three degrees.

### Observe the gauge pressures. High side (dis-

charge) pressure should be approximately two
times ambient temperature. Low side (suction)
pressure should be approximately 10% of high
side pressure.
For example, if shop temperature is 80°F, high
side pressure would be about 160 psi. and low
side pressure would be about 16 psi.

### NOTE: The above pressures are approxima-

tions only. Relative humidity, atmospheric pressure and altitude will all affect pressure readings. Depending upon atmospheric conditions,
the system may function efficiently with pressures that are lower or higher.

### If pressures are abnormally high or low, refer to

the Diagnosis Charts.
DISCHARGING THE SYSTEM
The refrigerant must be discharged before replacing any system component except the compressor. The compressor can be isolated with
the service valves.

### Discharge Procedure

Connect the pressure gauge and manifold to
the service valves.
Open both manifold hand valves fully.
CAUTION: Do not allow the refrigerant to discharge rapidly. The oil in the compressor and
system will be forced out along with the
refrigerant.

### Open both of the service valves slightly (from

back-seated to mid-position) and allow the refrigerant to discharge slowly.
L-24
HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
EVACUATING THE SYSTEM
The system must be evacuated whenever refrigerant has been discharged or when system
refrigerant level has become abnormally low. A
vacuum pump is used for the evacuation
process.

### The system must be evacuated to remove any

moisture or air that may have collected in the
system. If moisture is not removed from the
system, it will combine with R-12 to form a
highly corrosive substance.
The vacuum pump decreases system pressure
by creating a vacuum within the system. The
pressure drop causes the boiling point of moisture in the system to decrease also. The moisture then boils into a vapor which is easily
drawn off by the vacuum.

### At an ambient temperature of 23.9°C (75°F) and

a vacuum of 99 kPa (29.5 in. Hg), water will boil
at approximately 12°C (54°F). This will produce
complete vaporization of all moisture in the
system.
NOTE: At elevations above sea level, it may not
be possible to obtain a vacuum of 99 kPa (29.5
in. Hg) on the low side. For each 300 meters
(1000 ft) increase in altitude, the vacuum must
be corrected by 3.37 kPa (1 in. Hg) to compensate for the change in atmospheric pressure.

### For example, at an of altitude of 300 meters

(1000 ft), a vacuum of 96 kPa (28.5 in. Hg) will
be equivalent to 99 kPa (29.5 in. Hg) at sea
level. When this vacuum level is attained, a minimum evacuation time of 30 minutes should be
allowed to ensure total moisture removal.

### Evacuation With Vacuum Pump J 26695

NOTE: The J 26695 Vacuum Pump and motor
must be kept upright at all times to prevent oil
spills.
Connect the pressure gauge and manifold to
the service valves.
Discharge the system.
Connect the center service hose on the gauge
and manifold to the vacuum pump inlet fitting.

### Turn both manifold hand valves to the wide

open position.
Start the vacuum pump and observe the vacuum gauge reading.
Test the system for leaks as follows:
• Close the manifold hand valves.
• Stop the vacuum pump and observe the vacuum reading.
• If the system is leak-free, vacuum will hold
steady at the level indicated when the pump
was stopped. If vacuum remains steady for
3-5 minutes, resume and continue evacuation for a minimum of 30 minutes.
• If the system has a leak, vacuum will fall off
or rapidly drop to a zero reading. If a leak
exists, partiallly charge the system. Find and
repair the leak and resume evacuation.

### Continue operating the pump for a minimum of

30 minutes after attaining lowest vacuum indicated on the gauge.
Close the manifold hand valves and stop the
vacuum pump.
L-25
HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
Disconnect the center service hose from the
vacuum pump. The system is now ready for
charging.

### Evacuation With Portable Service Station

J 23501-01
The J 23500-01 air conditioner service station is
a self contained, portable unit equipped with a
vacuum pump, metering-charging cylinder, refrigerant supply, pressure and vacuum gauges,
service hoses and control valves.

### Turn the station vacuum pump control switch

Off (the switch is at the front of the station). The
pump control switch must be OFF before connecting the station to an electrical power
source.
Close all the hand valves.
Connect the red charging hose (1) to the discharge service valve.

### Connect the blue charging hose (2) to the inlet

(suction) service valve.
Discharge the system. Leave the suction and
discharge service valves in the mid-position.
CAUTION: The system must be completely discharged before evacuating. If the system is still
charged, refrigerant can enter and damage the
vacuum pump.

### Connect the vacuum pump hose to the vacuum

pump inlet.
Open the low and high pressure control valves
on the charging station.
Start the vacuum pump (3). Open the vacuum
control valve and note the vacuum reading.
Test the system for leaks as follows:
# Stop the vacuum pump and observe the vacuum reading.

• If the system is leak-free, vacuum will hold
steady at the level indicated when the pump
was stopped. If vacuum remains steady for
3-5 minutes, resume and continue evacuation for a minimum of 30 minutes.
• If the system has a leak, vacuum will fall off
or rapidly drop to a zero reading. If a leak
exists, partiality charge the system. Find and
repair the leak and resume evacuation.
• Continue evacuating the system for a minimum of 30 minutes after attaining the lowest
vacuum level.
# Fill the station charging cylinder (4) while the
system is evacuating.
• Close the vacuum control valve (5) and stop
the vacuum pump.
# Observe low pressure gauge (6) to determine
if a system leak exists. If the system is leakfree, the system is now ready for charging.

LEAK TESTING
External leaks in the system can be located using electronic detector J 29547 or halide torch J
6084.

### The electronic leak detector is recommended

because it is light, accurate and most important,
does not expose the user to toxic gas fumes.
The halide torch requires an open flame for leak
detection. When R-12 is exposed to an open
flame, it turns into Phosgene gas which is
poisonous.

### Procedures for using the two leak detectors are

as follows.
# Begin leak testing. Move the flexible probe
slowly under all suspect connections, joints
and seals.
NOTE: Because R-12 refrigerant is heavier than
air, leaks are more readily detected on the lower side of components being checked.

### The leak indicator light will illuminate when a

leak is detected.
NOTE: The indicator light will go out if the probe
tip is held near the leak point for an extended
period.
Repair leaks as required.
Leak Testing With Electronic Detector J 21547
NOTE: Leak detector J 29547 will locate R-12
leaks as small as one-half ounce per year.

### Calibrate the detector as outlined in the manu-

facturer's instructions.
Remove the flexible detector probe from the
case.
Turn the detector control switch On.
Prepare the detector for use.
# Place the flexible probe tip near the leak port
on the detector.

### Evacuate and recharge the system after leaks

are corrected.
Leak Testing With Halide Torch J 6084
The torch is fueled by propane gas contained in
the cylinder (4). The gas heats a copper reactor
ring mounted in the stove (2) at the top of the
torch. Air entering the search hose (5) is drawn
into the stove and into contact with the reactor
ring. If R-12 is present in the area being tested,
the normally light blue flame will change to
green or a purplish-blue color.
• Adjust the BAT thumbwheel a few teeth at a
time, until the light illuminates-then goes out
when the tip is removed from the leak port.

Leak Test Procedure
Open the cylinder valve (3) and ignite the torch.
Adjust the flame just only high enough to heat
the copper reactor ring to a cherry red color.

### Lower the flame until it is about 6.4 mm (1/4 in)

above or even with the copper reactor ring. A
smaller flame is more sensitive to the presence
of R-12.
Move the search hose (5) slowly under all suspected components.
NOTE: Because refrigerant is heavier than air,
leaks are more readily detected on the lower
side of the areas being tested.

### Watch for a change in flame color as the hose is

moved under various components. A flame color change indicates a leak.
WARNING: When R 12 refrigerant contacts an
open flame, phosgene gas is produced. Never
inhale the vapor from the torch because it is
poisonous.

### Repair any leaks as required.

Evacuate and recharge the system after correcting a leak.

Compressor Oil Level
The compressor oil level must be checked and
adjusted if the system has been discharged
rapidly, or when a component has been replaced. If a replacement compressor is being
installed, it must be filled with new compressor
oil.

### I-49

HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
The normal quantity of oil required for the compressor and entire system is 175 cc (6 oz. ±0.5
oz.).
CAUTION: Do not overfill the compressor. Excessive amounts of oil in the system will hinder
compressor operation and reduce cooling
efficiency.

### Two oil level checking procedures are necessa-

ry. Use procedure A when the compressor is
being replaced and the system was discharged
properly (no oil loss). Ude procedure B for routine maintenance or when checking oil level after replacing a system component.

### NOTE: In cases where rapid loss of refrigerant

and oil occured, the system must be evacuated
and purged and the compressor refilled with the
necessary amount of oil for the entire system.
Oil Level Check-Procedure A
m Remove the oil filler plug (1) from the original
and replacement compressors.
• Drain the oil from the replacement compressor into a clean container.
• Drain the oil from the original compressor
into a measuring cup or graduated beaker.

### Note the amount of oil drained.

• Refill the replacement compressor with the
same amount of oil drained from the original
compressor plus one additional fluid ounce.
For example, if the old compressor contained 3.5 ounces of oil, fill the replacement
compressor with a total of 4.5 ounces of oH.

### Oil Level Check-Procedure B

• Start the and operate the engine at idle
speed.
• Operate the air conditioning system for 10
minutes to return the maximum amount of oil
in the system to the compressor.
• Stop the engine and disconnect the magnetic
clutch feed wire.
• Front-seat the discharge and suction service
valves.
• Loosen the compressor oil filler plug (1) just
enough to release internal pressure. Remove
the plug after slowly bleeding off all
pressure.
• Look through the oil filler plug hole (A), and
rotate the clutch front plate to position the
piston connecting rod in the center of the oil
filler plug hole.
80139

### L-50

HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING
AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEM
• Remove the dipstick and count the number
of dipstick increments covered with compressor oil. Correct oil level is between four
and six increments.
• Adjust compressor oil level as necessary

### CAUTION: Do not overfill the compressor. Ex-

cessive amounts of oil in the system will hinder
compressor operation and reduce cooling
efficiency.
81203C
• Insert dipstick J 29642-12 in the oil filler plug
hole. Position the dipstick to the right of the
piston connecting rod. Then move the dipstick downward until the dipstick stop contacts the compressor housing.

### STANDARD RADIO ANTENNA

GENERAL INFORMATION
AM and AM/FM radio antennas must have a
good ground to eliminate static. The antenna
mast is grounded through the radio. The
antenna base is grounded to the vehicle body.
The wire mesh coaxial shield surrounding the
center conductor wire of the antenna lead-in
cable is grounded to the radio and the antenna
base.

### A1TENNA TESTS

Antenna ground continuity is checked with an
ohmmeter. The following four tests are required:
• Mast-to-ground test 1
• Tip of mast-to-tip of conductor test 2
• Body ground-to-battery ground test 3
r Body ground-to-coaxial shield test 4

### Test lead connections for the ohmmeter (OM)

are shown in the following schematic.
OM
i
OM
© o
1
OM
0=H
4
- 0 0 -
T
OM
85118
Mast-To-Ground Test 1
Test 1 determines if the antenna is making
electrical contact with the radio and if the
antenna mast is insulated from the base.

### Procedure is as follows:

• Connect one ohmmeter (OM) lead to the tip of
the antenna mast and the other lead to the
antenna base.
• With the antenna connected to the radio, there
should be continuity (approximately 15
ohms).
• Disconnect the antenna from the radio and
check continuity again.
• Continuity should not exist with the antenna
disconnected from the radio.

### Tip Of Mast-To-Tip Of Conductor Test 2

Test 2 checks the antenna for an open circuit as
follows:
• Disconnect the antenna cable from the radio.
• Connect one ohmmeter test lead to the tip of
the mast and the other lead to the tip of the
antenna cable lead-in (the part inserted into
the radio).
• Continuity should not exist (ohmmeter should
only register a fraction of an ohm).
M-3

STANDARD RADIO ANTENNA
Body irouii-Ti-Baiery Ground Test 3
Test 3 checks condition of the vehicle body
ground connection as follows:
• Connect one ohmmeter test lead to the vehicle
fender and the other lead to the battery
negative post.
• Resistance should be less than one ohm.
• If resistance is more than one ohm, check the
braided ground strap connected to the engine
and vehicle body for being loose, corroded, or
damaged. Repair as necessary.

and the other lead to the crimp on the coaxial

• Resistance should be less then one ohm.
• If resistance is more than one ohm, replace
the antenna base attaching screws with new
cadmium plated screws.

SUBJECT: S7JCRUZ CAMPAIGN (Type "S" Campaign)
Some 1987 YJ vehicles equipped with cruise control may have a cruise control regulator that could
react inconsistently when the cruise control system is in the ON position.
This is a Safety Campaign subject to all campaign procedures involving safety related elements.
Vehicles involved in this campaign were built between the following Vehicle Identification Numbers

### (VIN)

2 B X X X X X X X X X 5 3 0 2 1 9 and VIN
2 B X X X X X X X X X 5 3 1 0 9 3 .
Service correction involves inspecting vehicles and replacing the regulator if required.
PROCEDURE
1. Check the regulator for a daub of white paint.

### If there is a white mark, release the vehicle.

If a white mark is not evident continue with
the procedure.
2. Remove the mounting screws (A) that holds
the regulator (B) in place under the
dashboard on the drivers side by the fuse
panel.
3. Disconnect the electrical connector (C) from
the regulator.
103733
Copyright © 1987 American Motors Corporation and Jeep Corporation. All Rights Reserved. Litho in U.S.A.CAN 8980 001
227

### 4. Inspect the date code (D) on the connector

end of the regulator.
103731
Example of marking with date code underlined:
8953000320
0237B87M
(23rd day of 1987)
If the date code (first three digits of second line)
is 020, 041 or any number between 020 and 041,
the regulator must be replaced. If the date code
is outside of these limits, the regulator does not
have to be replaced.

### 5. Connect the electrical connector and install

the regulator
using mounting screws
previously removed.
6.
Place a daub of white paint on the regulator
case so that it can be seen in the installed
position.
NOTE: The regulator has already been preset
during its manufacture.

### 7. Road test the vehicle to confirm proper

operation of the new regulator.
a. Move the slide button of the control
switch to the ON position. Drive at 45
mph (72 km/h). Press and release the
SET/COAST button, then remove foot
from the accelerator pedal.
(1) The controlled speed should sta;
within 2 mph (3 km/h) of the "Se

### Speed". This is controlled by the

CENTERING ADJ.
(2) The road speed should not fluctuate
more than 2 mph (3 km/h). This k
controlled by the SENSITIVITY ADJ
b. Slow the vehicle to 15 mph (24 km/h).
c.
Press slide button of control switch to

### RESUME/ACCEL position and hold it

there as you gradually increase speed.
When the vehicle suddenly speeds up
and the accelerator pedal gives way,
glance at the speedometer and release
the slide button.
d. Tap the brake pedal to disengage the
system.
e. The speed at which the system took control is the "Low Speed Setting". If it is

### NOT between 27 and 33 mph (43 and 53

km/h), it should be corrected. This is controlled by the LOW SPEED SW. ADJ.
8. If necessary adjust the regulator as described
in Regulator Adjustment.
REGULATOR ADJUSTMENT
Low Speed Switch (Engagement) Adjustment

### On one side of the regulator there are two holes.

Insert a small screwdriver in the one marked
LOW SPEED SW. ADJ.
1. If the "Low Speed Setting" was too fast, turn
the LOW SPEED SW. ADJ. counterclockwise. If the setting was too slow, turn
the LOW SPEED SW. ADJ. clockwise.

### 2. Repeat the test and adjustment sequence

until the "Low Speed Setting" is 27-33 mph
(43-53 km/h).
Centering Adjustment
The CENTERING ADJ. is next to the LOW
SPEED SW. ADJ,
If controlled speed is more than 2 mph (3 km/h)
above or below the "Set Speed", turn the

### CENTERING ADJ.:

• counterclockwise to decrease
• clockwise to increase
Sensitivity Adjustment
The SENSITIVITY ADJ. is on the opposite side
of the regulator from the CENTERING ADJ.
If sensitivity needs to be adjusted turn the SEN-

### SITIVITY ADJ.:

•
counterclockwise to decrease
•
clockwise to increase
NOTE: Changes in the sensitivity setting affect
centering, so if sensitivity is changed, check the
centering again and adjust as required.

HEATER CORE HOSE CHAFING
Some 1987 WRANGLER/YJ vehicles equipped with 4.2L 6-Cyl. engines may have the heater
core-to-intake manifold hose chafing on a stud protruding from the dash panel.
NOTE: This problem was corrected on vehicles built after May 28, 1986, and starting with
sequence number 9086.
Service correction involves inspecting for this condition and repositioning the hose as follows.

### PROCEDURE

Replace hose, if necessary, before
repositioning.

dash panel stud.

### 6. Refill the cooling system.

7. Start the engine.
8. Check for leaks.

PARKING BRAKE CABLE NOISE
Some 1987 WRANGLER/YJ vehicles, built prior to VIN 2 BXXXXXXXHB520144, may produce a
noise in the right rear area when the rear of the vehicle is loaded. This noise may be caused by the
parking brake cable rubbing the edge of the right rear wheel rim.
Service correction involves the installation of a parking brake cable locating clip to prevent cable
movement.

### PROCEDURE

1. Remove the fasteners (D) holding the right
rear parking brake cable bracket (C) to the
floorpan (Fig. 1).
Fig. 1
2. Slide the bracket toward the right rear wheel.
3. Measure 559 mm ± 3 mm (22.0 in. ±
0.125 in.) back from the parking brake cable
mounting bracket (E) and snap the locating
clip (A) over the parking brake cable (Fig. 2).

### NOTE: Make sure the parking brake cable is

routed below the heat shield (B).
Copyright © 1986 American Motors Corporation and Jeep Corporation. All rights reserved. Litho in U.S.A.
8980 001 128
4. Slide bracket (C) up to the edge of locating
clip (A).

### 5. Using the fasteners removed earlier, attach

ELECTRICAL
ALTERNATOR NO-CHARGE
A no-charge condition has been identified on 1987 Wranglers equipped with 4.2L engines that is not
caused by an alternator malfunction.
The cause of this no-charge condition may be a bent terminal (brown wire) in the female (gray)
connector (A) of the 6-inch alternator jumper harness. When indications of a low battery are noted,
e.g., voltmeter below normal or slow cranking, the jumper harness gray connector should be inspected.
Service correction involves inspecting the jumper harness connector and straightening the terminal
as follows.

### PROCEDURE

1. Disconnect the gray connector (A).
FRONT
103586
2. Check the terminal of the brown wire to see if
it is bent.
3. If the pin(s) are bent use a needle nose pliers
and straighten the bent pin(s).
4. If the pin(s) are ok, proceed to diagnosing the
charging system as outlined in M.R. 279.

### 5. Connect the harness together.

6. Test alternator for proper performance. Refer to M.R. 279.

THIS I.S. NOTE HAS BEEN REVISED AS INDICATED BY THE REVISION BARS:
IDLE SPEED WARIATION
Some 1987 Wrangler vehicles equipped with the 2.46L engine may exhibit a variation in engine idle
speed. This condition is generally intermittent and may become more evident with increased temperatures and/or mileage.
The vehicle should be tested with the MS 1700 Diagnostic Tester. Because the condition is intermittent, the MS 1700 may not be able to detect the fault. If the vehicle passes all the tests and no other
problems are found, the oxygen (02) sensor may be the cause of this condition.

### PROCEDURE

1. Disconnect the 02 sensor connector (A).
2. Remove the 02 sensor from the exhaust manifold.
3. Clean the threads in the exhaust manifold.
NOTE: Antiseize sealer is already applied to
the threads of replacement 0 2 sensors.

### 4. Install a new 02 sensor marked with a yellow

tag. Tighten the sensor to 27-34 N-m (20-25
ft-lbs) torque.
5. Connect the 02 sensor connector.

NEW CRANKSHAFT REAR MAIN BEARING OIL SEAL
A new crankshaft rear main bearing oil seal with improved sealing characteristics and a new seal
installation tool have been released for the 2.46 Liter four-cylinder engine.
Install the new seal, P/N 8933 004 143, using the new seal installation tool J-36306 (A). The
installation tool is a required tool for installing the rear main bearing oil seals correctly. It will be sent to
all AMC/Jeep dealers automatically.
This new rear main bearing oil seal is used in production on engines built December 8,1986 and later.

### J-36306

103764
NOTE: The tool comes with a removable shim
(B). The shim is used ONLY if the new rear main
bearing oil seal (P/N 8933 004 143) is not
available and the old style seal (P/N 3241669) is
used instead. DO NOT use the shim when
installing the new seal.
103765

prevent dirt from contacting the seal lip.

1. Remove the transmission ( s e e Chapter

Automatic Transmission).
2. Remove the flywheel or converter drive plate.

### 3. Use a thin bladed straight screwdriver to

remove the old seal from around the
crankshaft flange.
4. Back off the plastic wing nut on tool J-36306
until it contacts the nut.
NOTE: Install the shim (B) ONLY if the old style
seal is used.

of the seal.

### 6. Install the new seal on tool J-36306 with

wing nut.

the crankshaft.

out. This will seat the seal.

ALTITUDE PERFORMANCE ADJUSTMENTS
This I.S. Note outlines adjustments for improved engine performance on 1987 Jeep Wrangler/YJ
vehicles, equipped with 2.46L (TBI) or 4.2L engines, being operated at altitudes above or below
that which the engine was originally certified.
When necessary, perform the engine adjustments outlined in the adjustment procedure portion
of this I.S. Note.
Any such vehicles so adjusted, must have the Vehicle Emission Control Information Update Label
attached next to the original Vehicle Emission Control Information label.
The adjustment procedures and update labels must be made available at no cost to independent
repair facilities and to the general public.

### Owner Notification

A notification is provided in the current Owner's Manuals to make customers aware of these
adjustments.

NO START CONDITION WHEN HOT
Some 1987 Wrangler/YJ vehicles equipped with the 4.2L engine may develop a no start condition
when operated in high ambient temperatures. This condition may be caused by fuel vaporizing in
the fuel lines.
Service correction involves replacing two sections of the fuel line with new fuel lines that are wrapped
with convoluted tubing. One section of line runs from the frame to the fuel pump. The other section
runs from the fuel pump to the fuel filter.

### ENGINE COMPARTMENT SPLASH SHIELDS

1987 Wrangler/YJ models with 4.2L I-6 engine
may collect dirt contamination during off-road
driving. Dirt or water may enter the engine compartment and interfere with engine operation.
Several modifications have been incorporated
in vehicles built after VIN 1JXXXXXX-

### XXX500974 to reduce water and dirt contami-

nation.
A service kit has been developed to provide
shielding in the engine compartment for vehicles built prior to the VIN above. This kit consists of two front splash shields, an air intake
deflector, two air cleaner grommets and sealed
nuts for the footman loop on the hood. The following procedures outline installation of this
shield kit.

### PROCEDURES

Front Splash Shields
1. Raise the vehicle with a frame contact hoist.
2. Remove both front wheels and tires.
3. Position a front splash shield to the right
front wheelhouse using the brake hose as a
locator (A-Fig. 1).

### Fig.1

4. Mark the center of each splash shield hole.
There are five holes for the wheelhouse and
two holes for the frame (B, C-Fig. 1).
5. Remove splash shield and center punch all
hole locations. Using a 7 mm (9/32 in.) drill
bit, drill all seven holes for the right splash
shield.

### Note: Be careful when drilling holes

through the wheelhouse into the engine
compartment. Keep drill from contacting
components inside the engine compartment.
Copyright © 1987 American Motors Corporation and Jeep Corporation. All rights reserved. Litho in U.S.A.
8980 001 360

### 6. Using Ditzler DP40/401, Sikkens Washpri-

mer or Sherwin Williams E2Y36, prime bare
metal areas exposed by drilling holes. After
applying primer, apply an enamel top coat
and allow it to dry.
7. Position splash shield and install it using
panel fasteners (Fig. 1). Push the rear end
of shield in behind shock absorber bracket
(L-Fig. 1).

### 8. Position the other front splash shield to the

left wheelhouse using the brake hose as a
locator.
9. Mark the center of the top splash shield
holes. Do not mark the two lower holes at
the frame (C-Fig. 1). These holes are not
used on the driver side shield.

### 10. Remove splash shield and center punch

the five top hole locations. Using a 7 mm
(9/32 in.) drill bit, drill the five holes into the
wheelhouse.
Note: Be careful when drilling holes
through the wheelhouse into the engine
compartment. Keep drill from contacting
components inside the engine compartment.
11 Using Ditzler DP 40/401, Sikkens Washprimer, or Sherwin Williams E2Y36, prime
bare metal areas exposed by drilling holes.

### After applying primer, apply an enamel top

coat and allow to dry.
12, Position splash shield and install it using
panel fasteners. Push rear end of the shield
behind the shock absorber bracket.
13. Install both front wheels and tires.

### GEARBOXES

Attention: Workshop, Parts Department
UNDERBODY NOISE
Some 1987 Wrangler models equipped with a 231 transfer case may experience an underbody
bumping noise while operating the vehicle on rough roads. This condition may be caused by
insufficient clearance between the transfer case lower housing and the skid plate/rear crossmember. A new skid plate, PN 8983 100 055, is available to correct this condition.
NOTE: The 231 transfer case entered production with VIN 2BXXXXXXXHB518291.
Service correction involves checking the transfer case-to-skid plate clearance and replacing the
skid plate if necessary.

### PROCEDURE

Clearance Check
1. Raise and support the vehicle.
2. Measure the clearance (A) between the rear
of transfer case and the skid plate as shown.
If the clearance is not at least 19 mm (3/4 in.)
check the transmission rear mount.

### If the transmission rear cushion is in good con-

dition, replace the skid plate as described.
If the rear cushion is damaged replace it
and recheck transfer case to skid plate/rear
crossmember clearance. If clearance remains
2302
Fig. 1
insufficient, continue with skid plate/rear crossmember replacement.
Copyright © 1987 American Motors Corporation and Jeep Corporation. All Rights Reserved. Litho in U.S.A.
8980 001 388

### Skid Plate/Rear Crassmsmbw Replacement

1. Raise and support the vehicle.
2. Place a safety stand under the transmission.
3. Place a second safety stand under the skid
plate.
2178
Fig a2
4. Remove the bolts (B) and the nuts (C) and
(D).
5. Remove skid plate/rear crossmember from
the vehicle underbody.

### 6. Install the new skid plate into position.

7. Install bolts (B) and torque to 41 N-m
(30 ft-lbs).
8. Install nuts (C) and torque to 45 N-m
(33 ft-lbs).
9. Install nut (D) and torque to 41 N-m
(30 ft-lbs).
10. Remove the safety stands and lower the
vehicle.

2.5L ENGINE
2.IL Crankshaft
A new crankshaft is used in 1988 2.5L engines.
The new crankshaft is shorter in length than the
previous shaft. A longer crankshaft dampener
bolt is required with the new, shorter shaft.
2.5L Valve Springs
1988, 2.5L engines are equipped with new
design, valve springs (A). The new springs are
slightly tapered top-to-bottom and are identified
by the two bottom coils (B) which are flush.

### New valve spring retainers and keepers (locks)

are also used to accomodate the new design
valve springs.
2516
The new valve springs can be removed/
installed on the vehicle with service tool J -
5892B. Part number for this tool is 8980 002
694. The tool is available from your PDC as part
of the special tool program.

### ENGINES

GENERAL INFORMATION
EMISSION MAINTENANCE TIMER AND
INDICATOR LIGHT
1988 Wrangler/YJ 49-State and Canada
models are equipped with an emission maintenence timer and indicator light. The timer and
light are used to alert the owner when oxygen
sensor-PCV valve replacement and other
scheduled emission maintenence is required.

### The indicator light is located in the instrument

cluster. The timer is mounted on the dash panel
near the accelerator pedal.
The timer (A) is operated by the ignition system.
It activates (flashes) the indicator light when
vehicle mileage reaches the scheduled maintenence interval of 133,000 kilometers (82,500
miles).

### Emission Maintenance Timer Service

The life cycle of the timer coincides with the
emission maintenance interval of 133,000
kilometers (82,500 miles). The timer can not be
reset after reaching this mileage interval. The
timer can only be replaced or disconnected.

### NOTE: The oxygen sensor and timer are inter-

dependent. If the timer should fail prematurely,
the oxygen sensor must be replaced along with
the timer. This is important in preserving the
correct sensor replacement interval and
ensuring proper engine performance.

### Emission Maintenence Timer Replacement

Remove the screws (B) attaching the timer (A)
to the dash bracket.
Disconnect the timer wire harness (C) and
remove the timer.
Connect the wire harness to the replacement
timer.
Mount the timer on the dash bracket and install
the timer attaching screws.
2428

6-CYLINDER STARTER MOTOR
SENERAL INFORMATION
A Mitsubishi starter motor is used on 1988
Wrangler/YJ six-cylinder engines. This starter
motor is a light-weight unit featuring a planetary
gear drive and permanent magnets for current
induction.

### The planetary gear drive is splined to both the

armature shaft and overrunning clutch. Starter
torque is transmitted to the overrunning clutch
STARTER MOTOR - 8-CYLINDER ENGINE
pinion through the planetary gears which provide higher rotational speeds.

### The starter magnetic field is produced by six

permanent magnets. The magnets are
mounted in the armature frame and positioned
according to polarity. They are permanently
attached to the frame and are not removable.
The starter motor is activated by a solenoid
mounted on the overrunning clutch housing.

### 1. Bushing

ELECTRICAL
6-CYLINDER STARTER MOTOR

### STARTER SERW1CE INFORMATION

The Mitsubishi starter motor is a serviceable
component and can be disassembled for
repair.
Replaceable components include the solenoid,
overrunning clutch, brushes, brush holder,
armature frame and magnets, overrunning
clutch housing and the planetary gear drive
assembly.

### Certain precautions must be observed when

servicing the Mitsubishi starter.
• The starter must not be roughly handled.
Hammer blows and similar mechanical
shocks can damage the unit.
• Be sure test connections are correct when
checking starter performance. A wrong connection will damage the starter magnets seriously enough to require replacement.
• Ensure cleanliness during starter repair.

### Metal chips are attracted by the starter mag-

nets. Be sure all chips are removed with compressed air and clean shop towels. Chips in
the armature frame, planetary gears, or overrunning clutch can cause premature wear.
• The starter armature, armature frame, overrunning clutch, planetary gears, solenoid
and rubber parts may be cleaned with dry
cloths and compressed air. Do not use liquid
cleaning agents on these components. All
other starter components may be cleaned
with commercially available solvents.
• Never clamp the starter motor armature
frame in a vise. Doing so may damage the
frame and magnets. Use only the mounting
flange on the overrunning clutch housing for
clamping purposes.

Inspection

### Remove the starter and check movement of the

### A damaged bushing or bearing, armature shaft,

or armature frame will cause the armature to
bind and not rotate freely.
If the armature and pinion rotate freely, perform
the No-Load Test before disassembly. If the
armature or pinion bind, disassemble and
repair the starter as needed.

### Starter No-Load Test

CAUTION: Do not operate the starter for more
than 5 seconds at a time during the no-load test.
The starter can be overheated and damaged if
operated for periods longer than this. Allow the
starter to cool down for a minimum of two minutes between tests.

### Connect a voltmeter (A) between terminal 45

and the starter frame. Connect (ground) the
remaining voltmeter terminal to the starter
frame or housing.
Install a mechanical tachometer (B) on the overrunning clutch pinion shaft to measure armature speed.

### Connect an ammeter (C) between the battery

positive post and terminal 30 of the solenoid.
Verify that the test battery is at specified test
voltage. Charge the battery if necessary.
Connect the battery negative terminal to the
starter frame or housing.

### Connect a test switch (D) between terminals 30

and 50 of the solenoid. The switch should be in
the open position.
C

Close the test switch (D) and operate the starter
for no more than 5 seconds. Record starter
rpm, current, and voltage. Then compare the
readings with those listed in the test specifications charts.

### NOTE: It is not necessary to obtain exact speci-

fied test voltage. If voltage is slightly higher,
rpm will also be higher proportionately (current
will not be affected). However, if test voltage is
higher than specified and exact test voltage is

### Interpret test results as follows:

Starter operation is normal if current flow and
rpm are within specified limits.
If rpm is low and current draw high, check for
the following conditions:
€ Connecting terminal or armature windings
shorted to ground
• Armature shaft bent or bearings are seized
• Armature housing damaged

### If the starter will not operate and current draw is

zero, check for the following conditions:
• Grease and dirt on brushes or commutator
• Open armature windings. Inspect commutator for burned spots.
• Worn brushes
• Damaged brush springs or spring holders
• Protruding insulation between commutator
bars
• Solenoid terminals damaged
• Brush connecting wire damaged

### If tests indicate an armature problem, check the

armature on the growler. Refer to the armature
testing procedures in this section.
Armature Ground Test
Place the armature in the growler jaws and turn
the power switch to TEST position.
Place one test lead (A) on the armature core.

### Place the other lead (B) on each commutator

bar and observe the test lamp. The lamp should
not light. If the lamp lights when the test lead
contacts one or more of the commutator bars,
the armature is grounded and must be replaced.
84936B
Armature Short Test

### CAUTION: To avoid damaging the growler, do

not operate the growler unless an armature is
mounted in the growler jaws.
Place the armature in the growler jaws and turn
the power switch to GROWLER position.

### Position the growler steel blade (C) parallel to

and touching the armature core. Slowly rotate
the armature one or more revolutions in the
growler jaws. If the steel blade vibrates at any
part of the core, the windings are shorted and
the armature must be replaced.

### 84937B

Armature lalance Test
Place the armature in the growler jaws and turn
the power switch to GROWLER position.
Place the contact fingers of the meter test lead
(D) across adjacent commutator bars.
Adjust the growler voltage control until the
pointer indicates highest voltage on scale.

### Test each commutator bar with the adjacent

bar until all have been tested. Zero voltage at
any commutator bar indicates a short circuit in
the pair being tested. The armature must be
replaced if a short is discovered.
84938B

(0.003 in).

STARTER CLEANING AND INSPECTION
Cleaning
Clean the armature, armature frame, overrunning clutch, solenoid, and brush holder assembly with clean, dry cloths or compressed air
only. Do not use liquid solvents to clean these
components. Use mineral spirits or similar solvents to clean the remaining starter components.

### Inspection

Inspect the armature frame and magnets. Do
not attempt to remove the magnets. They are
permanently attached. Replace the frame and
magnets as an assembly if either component is
damaged.
Replace the planetary gear assembly and pinion shaft if worn or damaged.

MODEL 231 TRANSFER CASE
GENERAL INFORMATION
Transfer Case Application
The Model 231 transfer case is used in 1987
W r a n g l e r / Y J m o d e l s built a f t e r
V I N
2BCCL8119HB518290 and in all 1988 Wrangler/YJ models.
2603

### Description

The Model 231 is a part-time transfer case with
a built-in low range reduction gear system. It
has three operating ranges plus a Neutral position. The low range system provides a gear
reduction ratio of 2.72:1 for increased low
speed torque capability.

### Operating Ranges

The Model 231 is a part-time unit with three
operating ranges which are: Two-wheel drive
high, four-wheel drive high and four-wheel drive
low. The four-wheel drive ranges are undifferentiated. Differential action between the front/
rear axles does not occur in the four wheel drive
ranges.

### Two-Wheel Drive Operation

Two-wheel drive range is for on-road, highway
operation or whenever the vehicle is operated
on a hard road surface.
Two-wheel drive is provided by a disconnect
mechanism in the front axle. A vacuum operated shift motor on the axle disconnects the
right-hand axle shaft when 2H range is
selected. The axle shift motor is controlled by a
vacuum switch that is actuated by the transfer
case shift sector and linkage.

### Four-Wheel Drive Operation

Two internal mechanisms provide the fourwheel drive ranges. A vacuum shift motor
connects the right-hand axle shaft and a synchronizer assembly engages the transfer case
front output shaft. The shift motor is operated
by a vacuum switch mounted on the transfer
case. The switch is actuated by the transfer
case shift linkage.
22

### GEARBOXES

MODEL 231 TRANSFER CASE
Shift Mechanism
Transfer case operating ranges are selected
with a floor mounted shift lever. The lever is
connected to the transfer case range lever by
an adjustable linkage rod. A straight line shift
pattern is used. Range positions are marked on
the the shift lever handle.

### Transfer Case identification

A circular ID tag (A) is attached to the rear case
of each Model 231 transfer case. The ID tag
provides the transfer case model number,
assembly number, serial number and low
range ratio.
The transfer case serial number also represents the date of build. For example, a serial
number of 8-7-87 would represent August 7,
1987.
iENERAL SPECIFICATIONS

### Transfer Case Type:

Part-time, dual range with low range reduction. Four-wheel
drive range is undifferentiated.
Torque Transfer Mode:
Output shaft and sprocket driven by interconnecting drive
chain.
Operating Ranges:
2-high, 4-high, 4-low and Neutral. Low range reduction ratio
is 2.72:1.

### Case Configuration:

Two-piece aluminum with removable extension and rear
retainer housings.
Lubricant Capacity:
1.54 liters (3.25 pints)
Required Lubricant:
MERCON® automatic transmission fluid.
Transfer Case Fill Level:

### To bottom edge of fill plug hole.

ALTITUDE PERFORMANCE ADJUSTMENTS
This I.S. Note outlines adjustment for optimum engine performance on 1SS5 AMC/Jeep/Renault
models being operated at high or low altitudes.
When necessary, perform the engine adjustments outlined in the Adjustment Procedures portion of
this I.S. Note. In addition, any 1985 model that is so adjusted must have a unique Emission Control
Information Update label installed. The part numbers (P/N) for these unique labels are provided in the

### 1. 1S85 ALLIANCE/ENCORE 1.4L - 1.7L

ENGINES AND FUEGO/SPORTWAGON
2.2L ENGINE
1985 Alliance/Encore 1.4L - 1.7L engines and
Fuego/Sportwagon 2.2L engines do not require
adjustment. The electronic control systems on
these engines have built-in compensating
circuits that make necessary adjustments
automatically.

### 2, 1985 CHEROKEE/WAGONEER 78 SERIES

2.8L GASOLINE AND 2.1L DIESEL ENGINES
For 1985, only the Cherokee/Wagoneer, 70
Series, 49-State/Canada 2.8L gasoline engine
requires adjustment as outlined below. The
1985 49-State/Canada and California 2.1 L
diesel engine and 1985 California 2.8L gasoline
engine do not require adjustment. The fuel
metering control systems on these engines
have built-in compensating devices that make
necessary adjustments automatically.
49-State/Canada 2 JL Engine Adjustment

### On 49-State/Canada (ONLY) 1985 Cherokee/

Wagoneer 70 Series 2.8L models sold for
operation at altitudes below 4,000 feet that are
being operated above 4,000 feet, the ignition
timing a s shown on the original Vehicle
Emission Control Information label in the engine
compartment, should be advanced 7° and
engine idle speed reset to the specifications
indicated on this same label.

### 1. Advance ignition timing 7° from the setting

indicated on the original Vehicle Emission
Control Information label and reset engine
idle speed to the setting indicated on the
same label.
2. Install Vehicle Emission Control Information
Update label, P/N EF 8980 000 743, next to
the original label.

### This adjustment applies to 1985 Cherokee/

Wagoneer, 49-State/Canada 2.8L models that
were originally sold for principal use at altitudes
below 4,000 feet. Refer to the Vehicle Emission
Control Information label in the engine compartment to identify these vehicles.

### NOTE: Whenever these vehicles are returned

to operation at altitudes below 4,000
feet, the ignition timing and engine idle
speed must be reset to original specifications and the Vehicle Emission Control Information Update label removed.

WAGONEER/TRUCK 4.2L ENGINE
For 1985, Eagle/Jeep 49-State/California/

models are different as outlined in the following
procedures.
49-State/Califoriia/Canada 4*2L Engine

### Adjustment - Automatic Transmission

On 1985 Eagle/Jeep, 49-State/California/
Canada 4.2L models with automatic transmission, originally sold for operation at altitudes
below 4,000 feet that are being operated above
4,000 feet, the ignition timing must be advanced
7° and engine idle speed reset. In addition, a
jumper wire must be added to the MCU circuit
to activate the altitude compensating circuit in
the MCU.

### 1. Move the carpeting away from the passenger

front seat toeboard to expose the MCU
harness.
2. Untape the two-terminal connector from the
MCU harness.
3. Connect jumper wire, P/N 318 6890, to the
two-terminal connector and reinstall the
carpet.
4. Advance ignition timing 7° from the setting
indicated on the original Vehicle Emission

### Control Information label in the engine

compartment and reset the engine idle speed
to the setting indicated on the same label.
5. Install Vehicle Emission Control Information
Update label, P/N EF 8980 000 743, next to
the original label.
These adjustments apply to 1985 Eagle/Jeep,
49-State/California/Canada 4.21 models with
automatic transmissions originally sold for
principal use at altitudes below 4,000 feet. Refer
to the Vehicle Emission Control Information
label to identify these vehicles.

### On 1985 Eagle/Jeep, 49-State/California/

Canada 4.2L models with automatic trans
mission originally sold for operation at altitudes

circuit jumper wire must be disconnected and
taped to the MCU harness.

### 1. Move the carpeting away from the passenger

front seat toeboard to expose the MCU
harness.

3. Retard ignition timing 7° from the setting

### Control label in the engine compartment and

reset engine idle speed to the setting

original label.

carburetor E G R port as follows (Fig. 1).

discard it.

end of tee connector 2.
c. Cut and install tee connector, P/N 321
0891, in vacuum line 3 (Fig. 1). Position the
connector about 1 % inches from the E G R -

### CTO end of the line.

in line 3 (Fig. 1).

Control Information label in the engine
compartment and reset engine idle speed to
the setting indicated on the same label.

### 6. Install Vehicle Emission Control Information

Update label, P/N E F 8980 000 743, next to
the original label.

49-State/California/Canada 4.2L models with

to original specifications, and the

### Vehicle Emission Control Update label

removed.

ALTITUDE PERFORMANCE ADJUSTMENTS
This I.S. Note outlines adjustment for optimum engine performance on 1986 AMC/Jeep/Renault
models being operated at high or low altitudes.
When necessary, perform the engine adjustments outlined in this I.S. Note. In addition, any 1986
model that is so adjusted must have a unique Emission Control Information Update label installed. The
part numbers for these unique labels are provided in the adjustment procedures outlined in this

### I.S. Note.

The adjustment procedures and unique labels must be made available at no cost to independent
repair facilities and the general public. A notification is also provided in current owner manuals to make
the owner aware of these adjustments. The Emission Control Information Update labels and technical
information are available from:

3.1986 CJ 2.46L CARBURETOR EQUIPPED

### ENGINES

1986, 2.46L carburetor equipped engines in
Califomia/49-State/Canada C J models require
adjustment as outlined below.
Adjystrneni - California/49-State/Canada
Carburetor Equipped 2.46L Engines
On 1986 California/49-State/Canada models,
with a carburetor equipped 2.46L engine,
originaiiy sold for operation at altitudes below
4,000 feet that are being operated above 4,000
feet, the ignition timing as shown on the original

### Vehicle Emission Control Information label in

the engine compartment, should be advanced
7° and engine idle s p e e d reset to the
specifications indicated on this same label. In
addition, a ground wire must be connected to the
MCU circuit to activate the altitude compensating
circuit in the MCU.

### 1. Locate the black with tracer altitude circuit

ground wire. The wire is in the MCU harness.
It is located near the ignit'on coil, or at the rearcenter of the engine compartment between the
dash panel and air cleaner.
2. Remove the tape from the eyelet attached to
the end of the ground wire.

### 3. Connect the ground wire eyelet to a conven-

ient ground location on the engine.
4. Advance ignition timing 7° from the setting
indicated on the original Vehicle Emission
Control Information label and reset engine
idle speed to the setting indicated on the
same label.

### 5. Install Vehicle Emission Control Information

Update label, part number E F 8980 000 818,
next to the original label.
This adjustment applies to 1986 C J California/
49-State/Canada models, with a carburetor
equipped 2.46L engine, originally sold for
principal use at altitudes below 4,000 feet. Refer
to the Vehicle Emission Control Information
label in the engine compartment to identify these
vehicles.

### NOTE: Whenever these vehicles are returned

to operation at altitudes below 4,000
feet, the MCU circuit jumper wire must
be removed, the ignition timing and
engine idle speed reset to original
specifications and the Vehicle Emission
Control Information Update label
removed.

### ENGINE COOLANT/OIL LEAK DETECTION

A high intensity black lamp has been approved for use in pinpointing engine coolant and oil leaks.
The following procedures have been developed to detect engine coolant leaks and for other fluid
leaks: power steering fluid, automatic and manual transmission fluid and engine oil.

### PROCEDURE

Engine Coolant Leak Detection
NOTE: All models (except imports) now have
a coolant leak detection additive in the cooling system when the vehicle is delivered from
the factory. This additive will appear bright
green in color under the black lamp.

### 1. Add one ounce of coolant additive to the

engine cooling system, if necessary.
2. Start and run the engine until it reaches
operating temperature.
3. Place the heater controls in the heat mode to
circulate coolant through the heater system.
4. Plug the black lamp into an electrical outlet
and turn the switch to the ON position. When
it is ready to use, it will glow.

### 5. Aim the black lamp at the components of the

cooling system to pinpoint leaks in the
radiator, hoses, heater core, water pump and
engine assembly components that house the
engine coolant. If leaks are present, the additive will be seen under the black lamp as a
bright green glow. This additive is water
soluable for ease of clean-up for repeat
inspections.

### PROCEDURE

Oil Leak Detection
NOTE: All models (except i m p o r t s ) have a
dye additive added to t h e e n g i n e oil and
automatic transmission fluid at the factory.
Because of the different additives used, the
engine additive may appear l i g h t blue or
yellow when viewed under the black lamp.

### The automatic transmission fluid additive will

appear a greenish yellow color under the
black lamp.

8980 000 820
When checking for an ©ii leak, verify the color
of the additive used by removing the dipstick
and observing the oil under the black lamp.

### 1. Add one ounce of oil leak detection additive to

the system that is suspected to be leaking,
(engine oil, transmission, etc.), if necessary.
2. Start and run the engine until it reaches
operating temperature to allow the additive to
circulate throughout the system. Detecting
extremely small leaks may. require running
the engine for a longer period of time.

### 3. Plug the black lamp into an electrical outlet

and turn the switch to the ON position. When
it is ready to use, it will glow.
4 Raise the vehicle.
5. Aim the black lamp at the areas that are
suspected of leaking and look for a bright
greenish-yellow glow at the leak origin.

Attention: Workshop, Parts Department
CLUTCH HYDRAULIC SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS
On some 1983-85 Eagle/Jeep models with a hydraulic clutch linkage, fluid leakage from one or both
clutch cylinders, may be caused by the formation of an abrasive substance in the system fluid. In some
cases, material in the master cylinder-to-slave cylinder hose may chemically react with the fluid to
produce a mildly abrasive chloride compound.
Include the following information as part of your normal diagnosis and repair procedure when
servicing the clutch hydraulic system.

### PROCEDURE

1. Inspect the system to determine which clutch
hydraulic cylinder is leaking.
a. If the slave cylinder is leaking, remove,
clean and overhaul the cylinder.
b. If the master cylinder is leaking, remove
and discard the cylinder.

### 2. Remove and discard the hose that connects

the master cylinder to the slave cylinder.
3. Drain the hydraulic fluid from the cylinder not
removed.
4. Install the replacement master cylinder or the
repaired slave cylinder.
5. Install a replacement master cylinder-toslave cylinder connecting hose. Refer to the
parts list at the end of this I.S. Note for
replacement hose part numbers.

### 6. Refill and bleed the clutch hydraulic system.

Refill the system with AMC/JEEP brake fluid,
P/N 8982 200 215, only.
7. Verify proper clutch operation and that all
hose connections are tight and leak-free.

The shift sleeves used in 1986 Jeep model 228 and Eagle model 128 transfer cases are now available
for service use in prior model 129/229 transfer cases.

### STEERING AND FRONT AXLE

Attention: Workshop, Parts Department
POWER STEERING GEAR SERY1CE UPDATE
This I.S. Note is to advise you of a revision to power steering gear housing service on 1985 Eagle/Jeep
models.
The current Eagle/Jeep mechanical repair manuals all outline a procedure for repairing fluid leaks
from the power steering gear housing ball plug (A). Please be advised that this repair procedure is
not effective on 1985 power steering gear housings. The steering gear assembly must be replaced
if a ball plug leak has developed.

### Leakage from the ball plug (A) can be verified

using the following test procedure.
Ball Plug Leak Test
1. Clean the ball plug area of the housing.
2. Start and operate the engine at idle speed.
3. Have a helper turn the steering wheel to the
full right turn position while you observe the
ball plug area.

### CAUTION: To avoid damaging the power

steering pump or gear, do not hold the wheel
against the right steering stop for more than
5 seconds.
34779
4. Replace the steering gear assembly if ball
plug leakage occurs.

CHECKING 4WHEEL-DRIVE ENGAGEMENT
If a vehicle equipped with a model 128 or 228 transfer case is suspected of not engaging the front
axle when shifted to 4WD, a 4-wheel-drive engagement check should be performed.

### PROCEDURE

Drive the vehicle in the 4WD mode a short
distance to allow the transfer case to engage.
Leave mode selector in the 4WD position. Turn
off engine. If equipped with automatic transmission, place gear selector in park position. If
equipped with manual transmission, shift into
gear

### With the vehicle on level ground, raise the left-

front wheel and attempt to rotate it. If the leftfront wheel cannot be rotated, 4-wheel-drive
engagement is indicated. If the left-front wheel
can be rotated, 4-wheel-drive is not engaged.
A shift control check must be performed.

### Procedures for checking the vacuum controls

and vacuum motors used in the Selec-Trac or
Selec-Drive systems can be found in the transfer
case section of the appropriate M.R. Workshop
Manual.

FLEX PLATE TRIGGER WHEEL SERVICE
On Jeep models with a 2.46L engine and
automatic transmission, the trigger wheel
portion of the flex plate assembly provides the
timing signal for the fuel and ignition systems.

### If the trigger wheel becomes damaged when

removing/installing the engine, transmission, or
torque converter, ignition performance will be
affected. The general result is either rough
engine operation and backfire, or a no-start
condition.
Check for suspected trigger wheel damage as
follows:
• Check trigger wheel radial runout on inner
surface (A) with a dial indicator. Maximum
allowable runout is 0.40 mm (0.016 in).

### Replace the flex plate assembly if runout

exceeds this figure.
• Inspect condition of the timing slot separators
(B) in the trigger wheel. Replace the flex plate
assembly if the separators are dented,
distorted, broken, or bent. Do not attempt to
repair the wheel as the results are usually not
satisfactory.
• Inspect the starter ring gear for damage.

### Replace the flex plate assembly if the ring

gear is loose or the teeth are damaged.

NEW SHIFT LEVER INSTALLATION TOOL
A shift lever installation tool is now available for Jeep models with an AX4-5 or BA 10/5 manual
transmission.
The new tool simplifies installation and ensures positive seating of the shift lever (A) on the stub lever

### (B).

Use the tool as follows:
1. Apply a generous amount of liquid soap to the
inside of the shift lever insulator (A).
2. Position the shift lever on the tranmission stub
shaft (B).
3. Apply a small amount of grease to the tool
threads.

### 4. Install tool J-36044 as shown. Tool may be

installed from the front or rear. Verify that the
lower shoe plate (D) is properly secured to
the stub shaft.
NOTE: On s o m e shift levers, it may be
necessary to reverse the top plate (E) of tool
J-36044.
Copyright © 1986 American Motors Corporation and R6gie Nationale des Usines Renault. All Rights Reserved. Litho in U.S.A.
8980 001 074

### 5. Turn the screw until the shift lever is in locked

position on the stub stjaft. The four dimples
on the inside of the shift lever must seat in the
groove near the top of the stub shaft. The
screw on the tool will become noticeably
easier to turn when the dimples seat into the
lock groove. Do not install the shift lever too
far down on the stub shaft. There should be
approximately 6.35 mm (
1A inch) of stub shaft
exposed when the shift lever is properly
installed.

### 6. Remove tool J-36044 and install the outer

shift lever boot.
NOTE: In some cases it may be necessary to
file (dress) the four edges at the top of the stub
shaft to ease installation.

Attention: Workshop, Parts Department
DISTRIBUTOR ALIGNMENT FLANGE BREAKAGE
When removing distributors from 1986-1987 Wrangler/YJ/Cherokee/Wagoneer/Comanche vehicles
equipped with 2.46L engines and 1987 Cherokee/Wagoneer/Comanche vehicles equipped with
4.0L engines, the timing alignment flange may be found to be broken off from the distributor housing.
It is not necessary to replace the distributor housing for service correction.

### PROCEDURE

NOTE: Perform this procedure with the
distributor removed from the engine.
1. The broken alignment flange can be reattached to the distributor housing using a
two-part epoxy glue, or equivalent.
2. Inspect the distributor holddown clamp. If
there is evidence of contact with the
alignment flange on the bottom side of the
holddown clamp (A), replace the holddown
clamp P/N 317 3227.

### 3. Install a replacement gasket, P/N 318 1288,

at the base of the distributor.
4. Install distributor holddown clamp. Tighten
the retaining bolt to 11-14 N-m (8-10 ft-lbs).
CAUTION: Distributor holddown bolt torque is
critical.

### CRUISE CONTROL/TURN SIGNAL/WIPER LEVER SERVICE

An updated procedure for removing and installing the cruise control/turn signal/wiper lever on
1984-1987 A M C / J E E P vehicles has been developed. The procedure also outlines installation of an
anti-rattle shim on levers not equipped with a shim.
The updated service procedures apply to the following models:
1984-87 Cherokee/Wagoneer
1986-87 Grand Wagoneer
1987 Wrangler/YJ
1986-87 J-10, J-20 Truck
1986-87 C o m a n c h e
1982-87 Eagle

### LEVER REMOVAL - WITH CRUISE CONTROL

1. Disconnect the battery negative cable.
2. On tilt columns, place the steering wheel in
the full up position,
3. Place the combination lever (A) in the right
turn position.
4. On models with the wiper/washer switch
mounted on the lever, turn the wiper/washer
switch to the Off position to align lever tab (B)
with slot (C) in the column switch.

### CAUTION: The column switch will be damaged

if the tab and slot are not aligned during removal.
5. Disconnect the cruise control switch harness
from the main harness. The harness connection is accessible from under the instrument
panel.
6. Attach a fish wire to the cruise control harness
as follows:
*е Use mechanics wire and make it long
enough to guide the harness out of the
column.
€ On Eagle models, tape the fish wire to the
harness connectors.
• On all other models, loop the fish wire
through the s m a l l hole in h a r n e s s
connector (D).

8 . Guide the switch harness out of the steering
(E). To remove the lever, pull it straight out of
column with the fish wire,
the switch.
9. The lever is serviced as an assembly only. Do
C A U T I O N : Do not bend or twist the lever during

### LEVER INSTALLATION - WITH

CRUISE CONTROL
LEVER REMOVAL - WITHOUT
CRUISE CONTROL
1. If a replacement lever is being installed,
attach the fish wire to the cruise control
harness connector(s).
2. Install an anti-rattle shim (F), P/N 8956 002
285, on the lever.

### 3. Guide the cruise control harness into the

column with the fish wire.
4. On Eagle models, install the lever as follows:
Align and start the lever in the column switch.
Then push the lever into the switch in one
continuous motion until it snaps into place.

### 5. On all except Eagle models, install the lever

as follows:
• Hold the washer switch thumb lever (G) in
the Off position to align lever tab (B) and
upper lug (H).
• Start the lever in the column switch (E).
Then push the lever into the switch in one
continuous motion until it snaps into place.

### CAUTION: Be sure lever tab (B) and the two

lugs (H) are aligned with slots (C) and (J) in the
column switch. The switch can be broken if
misalignment occurs during installation.
6. Remove the fish wire and connect the cruise
control harness to the main harness.

### 7. Connect the battery negative cable.

switch. Remove the lever by pulling it straight

CAUTION: Do not bend or twist the lever during
removal. It must be pulled straight out to avoid

285, on the lever.
2. Hold the washer switch in the Off position with
thumb lever (G). Start the lever in the column.

slot (C).
3. Push the lever into the column switch in one
continuous motion until the lever snaps into
place.

NEW FRONT WHEEL BEARING REPLACEMENT PROCEDURES
New service procedures have been developed to replace front wheel bearings on the subject vehicles.
A new special tool set, PN 8980 002 647 is available to remove the bearing assemblies from the
drive hub.

### The new tools are designed for use with an arbor

or hydraulic press and Kent-Moore bearing
remover tool J-22912-01. They must not be used
with any impact tools, such as a slide hammer
or machinist hammer, to remove or install the
bearings (Fig. 1).
NOTE: Some 1980 and 1981 model Eagles were
equipped with ball bearing-type hubs which are
not serviceable and must be replaced as an
assembly only. The non-serviceable bearings
can be readily identified, upon removal, by the
absence of the axle-to-bearing spacer (18),
(Fig. 2).
