IGNITION S Y S T E i - MOTORCRAFT (6-Cyl. Engine)
4.2L DISTRIBUTOR REMOVAL
Unfasten the distributor cap retaining screws.
Remove the distributor cap with the coil and
spark plug wires connected and place aside.

### Disconnect and plug the distributor vacuum

advance hose.
Disconnect the distributor primary wiring
connector.
Scribe a mark on the distributor housing in line
with the tip of the rotor. Scribe a mark on the
distributor housing near the clamp and continue
the scribe mark on the engine block in line with
the distributor housing mark. Note the position of
the rotor and distributor housing in relation to the
surrounding engine components as reference
points for installing the distributor.

### Remove the distributor holddown bolt and

clamp.
Withdraw the distributor carefully from the
engine.
4.2L DISTRIBUTOR INSTALLATION
Clean the distributor mounting area of the
cylinder block.
Install a replacement distributor mounting
gasket in the counterbore of the cylinder block.

### Position the distributor shaft in the cylinder

block. If engine was not rotated while the
distributor was removed, perform the following
procedure:
Align the rotor tip with the mark scribed on the
distributor housing during removal. Turn the
rotor approximately 1/8-turn counterclockwise
past the scribe mark.

### CAUTION: Ensure that the distributor shaft fully

engages the oil pump drive gear shaft. It may be
necessary to slightly rotate (bump) the engine
while applying downward hand force on the
distributor body to fully engage the distributor
shaft with the oil pump drive gear shaft.

### Slide the distributor shaft down into the engine.

Align the scribe mark on the distributor housing
with the corresponding scribe mark on the
cylinder block.
NOTE: It may be necessary to move the rotor
and shaft slightly to start the gear into mesh with
the camshaft gear and to engage the oil pump
drive tang, but the rotor should align with the
scribe mark when the distributor shaft is down in
place.

### Install the distributor holddown clamp and bolt,

but do not tighten the bolt.
If the engine was rotated while the distributor
was removed, it will be necessary to establish
timing according to the following procedure.
Remove the No. 1 spark plug. Hold a finger over
the spark plug hole and rotate the engine until
the compression pressure is felt. Slowly
continue to rotate the engine until the timing
index on the vibration damper pulley aligns with
the top dead center (TDC) mark (0 degree) on
the timing degree scale. Always rotate the
engine in the direction of normal rotation. Do not
turn the engine backward to align the timing
marks.

### Turn the distributor shaft until the rotor tip points

in the direction of the No. 1 terminal in the
distributor cap. Turn the rotor 1/8-turn
counterclockwise past the position of the No. 1
terminal.

### Slide the distributor shaft down into the engine

and position the distributor vacuum advance
mechanism housing in approximately the same
location (in relation to the surrounding engine
components) as when removed. Align the scribe
mark on the distributor housing with the
corresponding scribe mark on the cylinder
block.

### NOTE: It may be necessary to rotate the oil

pump shaft with a long flat-blade screwdriver to
engage the oil pump drive tang, but the rotor
should align with the position of the No. 1
terminal when the distributor shaft is down in
place.
Install the distributor holddown clamp and bolt,
but do not tighten the bolt.

### CAUTION: If the distributor cap is incorrectly

positioned on the distributor housing, the cap or
rotor may be damaged when the engine is
rotated.
Install the distributor cap with the ignition wires
on the distributor housing. Ensure the pickup
coil wire rubber grommet in the distributor
housing aligns with the depression in the
distributor cap and that the cap fits on the rim of
the distributor housing.

### NOTE: Two different diameter screws are used

to retain the distributor cap.
Apply AMC/Jeep Silicone Dielectric Compound,
or equivalent, to the connector terminal blades
and cavities. Connect the distributor primary
wiring connector.
CAUTION: Do not puncture the spark plug wires
or boots to make a connection. Use the proper
adapters.

### Connect a timing lamp to the No. 1 spark plug.

NOTE: The timing case cover has a socket
adjacent to the timing degree scale for use with a
magnetic timing probe. Ignition timing may be
checked by inserting the probe through the
socket until it rests on the vibration damper.

### The probe is calibrated to compensate for the

probe socket location, which is 9.5° ATDC.
Eccentricity of the damper will properly space
the magnetic probe. The timing degrees are
indicated on a meter.
WARNING: Use extreme caution when the
engine is operating. Do not stand in a direct line
with the fan. Do not put hands near the pulleys,
belts, or fan. Do not wear loose clothing.

### Operate the engine at the specified idle RPM

and observe the timing degree scale and index
with a timing lamp. Rotate the distributor
housing as needed to align the timing index on
the vibration damper pulley with the correct
mark on the timing degree scale.

### Refer to the Emission Control Information Label

or to Chapter B - Engines - General Service and
Diagnosis for ignition timing specifications.
When the ignition timing is correct, tighten the
distributor holddown bolt and recheck the timing
to ensure it did not change.

### Disconnect the timing lamp and connect the

vacuum hose to the distributor vacuum advance
mechanism.
4.2L DISTRIBUTOR COMPONENT
REPLACEMENT
When replacing the pickup coil assembly (8),
trigger wheel (3) or vacuum advance
mechanism (9), it is not necessary to remove the
distributor from the engine. It is necessary to
check ignition timing if the pickup coil assembly
or vacuum advance mechanism is replaced.

### Vacuum Advance Mechanism Installation

If a replacement vacuum advance mechanism is
to be installed, calibrate using the following
procedure.
Insert an Allen wrench into the vacuum hose
tube of the original vacuum advance
mechanism. Count the number of clockwise
turns necessary to bottom the adjusting screw.

### Turn the adjusting screw of the replacement

vacuum advance mechanism clockwise to the
bottom. Turn it counterclockwise the same
number of turns counted earlier.
Install the vacuum advance mechanism on the
distributor housing. Ensure that the link is
engaged on the pin of the pickup coil. Install the
retaining screws. Tighten the base plate screws,
if loosened.

### Check the ignition timing and adjust, if required.

Connect the vacuum hose to the vacuum
advance mechanism.
Remove the attaching screws and remove the
vacuum advance mechanism from the
distributor housing. It is necessary to tilt the unit
to disengage the link from the pickup coil pin

ELECTRICAL
IGNITION SYSTEM - MOTORCRAFT (6-Cyl. Engine)
Rotor
A unique feature of the SSI system is the silicone
applied to the rotor blade during manufacture.
Radio interference is greatly reduced by the
presence of a small quantity of silicone dielectric
compound on the rotor blade. After a few
thousand miles, this compound becomes
charred (1) by the high voltage current flowing
through the rotor. This is normal. Do not scrape
the residue from the rotor blade.

### When installing a replacement rotor, apply a thin

coat 0.75 - 3mm (0.03-in - 0.12-in) of AMC/Jeep
Silicone Dielectric Compound, or equivalent, to
the tip of the rotor blade.

GENERAL INFORMATION

### The ignition switch is mounted on the steering

column and is connected to the key lock
assembly by a remote lock rod.
IGNITION SWITCH REMOVAL
Remove the lower instrument panel trim panel.
Place the key lock in the OFF - LOCK position.
Remove the two ignition switch attaching
screws.

### Disconnect the ignition switch from the remote

rod.
Disconnect the black harness connector.
Disconnect the white harness connector.
Remove the ignition switch from the steering
column.
IGNITION SWITCH TESTING
To test the ignition switch circuitry and
continuity, place the slide bar in the position to
be tested and use either an ohmmeter or

### Continuity Light J-21008, or equivalent.

Ignition Switch Positions
Starting from the alignment hole end of the
ignition switch, the switch positions are:
• ACCESSORY
• OFF - LOCK
• OFF
• ON and START.
Each position has a detent stop except START
which is spring loaded to released.

### Electrical Resistance

No electrical resistance should be indicated
(test lamp ON) between two connected
terminals.
Maiimum Voltage Drop
The maximum voltage drop between any two
connected terminals should not exceed 12.5
millivolts per amp.

### For example: if a 10-amp load is drawn through

the switch, the maximum voltage drop should be
10 x 0.0125 or 0.125 volt.
The ignition switch slide bar positions can be
easily identified by first locating the alignment
hole which is found in the flat portion of the
ignition switch adjacent to the terminals.

MAIN HARNESS CONNECTOR
The main wiring harness connector is located at
the left upper corner of the dash panel. This
connector is made up of the engine and forward
lamp harness at the engine compartment and
the fuse and instrument panel harness at the
passenger compartment side.

### The connector can be removed from the dash

panel by removing the center bolt from the
engine compartment side and the two attaching
screws from the driver's side.
CAUTION: Be careful not to bend the male
spade terminals when removing or installing the
connector. The center of the connector is filled
with a non-conductive grease to prevent
corrosion of the terminals.

### If any wires are replaced on the engine

compartment side, the terminal opening must be
resealed with a durable waterproof sealer.
CAUTION: Do not use string-type body caulk as
a sealer.
FUSIBLE LINKS
General Information
Fusible links are harness wires covered with a
special non-flammable insulation. The links
protect circuits which are not normally fused due
to carrying high amperage loads or because of
their location in the chassis.

### Fusible links are used to prevent major harness

damage in the event a short circuit, short to
ground, or overload condition occurs.
Fusible links are located in the engine
compartment next to the starter solenoid/relay.
Fusible Link Values
Each fusible link is of a fixed value for the
specific load.

### Fusible Link Replacement Parts

Replacement fusible links are listed in the Parts
Catalog.
Fusible Link Failure Diagnosis
Failure of a fusible link is often caused by a
grounded circuit.
Therefore, the cause of the failure must be
determined prior to installing a new link.

### Fusible Link Renewal

Disconnect the battery negative cable.
Follow one end of the link to the terminal end.
Follow the remaining end to the wire harness.
Determine which circuit(s) may have caused the
failure using the Electrical Troubleshooting

### Manual (ETM).

Cut the harness wire below the fusible link mold.
Strip the insulation.
C-106
ELECTRICAL
CHASSIS WIRING HARNESS
Fusible Link installation
Fasten the correct fusible link using a splice clip.
Solder and cover with several layers of heat
shrinking tubing.

### Apply petroleum jelly to tubing ends.

Connect negative battery cable.
NOTE: The solder joint MUST be made with
rosin core solder ONLY. DO NOT use acid or
acid core solder. Protect the harness wires from
damage when soldering.

HEADLAMP AIMING PROCEDURE
Headlamps must be aimed on low beam. They
may be aimed either with mechanical aimers, or,
by using a screen.

### Use Headlamp Aimer J-25300-A following the

instructions supplied with the equipment, for
proper aiming.
If a screen is to be used, preparation for aiming
is as follows:
Locate the vehicle in a darkened area with a
level floor and with the screen (wall) having a
nonreflecting white surface.

### Mark a reference line on the floor 7.5 meters

(25 ft) away from, and parallel to, the screen.
Attach the four trim ring screws (A).

Position the vehicle perpendicular (at a right
angle) to the screen and with the headlamps
directly over the reference line 25 feet from the
wall.

### Locate the middle tape on the screen so it is

aligned with the centerline of the vehicle.
Equalize all tire pressures.
Rock the vehicle from side to side to equalize the
springs and shock absorbers.
Measure the distance between the vehicle
headlamp centers.

### Position the marker tapes vertically on the

screen to the right and left of the middle tape at
half this distance.
Measure the distance from the center of each
lamp to the surface on which the vehicle rests.
Position the marker tape horizontally on the
screen to cross the vertical tapes at the
measured height of each lamp center
respectively.

### Clean the headlamps.

Turn the headlamps on LOW beam.
NOTE: Cover the lamp not being aimed.
Turn the screw counterclockwise until the top
edge of the high intensity area is even with the
horizontal line.
Turn the horizontal adjusting screw (B)
clockwise until the beam is off the centering
tape.

### Turn the same screw counterclockwise until the

left edge of the high intensity area is 10.2cm
(2-in) to the right of the lamp centerline.
Cover the lamp that has been aimed and aim the
other lamp using the same procedure.

### DIRECTIONAL SIGNAL SWITCH DIAGNOSIS

• loose connections, and,
• burned out lamps.
A flashing rate, approximately twice the normal
rate, usually indicates a lamp has shorted in
the circuit.
If a three-lamp flasher is installed in a vehicle
having only two lamps per side, the lamps will
light but will not flash.

### If a two-lamp flasher is used on a vehicle having

three lamps (trailer towing), the higher current
draw will cause the lamps to flash too fast.
If there is no signal at any front, rear, or indicator
lamp, check the fuse.
If the fuse is not defective, substitute a flasher
which is known as not defective.

### If the replacement flasher does not remedy the

problem, check the signal system wiring
connections at the fuse and at the steering
column connector.
If the brake stoplamps function properly, the rear
signal lamps are not defective.
NOTE: The directional signal flasher is attached
directly to the fuse panel.

ELECTRIC WISHER PUiP ASSE11LY
General Information
The electric washer pump assembly is mounted
in the water reservoir. The impeller motor case is
grounded to the body sheet metal by a black
(BLK) ground wire. It is energized by a violet
(VIO W/TR) feed wire.

### Diagnosis

Refer to the Electrical Troubleshooting Manual
(ETM) for diagnostic information.
INTERMITTENT GOVERNOR DIAGNOSTIC
TESTING
Remove the intermittent governor wiper
module.
Connect the intermittent governor wiper module
connectors together.

### To determine if the delay is defective, rotate the

wiper switch in that mode and measure the
resistance between A-D and A-G, (wiper switch
disconnected).
If the resistance is not 0-500K OHMS, replace
the wiper switch as outlined in the Steering
Column Section.

### If resistance is correct, replace the module.

NOTE: The intermittent circuit is the same as the
nonintermittent circuit when the module is
removed.
Refer to the Electrical Troubleshooting Manual
(ETM) for further testing. (A "How-toTroubleshoot" section is located in the front of
the ETM.)

### Test for:

• If the wipers operate in the low and high speed
modes, and the washer is working, then the
intermittent wiper module is defective.
• If the wipers operate in the low and high speed
modes, and the washer is working, then the
delay resistance in the wiper switch is
defective.

### C-132

ELECTRICAL
REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER
GENERAL INFORMATION
To defog the rear window, press the rocker
switch to the ON position. A light on the rocker
switch arm will indicate that the defogger is
operating.

### Defogger operation will normally cease after

about ten minutes. Pushing the switch again will
give five additional minutes of defogger
operation.
To stop defogger operation, push the switch to
the OFF position.
Use the defogger only when the engine is
operating to prevent excessive battery drain.

### CAUTION: Use care when washing the inside of

the rear window to prevent damage to the
defogger heating elements. Use a soft cloth and
a mild washing solution. Wiping motions should
be parallel to the heating elements. Also, keep
all objects a safe distance from the window to
prevent damaging the heating elements.

### Refer to the Electrical Troubleshooting Manual

(ETM) for rear window defogger additional
diagnostic information.

Squeeze the ends of the switch to release the

REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER GRID TEST
When a grid is inoperable due to an open circuit,
the area of glass normally cleared by that grid
remains fogged or iced unless, and until, it is
cleared by the adjacent grids.

### The feed wire is connected to the left (driver)

side of the window and the grounding terminal is
behind the left taillamp assembly.
C-133
ELECTRICAL
REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER
SEE
I.S.
N
O
T
E
S
With the engine running at IDLE, push the rear
window defogger switch to the ON position and
release. The pilot lamp in the rocker switch
should light, indicating defogger operation.

### Use a 12-vdc voltmeter and contact the positive

lead of the voltmeter to the feed side vertical bus
element on the inside surface of the glass and
contact the negative lead to the ground side bus
element. Voltage on the meter should be 11 to
13 volts. Connect the negative lead of the
voltmeter to a good ground; the metal reading
should be constant.

### Keep the negative lead connected to ground.

Use the positive lead and carefully contact each
grid at the approximate centerline of the window.
A voltage drop of one-half the full amount,
approximately 6 volts, indicates a good grid or
closed circuit.

### A voltage drop of 12 volts at the centerline

indicates a break in the grid between the positive
voltmeter lead and the ground.
No voltage drop (0 volts) at the centerline
indicates a break in the grid between the
centerline and the voltage source or lead.
85041

### The exact location of the break can then be

pinpointed by moving the positive voltmeter lead
to the left or right along the grid until an abrupt
change in the voltage reading is noticed. The
break is at that point in the grid.
REAR WINDOW DEFOiGER GRID REPAIR

### Locate the broken or open grid.

Use the grid repair kit (available as a service
part) in accordance with the following procedure:
• Mark the location of the broken or open grid on
the exterior surface of the glass using a
suitable marking pencil.
• Lightly rub the area to be repaired (inside the
rear window) using fine steel wool. Clean the
area with alcohol.

### Attach two strips of cellophane tape to the inside

surface of the rear window (above and below the
break in the grid).

IN GRID
TAPE

### C-134

ELECTRICAL
REAR WINDOW DEFOGGER
Mix the repair coating until it is uniform in
consistency, with silver particles mixed
throughout the fluid, and apply the coating to the
break in the grid with a small brush furnished
with the kit. Apply a heavy coat of mixture,
extending approximately 6mm (1/4-in) on each
side of the break.

### Start the engine.

Depress the rear window defogger switch.
Run engine for one minute.
Turn ignition switch OFF.
Apply a second heavy coat of the mixture to the
break in the grid. Extend it about 6mm (1 /4-in) on
either side of the break.

### Start the engine.

Depress the rear window defogger switch.
Run the engine until the defogger completes a
cycle (pilot light goes off).
Turn the ignition switch OFF.
Remove the tape from the inside of the rear
window.
Check the repair grid for continuity.

### CAUTION: Do not touch or clean the repaired

area for 24 hours.
Clean the inside of the rear window, with the
exception of the repaired area, with liquid
window cleaner.
Clean the pencil markings from the exterior
surface of the glass.
NOTE: Apply a coat of tincture of iodine on
approximately 2.5cm (1 -in) of either side of the
repaired area should the repaired area of the
grid appear off-color after performing the repair
procedure. Use a fine brush or pipe cleaner.

### Allow the iodine to dry for about 30 seconds and

carefully wipe off the excess with a lint free cloth.

CRUISE CONTROL OPERATION

### Cruise control operation is limited to speeds

WARNING: Do not use the cruise control
feature when driving on slippery or congested
roads.

To diagnose Cruise Control system malfunctions, refer to the Service Diagnosis Chart

### CRUISE CONTROL DIAGNOSIS

General Information
Whenever a cruise control malfunction occurs,
first verify that the cruise control wire harness is
properly connected to the module before starting normal diagnosis and repair procedures.

### A poor connection can cause a complete or

intermittent malfunction and is also the only
nontestable connection in the circuit. This
connection is disturbed whenever the AM
PC-1-R Cruise Control Tester, P/N 8180 320
315, is used.
For this reason, a loose connection may be
misdiagnosed as a module malfunction. Also,
whenever a module is replaced, it will be
necessary to adjust the replacement module.

### CRUISE CONTROL DIAGNOSTIC

TESTING EXPLANATION
LAMP NO. 1 OFF - Set Switch
• Check voltage from HAZ/STOP and inline
fuses at terminal 14 (DK GRN), (cruise switch
ON) to ground terminal 1 (BLK).
LAMP NO. 2 OFF - Cruise Switch/Speed Sensor
• Check voltage from HAZ/STOP and inline
fuses at terminal 5 (BRN), cruise switch ON, to
ground 1 (BLK).
• Check resistance between terminals 2 (GRY)
and 3 (BLU), 15-50 ohms.

### LAMP NO. 3 OFF - Brake Lamp(s) Ground

• With ignition ON, jumper terminals 7 (VIO
W/TR) and 13 (LT BLU W/TR); if brake lamps
do not turn ON, check gauges fuses and brake
switch connections.
LAMP NO* 4 OFF - Throttle Position
Feedback Sensor
• Check voltage from gauges fuse (ignition ON)
at terminal 7 (VIO W/TR) to ground terminal 1

### (BLK).

• Check resistance between terminal 2 (GRY)
and 11 (TAN) 240-4K ohms. 280-430 ohms =
idle. 4K (4000) ohms - wide open throttle.
LAMP NO. S OFF - Resume/Accelerate /
Vent Valve
• Check voltage from HAZ/STOP and inline
fuses (cruise switch at Resume/Accelerate) at
terminal 10 (YEL) to ground terminal 1 (BLK).
• Check resistance between terminals 6 (WHT)
and 12 (ORN), 30-50 ohms.
• Terminals 6 (WHT) and 12 (ORN) to ground
must have infinite resistance, (OPEN).

### LAMP NO. 6 OFF - Resume/Accelerate /

Charge Valve
• Check voltage from HAZ/STOP and inline
fuses (cruise switch at R/A) at terminal 10
(YEL) to ground terminal 1 (BLK).
• Check resistance between terminals 4 (RED)
and 12 (ORN), 30-50 ohms.
• Terminals 4 (RED) and 12 (ORN) to ground
must have infinite resistance, (OPEN).

### Cruise Control Servo Checks

• Check servo cable for breaks and hook-up.
• Check engine vacuum can and hose
connections (small hose).
• Pinch brake vent (large hose) at servo and
repeat test.
If servo operates, adjust brake vent hose valve
(on brake sled).

### If hose is kinked, check routing. If it is cut,

replace with new harness.

Cruise Control Module Adjustments
The cruise control module adjustments are preset by the manufacturer. If all other components
of the system appear to be functioning normally
and the cruise control remains inoperative,
perform the following adjustments to determine
if the module is functional.

### CAUTION: The adjustments are extremely

delicate. Insert the screwdriver into the slots
VERY CAREFULLY. Do not push hard or turn
hard against the stops. The arms have a
maximum turning angle of 270 degrees (threequarter turn).
Verify if the cruise control module is defective by
using the indicated settings:

### Centering Adjustment

Turn the centering adjustment to the 10 o'clock
position (A).
Low Speed Switch Adjustment
Turn the low speed switch adjustment to the
10 o'clock position (B).
Sensitivity Adjustment
Turn the sensitivity adjustment full clockwise

### (C).

NOTE: The adjustments may not be precisely
correct for the vehicle, but are acceptable to
determine if the module is functioning. The need
for more precise adjustments can be
determined by a road test.
C

### O O Q

A
B
C
If the adjustments have no effect on the cruise
control operation, replace the cruise control
module.
NOTE: The cruise control module is the only
component of the system that cannot be isolated
and tested separately. It must be tested while
connected to the other components of the
system.

CLUTCH
GENERAL INFORMATION
CLUTCH COMPONENTS
The clutch assembly consists of a driven plate
and diaphragm-type clutch cover actuated by a
hydraulic system.
Clutch Cover and Driven Plate
A single, dry-disc driven plate and a diaphragm
style clutch cover are used. The cover has a
one-piece, circular diaphragm spring with integral release fingers. The driven plate friction
material is riveted to the hub which contains
four cushion springs.

### Driven plate and cover diameter is 266 mm

(10.5-in) on six-cylinder models and 232 mm
(9.28-in) on four-cylinder models.
Clutch Hydraulic System
Two hydraulic cylinders are used in the system.
The throwout bearing, disc and pressure plate
are operated by a slave cylinder. The slave cylinder is operated by the master cylinder which
is connected to the clutch pedal.

### The slave cylinder is mounted inside the clutch

housing. The master cylinder is mounted on the
engine compartment side of the dash panel.
System hydraulic fluid is contained in the
master cylinder reservoir. Fluid level is indicated on the side of the reservoir.

### Use only Jeep brake fluid, or equivalent marked

SAE J-1703 or DOT 3, in the clutch hydraulic
system.
Slave Cylinder and Throwout Bearing Assembly
The slave cylinder and throwout bearing are a
unique one-piece design. The bearing is permanently attached to the cylinder piston.

### The slave cylinder completely encircles the

transmission input shaft. In operation, piston
movement causes the throwout bearing to
move in a linear (straight line) direction. The
cylinder is attached to the transmission front
case.

CLUTCH COVER AND DRIVEN PLATE
REMOVAL
Remove the transmission and transfer case as
outlined in Chapter E.
CAUTION: The clutch cover is under considerable spring tension. The cover bolts must be
loosened evenly and in rotation to avoid distorting the cover.

### Loosen the clutch cover bolts evenly and in ro-

tation to relieve spring tension on the cover.
Loosen the bolts a few threads at a time only.
Remove the cover bolts and remove the cover
(1) and driven plate (2).
On six-cylinder models, remove the lubricating
wick from the pilot bushing bore. Soak the wick
in engine oil.
101260

### CLUTCH COVER AND DRIVEN PLATE

INSTALLATION
On six-cylinder models, squeeze excess oil
from the pilot bushing lubricating wick and insert the wick into the pilot bushing bore.
NOTE: Avoid getting oil from the wick on the
flywheel clutch surface.

### Insert the clutch plate alignment tool in the driv-

en plate hub. Use tool J 5824-01 on four-cylinder models and tool J 33169 on six-cylinder
models.
Insert the alignment tool in the pilot bushing
bore and position the driven plate on the flywheel surface.

### Position the clutch cover over the driven plate

and on the flywheel.
Install the clutch cover attaching bolts finger
tight only.
CAUTION: The clutch cover bolts must be tightened correctly to avoid distorting the cover.
Tighten the bolts only as outlined to prevent
possible cover distortion.

### Tighten each cover bolt evenly and in rotation a

few threads at a time.
Final tighten the cover bolts. On four-cylinder
models, tighten the bolts to 31 N^m (23 ft-lbs)
torque. On six-cylinder models, tighten the
bolts to 54 N«m (40 ft-lbs) torque.
Install the transmission and transfer case as
outlined in Chapter E.
D-4

### CLUTCH

CLUTCH SERVICE
PILOT BUSHING REPLACEMENT
Remove the transmission and transfer case as
outlined in Chapter E.
Remove the clutch cover and driven p'ate as
outlined in this section.
On six-cylinder models, remove the pilot bushing lubricating wick. Soak the wick in engine oil.

### Remove the bushing with puller J 5822 and

slide hammer J 2619-01.
CAUTION: The replacement bushing can be
damaged if misaligned during installation. Keep
the bushing parallel with the crankshaft centerline to avoid damage.
Install the replacement pilot bushing in the
crankshaft bore. Use tool J 5824-01 on fourcylinder models or tool J 33169 on six-cylinder
models.

### On six-cylinder models, squeeze excess oil

from the pilot bushing lubricating wick and insert the wick into the pilot bushing bore.

mounting studs on the dash panel.
Remove the cylinder.

Position the cylinder on the dash panel mounting studs.
Install and tighten the cylinder attaching nuts on

equivalent labeled SAE 1703 or DOT 3, only.

bleed the hydraulic system. Refer to the bleeding procedure outlined in this section.

CLUTCH HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FLUID
The only fluid recommended for use in the
clutch hydraulic system is Jeep brake fluid, or
equivalent labeled SAE 1703 or DOT 3. Use
recommended fluids only. Never use previously
drained fluid or fluid that has been stored in an
open container.

### CLUTCH HYDRAULIC SYSTEM BLEEDING

Fill the master cylinder with the specified brake
fluid.
Raise the vehicle.
Attach one end of a bleed hose to the bleed
screw (12) on the slave cylinder bleed line (2).
Insert the other end of the bleed hose in a glass
container partially filled with brake fluid. Be sure
the hose end is completely submerged in the
brake fluid.

Carefully loosen the bleed screw (12). Hold the
bleed screw fitting firmly to prevent it from turning while loosening the screw. Do not allow the
bleed line (2) to bend or flex when loosening the
screw.

### Have a helper press and hold the clutch pedal

to the floor.
Tighten the bleed screw and have the helper
release the clutch pedal.
Check master cylinder fluid level. Add fluid if
necessary. Do not allow the cylinder reservoir
to run out of fluid during bleeding operations.

### Repeat the bleeding process until fluid entering

the glass container is free of bubbles.
NOTE: Be sure the bleed hose end remains
submerged in brake fluid during bleeding
operations.
Lower the vehicle.
Fill the clutch master cylinder to the correct
level.

### CLUTCH HYDRAULIC SYSTEM FLUID LEVEL

The system fluid is contained in the clutch
master cylinder reservoir.
The correct fluid level is indicated on the side of
the cylinder reservoir.
Do not overfill the reservoir and use specified
fluids only.

GENERAL INFORMATION
MANUAL TRANSMISSION
Wrangler/YJ vehicles are equipped with either
the Model BA 10/5 or the AX-5, five-speed
manual transmission depending on engine type.

### Model AX-5 is used in four-cylinder models.

Model BA 10/5 is used in six-cylinder models.
Both transmissions are synchromesh units with
fully synchronized gear changing. Fifth gear is
an overdrive range in both transmission models. A top mounted shift lever is used for both
models.

### TRANSFER CASE

The Model 207 transfer case is used for all engine/transmission applications in Wrangler/YJ
models.
The Model 207 is a part-time, four wheel drive
unit with three operating ranges plus a Neutral
position. A built in low range gear system provides a 2.6:1 reduction ratio for increased low
speed torque capability. The three transfer case
operating ranges are: Two-wheel high, fourwheel high and four-wheel low. Operating
range is selected with a floor mounted shift
lever.

### Two-wheel high range is for on-road, highway

operation. The four-wheel drive ranges are for
off-road operation or when the vehicle is driven
on paved road surfaces covered by snow, ice,
or similar low traction elements.
A synchronizer assembly in the transfer case
allows the unit to be shifted between while the
vehicle is in motion.

GENERAL SERVICE INFORMATION
This section covers removal, installation and lubrication procedures for model AX-5 and BA
10/5 manual transmissions.
The procedures, specifications and special
tools needed to overhaul the Model 207 transfer case are contained in the B.V. AX-4/5 and

### B.V. BA 10/5 Component Service Manuals

respectively.
Transmission Identification
AX-5 Identification
The eight digit AX-5 identification code (1) is
stamped on the bottom surface of the transmission case next to the intermediate plate. The
first number is year of manufacture (e.g. 5 =
1985, 6 = 1986). The second and third numbers
indicate month of manufacture (e.g. 01 = January, 02 = February, etc.). The next series of
numbers is the transmission serial number.
101278

### BA 10/5 Identification

The BA 10/5 identification plate (A) is attached
to the passenger side of the transmission front
case. The Jeep identification/part number is on
the top line of the plate. The manufacturers
reference number is on the middle line and the
transmission serial number is on the lower line.
101060

Forward speed gear ratios for the AX-5 and BA
10/5 transmissions are as follows:

The Model 207 transfer case is used for all engine/transmission applications in Wrangler/YJ
models.

NOTE: Be sure to align the propeller shaft
yokes with the axle yokes according to the reference marks made during removal.
Install the rear crossmember. Tighten the
crossmember-to-frame bolts to 41 NеН (30 ftlbs) torque. Tighten the rear support-to-crossmember bolts to 45 Hm (33 ft-lbs) torque.

Fill the transfer case with Jeep Quadra-Trac
lubricant.
Adjust the transfer case shift linkage. Refer to
the procedure in this section.
Lower the vehicle.

Raise the vehicle.
Loosen the lock bolt (2) on adjusting trunnion
(3) just enough to allow linkage rod (4) to slide
freely in the trunnion.

Model 207 transfer case is to the bottom edge

a two-piece fill plug, correct fill level is to the

### GENERAL INFORMATION

GENERAL SERVICE INFORMATION
The Model 999, three speed, automatic transmission is used in Wrangler/YJ models.
This section covers removal, installation, lubrication and in-vehicle service and adjustment
procedures for the Model 999 automatic
transmission.

### The procedures, specifications and special

tools needed to overhaul the Model 999 transmission are contained in the T.A. 700/900 Component Service Manual.
TRANSMISSION COMPONENTS
The Model 999 is a three speed, automatic
transmission with a compound planetary gear
system. A shift lever and linkage is used to select desired drive range. Transmission shift
points are controlled by an externally mounted
throttle linkage. The transmission case and
converter housing are a one-piece aluminum
casting. An aluminum adapter housing connects the transmission to the transfer case
models.

### The Model 999 has two multiple disc clutches

(3-4), two bands and actuating servos (7-18), an
overrunning clutch (8) and two planetary gear
sets (5-6). These components provide one reverse and three forward gear ranges. The planetary gear sets (5-6) are connected by a common sun gear. The sun gear is interconnected
to the multiple disc clutches through the driving
shell (16) which is splined to the sun gear and
front clutch retainer.

### The hydraulic system consists of a single oil

pump (2), a valve body (15) containing the pressure regulatingshift control valves, a governor
valve (9), two servos and a three element torque converter.
The transmission fluid is cooled by circulating
the fluid through an external cooler built into the
radiator lower tank. Transmission fluid is
filtered by a Dacron element filter attached to
the valve body.

### The transmission is vented through a passage

drilled into the upper portion of the oil pump
housing.

TRANSMISSION IDENTIFICATION
A seven-digit part number (1) is stamped on the
left side of the case just above the oil pan surface. This number is followed by a four-digit
code number (2) which indicates date of manufacture. The final four-digit number group (3) is
the transmission serial number.
84071

### TORQUE CONVERTER IDENTIFICATION

The torque converter has an identification decal
attached to the converter. The decal indicates
converter type and stall ratio. The letters LS
indicate a low stall converter. The letters HS
indicate a high stall converter.

### Torque Converter Service

The torque converter cannot be disassembled
for repair. The converter must be replaced as
an assembly if diagnosis reveals a malfunction.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

### PRELIMINARY DIAGNOSIS

The preliminary diagnosis is the first step in the
diagnostic sequence. Two basic procedures
are involved. The first procedure is for vehicles
that are driveable. The second procedure is for
vehicles that will not back up or move forward.

### Vehicle Is Driveable

Verify engine operating condition.
Check transmission fluid level and condition.
Adjust the throttle and gearshift linkage before
road testing if the complaint was based on
delayed, erratic, or harsh shifts.

### Perform a stall test if the complaint was based

on sluggish, low-speed acceleration or abnormal throttle opening requirements to maintain
highway speeds.
Road test the vehicle and analyze the results.
Refer to Road Test and Road Test Analysis in
this section.

### Perform hydraulic and air pressure tests if road

test analysis indicates this is necessary.
Vehicle Will Not Back Up or Move Forward
Verify proper engine operation.
Check transmission fluid level and condition.
Check for broken or disconnected throttle
linkage.

### Check for broken cooler lines and loose or

missing pressure test port plugs.
Raise the vehicle, start the engine and shift the
transmission into gear.
• If the propeller shafts turn but the wheels do
not, the problem is in the differential or axle
shafts.
• If the propeller shafts do not turn and the
transmission is noisy, stop the engine. Remove the transmission oil pan and check for
debris. If debris is not present, remove the
transmission and check for a damaged drive
plate, drive plate bolts, converter hub, input
or output shaft, or oil pump.
• If the propeller shafts do not turn and the
transmission is not noisy, perform a hydraulic pressure test to determine if the problem
is related to a hydraulic or mechanical
component.

### FLUID LEVEL AND CONDITION

Check fluid level and condition as follows.
WARNING: Keep hands or loose articles of
clothing away from the fan, accessory drive
belts or other rotating engine parts. Contact
with rotating or hot engine components can result in personal injury.

### Drive the vehicle until the transmission fluid is

at normal operating temperature of approximately 79.4°C (175°F).
NOTE: Avoid inaccurate fluid level readings. Do
not check fluid level until the fluid is at normal
operating temperature.

### DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Shift the transmission into Neutral.
Apply the parking brakes.
Operate the engine at curb idle speed.
Clean the transmission filler cap and tube
before removing the dipstick.
Remove the transmission dipstick and check
fluid level. Correct fluid level is between the

### ADD and FULL marks on the dipstick.

Adjust fluid level if necessary.
NOTE: If fluid level was abnormally low, check
the transmission for leaks.
Check condition of the fluid. The fluid should be
dark red in color and free of dirt or debris.
w If the fluid is discolored or smells burned, but
the transmission operates correctly, replace
the fluid and filter.
# If the fluid is badly discolored, burned and
contains metal or friction material particles
and shift problems were experienced, overhaul may be required.

### Stop the engine and seat the dipstick in the fill

tube after checking fluid level.
NOTE: A low fluid level allows the pump to take
in air along with the fluid. Aerated fluid causes
low pressures and delayed shifts. If the transmission is overfilled, the fluid will churn into
foam causing the same conditions. In either
case, air in the fluid will cause overheating, oxidation and varnish buildup. Foaming can also
result in fluid escaping from the transmission
vent where it may be mistaken for a leak.

### Fluid condition must also be checked. When the

fluid is dark, smells burnt or is contaminated
with metal or friction material particles, overhaul
may be necessary. Examine the fluid on the
dipstick closely. After checking fluid level and
condition, seat the dipstick fully to seal out
water and dirt.

### LINKAGE ADJUSTMENT

Correct transmission throttle and gearshift
linkage adjustment is important to proper operation. Misadjusted linkage can cause shift
problems and premature wear of transmission
components.
Throttle Linkage

### The throttle (TV) linkage positions a valve that

controls shift speed, quality and timing. If adjustment is too short, early shifts and slippage
between shifts may occur. If adjustment is too
long, shifts may be delayed and part throttle
downshifts may be very sensitive.

### Gearshift Linkage

The gearshift linkage positions the manual
valve in the valve body. Incorrect adjustment
will cause creeping in Neutral, premature clutch
wear, delayed engagement in any gear, or a nostart condition.

### Gearshift Linkage Check

Proper operation of the neutral start switch will
provide a quick check of linkage adjustment as
follows.
F-S

starter operates, Neutral position is correct and
the linkage is properly adjusted.

### NOTE: If the starter fails to operate in Park or

Neutral, or if the gearshift lever had to be
moved back and forth to start the engine,
linkage adjustment is required.

ROAD TEST
Before road testing, be sure the fluid level,
throttle and gearshift linkage adjustments have
been checked and corrected if necessary.

### Observe engine performance during the test (an

engine malfunction will effect transmission operation). Operate the transmission in all gearshift positions and check for slippage or shift
variations. Note if shifts are harsh or spongy,
and record the speeds at which up-and-down
shifts occur.

### Watch closely for slippage or engine speed

flare-up which indicates clutch, band or overrunning clutch problems. If the condition is advanced, the transmission may not shift into one
or more drive ranges.
The Clutch and Band Application Chart provides a basis for analyzing road test results. A

### Analyzing Road Test Results

Refer to the Clutch and Band Application Chart.
Note what elements are applied in the various
gear ranges. The rear clutch is applied in all
forward ranges (D, 2,1). The overrunning clutch
is applied in first gear D and 2 range only. The
rear band is applied in 1 and R range only.

### For example, if slippage occurs in D and 2

range first gear but not in 1 range, the overrunning clutch is slipping. Similarly, if slippage occurs in any two forward gears, the rear clutch is
slipping.
Applying the same method of analysis, note
that both clutches are applied in D third gear
only. If slippage occurs in third gear, either the
front or rear clutch is slipping. By selecting another gear which does not use one of these

### F-10

AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
4#
DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING
4#
elements, the slipping clutch can be determined. For example, if slippage also occurs in
reverse, the front clutch is slipping. If the transmission does not slip in reverse, the rear clutch
is slipping.

### NOTE: Although road test analysis will identify

the slipping element, the actual cause of a malfunction usually cannot be determined until hydraulic and air pressure tests are performed.
Do not disassemble the transmission until hydraulic and air pressure tests have been
performed.

### HYDRAULIC PRESSURE TEST

The hydraulic pressure test is performed with
Test Set J 24027. The set consists of five colorcoded pressure hoses, a 2 758 kPa (400 psi)
capacity high pressure gauge and a 689 kPa
(100 psi) capacity low pressure gauge.

### The high pressure gauge is used to record rear

servo pressure in R and 1 positions only. The
low pressure gauge is used for all other
readings.
The test set permits simultaneous connection
to all the pressure ports for sequential or independent pressure readings.

### Pressure Test Port Location/Connection

The accumulator line pressure port (1) is on the
right side of the case between the front and rear
servo castings. Connect the blue hose (A) to
this port.
The governor pressure port (2) is in the lower
center section of the adapter housing. Connect
the black hose (B) to this port.

### Lubrication pressure is measured by installing a

T-fitting in the fluid cooler return line. The line is
attached to the fitting (3) on the left rear edge of
the case. Connect the white hose (C) to the
cooler line.
The front servo release pressure port (4) is on
the right side of the case just behind the filler
tube opening. Connect the yellow hose (D) to
this port.

### The rear servo apply pressure port (5) is on the

right side of the case just above the oil pan.
Connect the red hose (E) here.

Hydraulic Pressure Test Procedure
Before testing, check and adjust the fluid level
and linkage.

### Connect a tachometer to the engine.

Raise the vehicle on a hoist that will allow the
wheels to rotate freely.
Connect the test gauge hoses to the appropriate pressure ports.
Test One
Test one checks pump output, pressure regulator valve operation, front/rear clutch and oil filter condition. It measures transmission operating pressure at the accumulator and front servo
pressure ports in D range.

### Turn the test gauge selector handle to line pres-

sure position.
Start and operate the engine at idle speed.
Move the gearshift lever to D range and note
line pressure. Pressure should be 372 to 414
kPa (54 to 60 psi).
Increase engine rpm to 1600 and slowly move
the valve body throttle lever fully forward, then
fully rearward. With the throttle lever in the forward position, pressure should be 372 to 414
kPa (54 to 60 psi) and gradually increase to 648
kPa (94 psi) as the lever is moved rearward.

### Turn the test gauge selector to front servo ap-

ply position.
Operate the engine at 1000 rpm. Allow the
transmission to upshift into third gear and note
servo pressure. Pressure should not vary from
previous line pressure by more than 21 kPa (3
psi).

### Slowly move the throttle linkage to full throttle

position and note servo pressure prior to and
after transmission downshift. Servo pressure
12
AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING
should increase then drop to 0 psi after
downshift.
Slowly move the valve body throttle lever fully
forward then fully rearward. In the toward position, pressure should be 372 to 414 kPa (54 to
60 psi) and 621 to 662 kPa (90 to 96 psi) as the
lever is moved rearward.

### Test Two

This test checks pump output, pressure regulation, and front clutch/rear servo condition by
comparing operating pressures at the rear servo and accumulator pressure ports in ranges 1
and 2.
Turn the test gauge selector to line pressure
position.

### Move the gearshift lever to 1 range and operate

the engine at 1000 rpm.
Slowly move the valve body throttle lever fully
forward then fully rearward. In the forward position, pressure should be 372 to 414 kPa (54 to
60 psi) and gradually increase to 621 to 662 kPa
(90 to 96 psi) as the lever is moved rearward.

### Turn the test gauge selector handle to the rear

servo apply position.
Operate the engine at 1000 rpm.
Slowly move the valve body throttle lever fully
forward then fully rearward. Compare servo
pressure with line pressure at the accumulator
port. Servo pressure should not vary from line
pressure by more than 21 kPa (3 psi).

### Turn the test gauge selector to line pressure

position.
Place the gearshift lever in 2 range and operate
the engine at 1000 rpm.
Test Three
This test checks pump output, pressure regulation and the front clutch/rear servo condition by
measuring and comparing operating pressure
at the rear servo pressure port in Reverse.

### NOTE: For this test, only the high pressure

gauge is used. The gauge hose is connected
directly to the rear servo. It is not necessary to
move the gauge selector to any specific
position.
Operate the engine at curb idle speed.
Move the gearshift lever to Reverse and note
the gauge reading. Pressure should be approximately 1 103 kPa (160 psi) at idle.

### Slowly increase engine speed to 1600 rpm and

note the high pressure gauge reading again.
Pressure should increase to approximately 1
862 kPa (270 psi) as engine speed is increased.
Operate the engine at idle speed. Move the
gearshift lever from Reverse to Drive and note
the high pressure gauge reading. Pressure
should drop to 0 psi when the lever is moved to

### Drive. This test checks for leakage into the rear

servo which can cause rear band burnout.
Test Four
This test checks governor operation. It measures governor pressure response to changes

O

in engine speed. It is necessary to check governor operation only when speeds are incorrect
or the transmission will not downshift.

### Turn the test gauge selector to governor pres-

sure position.
Move the gearshift lever to D range. Operate
the engine at idle speed and note pressure. The
pressure should be 10 kPa (0 to 1-1/2 psi) maximum. If pressure exceeds this figure, the governor valve or weights are sticking open.

### Slowly increase engine speed and observe both

the speedometer and test gauge. Governor
pressure should increase in proportion to vehicle speed (approximately 1 psi per 1 mph). The
pressure rise should be smooth and drop back
to 10 kPa (0 to 1-1/2 psi) when the throttle is
closed.

### Test Five

This test checks lubrication pressure. The test
is especially important when the transmission is
noisy, when unexplained rear clutch failure has
occurred, or when fluid is forced out the fill tube
and the fluid level was known to be correct.

### Install the T-fitting in the transmission cooler

line.
Connect the white test gauge hose to the Tfitting and turn the test gauge selector to lubrication pressure position.
Start and operate the engine at idle speed.
Move the gearshift lever to D range and note
pressure.

### Lubrication pressure at idle speed should be 35

to 103 kPa (5 to 15 psi).
Increase engine speed to 1000 rpm and slowly
move the valve body throttle lever fully forward
then fully rearward. With the lever forward,
pressure should be 35 to 103 kPa (5 to 15 psi).

### With the lever rearward, pressure should be 68

to 207 kPa (10 to 30 psi).

AIR PRESSURE TEST
Air pressure testing checks clutch, band and
servo operation before and after repair. The
test involves substituting air pressure for fluid
pressure to operate the clutches and bands.

### The valve body must be removed for this test.

NOTE: Use dry, filtered compressed air only to
perform air pressure tests. Pressures of 207 to
689 kPa (30 to 100 psi) are required to perform
the tests.
4
3
84082
Rear Clutch Test
Place one or two fingers on the clutch housing
and apply air pressure to the rear clutch apply
passage (2). Movement of the piston may be
felt and a soft thud may be heard as the clutch
applies. Check for excessive air leakage while
pressure is applied.

### Front Servo Test

Apply air pressure to the front seivo apply passage (3). The servo rod should extend and apply the front band. Check for excessive air leakage while pressure is applied. Spring tension
should release the servo when air pressure is
removed.

### Front Clutch Test

Place one or two fingers on the front clutch
retainer and apply air pressure to the front
clutch apply passage (1). Movement of the piston can be felt and a soft thud may be heard as
the clutch applies. Check for excessive air leakage while pressure is applied.

Rear Servo Test
Apply air pressure to the rear servo apply passage (4). The servo rod should extend and apply the rear band. While air pressure is applied,
check for excessive air leakage. Spring tension
should release the servo when air pressure is
removed.

Governor operational problems are diagnosed

STALL TEST
Stall testing checks the holding ability of the
converter stator-clutch and the transmission
clutches. Stall testing determines maximum engine rpm obtainable at full throttle with the
wheels locked and the transmission in Drive.

### Refer to the Stall Speed Specifications Chart

and diagnosis guides when testing is
completed.
WARNING: Never allow anyone to stand in front
of the vehicle when performing a stall test.
Block the front wheels and have the parking
and service brakes fully applied during the test.

### Stall Test Procedure

Connect a tachometer to the engine.
Check and adjust transmission fluid level.
Start and operate the engine until the transmission fluid reaches operating temperature.
Block the front wheels.
Fully apply the parking brakes.

### Fully apply the service brakes.

Open the throttle completely and record maximum obtainable engine rpm. Engine rpm should
be between 1850-2150 rpm.
CAUTION: Release the accelerator immediately
if engine speed exceeds 2150 rpm. Engine
speed above this figure indicates transmission
clutch slippage is occurring. Do not hold the
throttle open any longer than five seconds at a
time. If more than one stall test is required, operate the engine at 1000 rpm with the transmission in Neutral for at least 20 seconds to cool
the transmission fluid, and release.

### Shift the transmission into Neutral and operate

the engine for 20 seconds to cool transmission
fluid.
Stop the engine, shift the transmission into
Park and release the brakes.
Refer to the stall test diagnosis.
Stall Test Diagnosis
Stall Speed Too High

### If engine speed is 2300 rpm or higher, transmis-

sion clutch slippage is indicated.
F-17
AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Stall Speed Too L o w
If maximum obtainable engine speed was 1650
rpm or less, the torque converter stator-clutch
is not holding. The condition should be confirmed by road testing. A slipping stator clutch
will cause poor low speed acceleration. However, highway performance may not be affected.

### Stall Speed Normal

If stall speed is normal, road test the vehicle to
confirm converter performance. If road testing
reveals that low speed acceleration is normal,
but an abnormally high throttle opening is required to maintain highway speeds, the converter clutch is seized.

### Noise

Fluid flow through the converter during a stall
test may generate a whining noise. This is normal. However, loud metallic noises indicate internal damage. Operate the vehicle on a hoist,
at light throttle in Drive and Neutral, to verify
that this type of noise is actually from the
converter.

### CONVERTER HOUSING FLUID LEAK

DIAGNOSIS
Two facts must be established when diagnosing converter housing leaks. First, it must be
verified that a leak condition actually exists, and
secondly, the real source of the leak must be
determined. Suspected converter housing fluid
leaks may not be leaks at all. They may be the
result of fluid spilled during transmission top-off
or refill.

### Converter housing area leaks may have several

sources. The leak source should be identified
before attempting repair. The paths followed by
various types of fluid leaks are described
below.
84083
Leak Paths
• Oil Pump Seal (1) — leaks past the seal lip
tend to move along the drive hub and onto
the rear of the converter housing (2). However, if total seal failure occurs, fluid will be
deposited inside the converter housing only,
near the outside diameter of the housing.
• Oil Pump Body —
leaks past the pump
body follow the same path as an oil pump
seal leak or fluid may travel down the pump
face into the converter housing.
• Oil Pump-to-Case Bolt (3) — leaks past any
one of these bolts are deposited on the inside of the converter housing only and not on
the converter itself.

### F-18

AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING
• Oil Pump-to-Case Gasket (4) — leaks past
the gasket are deposited inside the converter
housing only.
# Front Band Lever Pin Plug — leaks past the
plug threads are deposited inside the hous
ing and not on the converter
# pump bushing or converter hub scored, nicked, pitted or burred

threads are stripped

### Correct these conditions as follow:

Leak Diagnosis Procedure
Check fluid level and condition. Adjust fluid level if necessary.
Raise and support the vehicle.
Inspect the transmission. Correct any external
leaks from the oil pan gasket, filler tube, governor line, cooler lines and fittings, pressure test
port plugs and case-to-adapter housing gasket.

### Remove the converter housing inspection plate.

Wipe all fluid from the converter housing area.
Operate the engine at 2000 rpm for 2 minutes
and check for leaks.
If a fluid leak pattern is not evident, proceed to
the next step.
If a circular type of leak pattern develops, it
indicates a damaged torque converter.

### If a trickle type of leak develops, it indicates an

oil pump leak caused by one or more of the
following conditions:
• pump drainback hole obstructed
• pump housing vent obstructed
Remove the transmission and converter.
Tighten the front band adjusting screw until the
band fully applied. This keeps the front clutch
assembly in place when the oil pump is removed and aslo avoids damaging the clutch
discs.

### Remove the oil pump and oil seal.

Inspect the pump housing drainback and vent
holes for obstructions. Replace the pump if the
drainback hole cannot be opened with thin wire.
Blow solvent through the vent. Replace the
pump housing if the vent cannot be opened.

### Inspect condition of the pump housing and con-

verter hub. Replace the housing if the bushing
is scored. Polish the converter hub with crocus
cloth to avoid damaging a replacement seal.
Install the replacement pump oil seal, O-ring,
gasket and oil pump

### Loosen the kickdown lever pin plug two turns.

Apply a small quantity of No. 2 Permatex, or
equivalent, to the plug threads. Tighten the plug
to 17 N*m (150 in-lbs) torque
Adjust the front band.
Install the transmission and converter.

In-Vehicle Procedures
A — Fluid Level and Condition: Fluid should
be at the full mark with the engine idling. Fluid
should not be milky, full of bubbles or dark and
burnt smelling. Use JEEP automatic transmission fluid or an equivalent Dexron® II fluid only.

### B — Throttle Linkage: Check for smooth trav-

el. Clean but do not lubricate the linkage pivot
points. Adjust as necessary.
C — Gearshift Linkage: Adjust if necessary.
D
—
Engine Idle Adjustment: Set to
specifications.

AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION

### DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

E — Hydraulic Pressures: Perform the hydraulic pressure test to determine if operating pressures are within specifications. Repair hydraulic
components as necessary. Check and correct
throttle and line pressure settings if required.

### F — Front Band: Adjust to specifications.

G — Rear Band: Adjust to specifications.
H — Neutral Start Switch: Check the wires and
connections. Test the switch. Valve body manual lever must ground the switch in P and N. If
not OK, check ground strip at the valve body
manual lever. If OK, check the starting circuit.

### I — Park Lock: Check condition of the lock rod

ball, sprag, reaction plug, governor support and
sprag shaft. Replace parts as required.
J — Transmission Oil Cooler: Check cooler
and lines for obstructions or leaks. Look for
milky colored transmission fluid which indicates
coolant in the fluid.

### K — Output Shaft Bearing, Bushing or Seal:

Remove the extension housing, inspect the
parts and replace as necessary.
L — Governor Valve: Clean and inspect the
valve components. Check the weights, shaft
and valve for burrs, nicks, scores or binding.

### Check the spring for collapsed or distorted coils

and the snap rings for distortion. Check the filter for dirt and debris. Inspect the body for
cracks or warpage. Check torque on the governor and output shaft support bolts.
M — Oil Filter: Inspect and replace if clogged.

### N — Valve Body: Remove, disassemble and

clean thoroughly. Inspect valves and plugs for
nicks, scratches, burrs and rounded edges on
valve lands. Check the bores for scratches, the
springs for collapsed coils, and all mating surfaces for nicks, burrs or warpage. Tighten the
valve body screws to exact specifications during assembly.
0
—

### Front Servo and Linkage: Inspect the

piston for wear, cracks, and worn or broken
seal rings. Check the springs for collapsed for
broken coils. Check the servo bore for
scratches, nicks or wear. Check the lever, strut
and band for damage. Check the lever shaft
and O-ring for wear.
P —

### Rear Servo and Linkage: Refer to the

front servo inspection/service procedures.
Q — Accumulator: Clean and inspect for broken seal rings, scratched bores or broken or
collapsed springs. Check the piston for cracks
or evidence of the piston cocking in the bore.

—

body and use air pressure to apply clutches and
bands to check operation.
S

Engine Tune and Performance: Verify
proper engine operation. Be sure the compression meets specifications and that the fuel and
ignition systems are functioning properly.

### T — Stall Test: Perform the stall test to check

holding ability of the converter and transmission clutches.

Out-of-Vehicle Procedures
a — Converter Drive Plate: Check the plate for
flatness, cracks, loose attaching bolts, or damaged ring gear teeth.
b — Oil Pump: Clean the pump and check all
clearances. Inspect the rotors for scoring and
the seal and bushings for wear. Inspect the
pump housing and reaction shaft support mating surfaces for flatness.
c — Transmission Vent: Make sure the vent is
open and not obstructed.
p-: •23

### AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING
d — Front Clutch: Clean and inspect all parts.
Examine the retainer and piston for scores and
scratches, the discs and plates for wear, the
return springs for collapsed coils, and the seal
rings for damage. The vent check ball in the
retainer must operate freely.
e — Rear Clutch: Refer to the front clutch
inspection/service procedures.
f _

### Planetary Gear Set: Clean and inspect the

annulus gear, planet pinion carrier assembly
and sun gear. Check for worn thrust washers,
damaged gear teeth, and excessive pinion end
clearance. Examine the bushings in the sun
gear for excessive wear.
g — Rear Band: Inspect the band for wear and
for a good bond of lining to band. Inspect the
lining for damage and wear. Replace the band if
worn or damaged.
h — Overrunning Clutch: Clean and inspect
the clutch parts for brinnelled clutch rollers or
cam, or for improperly assembled rollers or
springs. Check for collapsed springs and bent
spring retainer tabs.
i — Torque Converter: If the converter hub
seal surface or drive slots are damaged, or if
the converter contains foreign material, burntoxidized fluid or debris, replace the converter.

### Do not attempt to clean or flush the converter.

j — Seal Rings: Inspect the reaction shaft and
governor support seal rings for wear, cracks or
breakage. Inspect the ring grooves for nicks,
burrs or distortion. Inspect the bores in the
front clutch retainer and the output shaft support for nicks, grooves, wear, cracks or
scratches.

GENERAL SERVICE INFORMATION
The Model 999, three speed, automatic transmission is used in Wrangler/YJ models.
This section covers removal, installation, lubrication and in-vehicle service and adjustment
procedures for the Model 999 automatic
transmission.

### The procedures, specifications and special

tools needed to overhaul the Model 999 transmission are contained in the T.A. 700/900 Component Service Manual.
GEARSHIFT LINKAGE ADJUSTMENT
Raise the vehicle.
Loosen the shift rod trunnion jamnuts.

### Remove the shift rod trunnion-to-bellcrank lock

pin and disengage the trunnion and rod at the
bellcrank.
Place the gearshift lever in Park.
Move the valve body manual lever rearward into
Park detent. Be sure the lever is moved rearward as far as possible. Park detent is the last
rearward detent.

### Check for positive engagement of the park lock

by attempting to rotate the propeller shaft. The
shaft will not rotate if the park lock pawl is fully
engaged.
Adjust the shift rod trunnion to obtain a free pin
fit in the bellcrank arm and tighten the trunnion
jamnuts. Prevent the shift rod from turning
while tightening the jamnuts.

### NOTE: Gearshift linkage lash must be eliminat-

ed to obtain proper adjustment. Pull downward
on the shift rod and press upward on the outer
bellcrank to eliminate lash.
Move the gearshift lever to Park and Neutral
and check starter operation. The engine should
start only in these positions. If the engine does
not start in P or N (or starts in R, D, 2, or 1),
adjustment is incorrect or the neutral switch is
defective.

### Lower the vehicle.

THROTTLE LINKAGE ADJUSTMENT
Disconnect the throttle control rod spring.
Use the throttle control rod spring (1) to hold
the adjusting link (2) forward and against the
nylon washer (3).

VALVE BODY SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
Transmission removal is not necessary in order
to service the valve body. The valve body can
be removed ind serviced independently.

### Valve body removal, pressure adjustment and

installation procedures are outlined in this section. Refer to the T.A 700-900 Component Service Manual for valve body
overhaul
procedures.
Valve Body Removal
Raise the vehicle.
Remove the oil pan and drain the fluid. Inspect
fluid condition while draining.

### Loosen the throttle and manual valve control

lever clamp bolts. Slide the levers up and off the
valve body shafts.
Remove the neutral safety switch.
Remove the valve body attaching screws (1).
Remove the valve body as follows: Lower the
valve body about one or two inches. Then pull it
forward to disengage the park lock rod and remove the valve body from the transmission.

### NOTE: If the park lock rod is difficult to remove,

turn the transmission output shaft back and
forth (with the propeller shaft) until the red
clears the lock sprag.
Remove the accumulator spring from the valve
body.
Remove and discard the oil filter.
Valve Body Installation

### Clean the valve body and transmission mating

surfaces. Remove any burrs from the case and
valve body steel plate surfaces before
installation.
Position the accumulator spring on the valve
body.
p.; •29
AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT

### Insert the park lock rod through the opening in

the rear of the case.
Position the knob on the end of the park lock
rod against the reaction plug in the sprag. Then
exert rearward pressure on the rod to move the
rod past the sprag. Rotate the output shaft if
necessary.

### Align and position the valve body on the case.

Install the valve body attaching screws (1) finger-tight only. Do not final-tighten the screws at
this time.
Install the neutral switch.
Place the valve body manual valve in Neutral
position.
Move the valve body as necessary to align the
neutral finger on the manual lever with the neutral switch plunger.

### Tighten the valve body attaching screws (1) al-

ternately and evenly to 11 Nnn (100 in-lbs)
torque.
Install the oil filter. Tighten the filter screws to 4
N*m (35 in-lbs) torque.
Install the manual and throttle valve control
levers on the valve body shafts. Tighten the
lever clamp bolts and verify free movement of
the shafts. The shafts must not bind at any
point.

### NOTE: Do not use any sealer on the pan

gasket.
Lower the vehicle.
Fill the transmission with JEEP auto matic
transmission fluid or an equivalent Dexron® II
fluid.
Adjust the gearshift and throttle linkage.
Valve Body Pressure Adjustments
Transmission line and throttle pressure can
both be adjusted at the valve body. The two
adjustments are interdependent in that each affects shift quality and timing. As a result, the
adjustments must be performed accurately and
in the correct sequence, which is: line pressure
adjustment first - throttle pressure adjustment
last.

### Line Pressure Adjustment

NOTE: Use a steel machinists ruler for the following measurement to ensure accuracy.
Measure the distance from the valve body to
the inner edge of the adjusting screw (1). Distance measured (2) should be 33.4 mm (1-5/16
in).

### Install the oil pan and replacement gasket.

Tighten the pan bolts to 17 N-m (150 in-lbs)
torque.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT

84163
If adjustment is required, turn the adjusting
screw (1) in or out to obtain a 33.4 mm (1-5/16
in) setting.

### NOTE: The 33.4 mm (1-5/16 in) dimension is an

approximate setting. Manufacturing tolerances
may make it necessary to vary from this setting.
One complete turn of the adjusting screw
changes line pressure approximately 9 kPa (12/3 psi). Turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise to increase pressure or clockwise to decrease pressure.

### Valve Body Throttle Pressure Adjustment

Insert gauge J 24031 between the throttle lever
cam (A) and kickdown valve (B).
84101A
Push the gauge inward to compress the
kickdown valve against the spring and bottom
the kickdown valve in the valve body. Maintain
pressure on the spring and valve.

### Turn the throttle lever stop screw (C) until the

screw head touches the throttle lever tang and
the throttle lever cam touches the gauge.
NOTE: Be sure to maintain pressure against the
kickdown valve spring and valve during adjustment. If pressure is relaxed, adjustment will be
incorrect.

### FRONT — REAR SERVO OVERHAUL

The front and rear servos can both be serviced
without removing the transmission. The servos
are accessible after the oil pan and valve body
have been removed. Servo removal, overhaul
and installation procedures are outlined in the

### T.A. 700-900 Component Service Manual.

GOVERNOR VALVE AND PARK GEAR SERVICE
The transfer case and transmission adapter
must be removed for access to the governor
valve and park gear. Park gear and governor
valve removal, disassembly, cleaning and installation are outlined in this section.

### Governor Valve and Park Gear Removal

Raise the vehicle.
Mark the propeller shaft yokes for assembly
alignment reference.
Disconnect the front and rear propeller shafts
at the transfer case.
Disconnect the speedometer cable at the transfer case.

### Position a support stand under the transmis-

sion converter housing.
Remove the rear crossmember.
Support the transfer case with a transmission
jack.
Remove the bolts attaching the transfer case to
the transmission adapter housing and remove
the transfer case.

### Remove the bolts attaching the adapter housing

to the transmission and remove the adapter
housing.
Rotate the transmission output shaft (A) until
the governor valve faces downward.
Remove an E-clip (B) from one end of the governor valve shaft.
Slide the governor valve shaft out of the governor body (C) and output shaft (A).

### Remove the snap ring (D) that holds the gover-

nor body and park gear (E) on the output shaft
(A).
Remove the bolts (G) that attach the governor
body and park gear to the output shaft rear
support (F).
NOTE: On some models, the bolts (G) may be
secured with lock straps. If so, bend the strap
tabs away from the bolt heads before loosening
the bolts. Then remove the tabs along with the
bolts.

### Remove the governor body (D) from the output

shaft (A) and park gear (E).
Remove the park gear (E) from the output shaft
(A).
F-32
AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION
IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
Governor Waive Disassembly and Cleaning
Remove the large snap ring (9) from the weight
end of the governor body (4).
? f 7 6
84103

### Remove the weight assembly (5-6-7).

Remove the small cap ring (8) that retains the
spring (6) and inner weight (7) in the outer
weight (5). Remove the spring and filter screen
(11).
Thoroughly clean each of the governor parts in
solvent. Use compressed air only to dry the
parts.

### NOTE: Do not use shop towels to dry the gov-

ernor parts. Small quantities of lint from the
towels could cause the valve and weights to
stick after installation.
Governor Valve Inspection and Assembly
Trial-fit the valve (2), valve shaft (3) and weights
in the governor body. The valve and weights
should slide freely when clean and dry. Small
burrs or scratches in the body, or on the valve,
shaft or weights may be polished-out with crocus cloth.

### Inspect the weight spring (6), E-clips (1) and

(10) and snap rings (8) and (9). Replace any
component if distorted, collapsed or broken.
Clean the governor filter (11) in solvent and dry
it with compressed air. Replace the filter if
damaged.
Check torque of the bolts that attach the output
shaft rear support (F) to the transmission case
(the governor body and park gear are attached
to the support). If the bolts are loose, cross
leakage and loss of governor pressure can
occur.

### Inspect the park gear (E). Replace the matic

transmission fluid.
Install the spring (6) and inner weight (7) t with
snap ring (8).
Install the assembled spring and weights in the
governor body. Secure the assembly in the
body with snap ring (9).

### Install the filter screen (9).

Governor Valve and Park Gear Installation
Install the park gear on the output shaft.
Install the governor body (D) on the output shaft
(A) and against the park gear (E).
Align the shaft bore in the governor body with
the shaft bore in the output shaft.

Install the bolts (G) that attach the governor
body and park gear to the rear support. Fingertighten the bolts only.
Install E-clip (10) on the governor valve shaft
(3).

### Slide the governor valve shaft (3) through the

weights (7-8), body (4) and output shaft (A).
Tighten the bolts (G) that attach the governor
body and park gear to the rear support to 11
N#m (100 in-lbs) torque.
Install the governor valve (2) on the shaft (3).

### Secure the valve to the shaft with E-clip (1). Be

sure the valve moves freely on the shaft and in
the body.
Install the transmission adapter housing. Tighten the housing bolts to 32 N ^m (24 ft-lbs)
torque.
Install the transfer case and rear crossmember.

### Connect the speedometer cable.

Connect the propeller shafts. Align the assembly reference marks and tighten the U-joint
clamp bolts to 19 fskn (14 ft-lbs) torque.
Adjust the gearshift and throttle linkage.
Lower the vehicle.
Fill the transmission with JEEP automatic transmission fluid or an equivalent Dexron® II fluid.

### PARK LOCK COMPONENT SERVICE

Park Lock Component Removal
Remove the transfer case and transmission
adapter housing.
Slide the sprag shaft (1) out of the adapter
housing and remove the sprag (2) and spring
(3).
Remove the snap ring (4) and slide the sprag
plug (5) out of the adapter housing. Remove the
plug pin also if so equipped.

### Inspect the lock ball on the park lock rod (6).

Replace the rod if the ball is worn or damaged.
Refer to the valve body removal/installation
procedures in this section if the rod must be
replaced.
84104
Clean and inspect the park lock components
and the park gear. Replace any component that
is worn or damaged.

Park Lock Component Installation
Install the sprag plug (5) and snap ring (4) in the
housing. Also install the plug pin if so equipped.

### Position the sprag (2) and spring (3) in the

housing and install the shaft (1).
NOTE: Be sure the square lug on the sprag
faces the park gear and the spring is positioned
so it moves the sprag away from the gear.
Install the transmission adapter housing and
transfer case.

### NEUTRAL SAFETY SWITCH

The switch (1) is actuated by the valve body
manual lever (2). The switch has three terminals. The center terminal is the starting circuit. It
provides a ground for the starter solenoid circuit through the gearshift lever in Park and Neutral. The outer terminals of the switch are for
the backup lamp circuit. Switch removal, testing
and installation procedures are as follows:
1
84105

### Starting Circuit Test

Remove the wiring connector from the switch
(1).
Check continuity between the center switch terminal and the transmission case in all gearshift
lever positions. Continuity should exist only in
Park and Neutral.

### If continuity exists in any position other than

Park or Neutral, check and adjust the gearshift
linkage and repeat the continuity check. Replace the switch if continuity still exists in any
position other than Park or Neutral.
Backup Lamp Circuit Test

### Remove the wiring connector from the switch

(1).
Check continuity between the switch outer terminals. Continuity between the two terminals
should exist only in Reverse. Replace the
switch if continuity is indicated in any gear other
than Reverse.

### Check continuity between each terminal and the

transmission case in Reverse. Replace the
switch if continuity is indicated.
Neutral Safety Switch Replacement
Raise the vehicle.
Disconnect the switch harness.
Position a drain pan under the switch and remove the switch from the c center of the case
opening if necessary.
35

### AUTOMATIC TRANSMISSION

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE AND ADJUSTMENT
Install the replacement switch and seal in the
case. Tighten the switch to 35 N*m (24 ft-lbs)
torque.
Verify that switch continuity exists only in Park
and Neutral.
Top off the transmission fluid level.

### OIL COOLER AND COOLER LINE FLUSHING

Main Oil Cooler
The main transmission oil cooler is located in
the radiator lower tank. The cooler and cooler
lines must be flushed whenever a transmission
malfunction generates sludge and metal or friction material particles.

### Auxiliary Oil Cooler

The auxiliary oil cooler augments the transmission cooler in the radiator lower tank. The auxiliary cooler helps prevent fluid overheating during heavy-duty operation. The auxiliary cooler
and lines must also be flushed whever a malfunction generates sludge and metal or friction
material particles.

### Oil Cooler and Line Flushing Procedure

Remove the auxiliary oil cooler and lines.
Disconnect and remove the main cooler lines.
Dislodge any foreign material in the inlet side of
the main cooler with a small screwdriver.
Reverse flush the main and auxiliary coolers
and lines with a combination of mineral spirits
and short bursts of compressed air. Continue
forcing solvent through the coolers until all oil
and foreign material are removed.

### Remove any remaining mineral spirits from the

coolers and lines by flushing them with clean
transmission fluid.
Check fluid flow through the main cooler as
follow:
• Connect the cooler inlet line to the main (radiator) cooler.
• Connect the cooler outlet line to the main
cooler but not to the transmission.
• Place the transmission end of the cooler outlet line in a one quart container.
• Overfill the transmission by one quart.
• Shift the transmission into Neutral.
• Run the engine at curb idle speed for exactly
20 seconds and observe oil flow into the
container. If less than one quart flows into
the container in 20 seconds, replace the radiator or recondition the cooler.

### Connect the main cooler outlet line to the

transmission.
Install and connect the auxiliary cooler and
lines.
Check and adjust transmission fluid level.
